i. china 's state - owned enterprise [ soe ] reform is at a key time and in a critical stage by the mid-1990s the business climate had undergone a qualitative change .
the greatest impact on enterprises was : - - market forces were replacing planning .
- - the opening to the outside world of the chinese market was evolving further .
as to enterprises , the most direct impact was that the critical moment for the excellence through competition of a market economy had really arrived .
it was a time of many challenges , as well as a host of opportunities .
market share and profits were concentrated in these enterprises , with their name - recognition growing quickly .
meanwhile , long - standing deeper soe conflicts were also being fully exposed .
they were mainly : - - a system conflict caused by the lack of separation between government administration and business management .
- - the conflict of lagging business institution innovation and operating forces unsuited to market competition .
in recent years , a sizable number of enterprises have been in a state of stopped or semi - stopped production , with up to 10 million soe employees being laid off or seeing their wages stopped or reduced .
the exposure of such conflicts lowered the overall operating efficiency of our state - owned economy .
while state - owned industrial enterprises now account for roughly two - thirds of our industrial capital and 70 percent of banking loans to industry , they create only one - half of our gross industrial output value .
soe inefficiency has affected china 's potential for sustained economic growth .
at present , market restraints are growing markedly stronger .
but a polarized soe order is evolving quickly .
this has left the desired state that should have appeared of large - scale enterprise reorganization , structural adjustment , and institution innovation unfulfilled .
means of intensifying soe reform grounded in years of reform practice , the fourth plenary session of the 15 th central committee issued a " resolution " on soe reform and development in september 1999 , to better clarify the means of intensifying soe reform . 1 .
- - we need to shift our stress on running each soe well to a strategic adjustment of our state - owned economic order , concentrating on fields in which the state must control and provide public service , to bring into better play the irreplaceable role of the state - owned economy .
we need to make a strategic adjustment of our state - owned economic order since competitive lines have already converted to a buyer 's market , it is neither possible or essential at this time for state finance to support a state - owned economy with so many lines and of such large size .
as an economy of diverse ownership forms develops quickly , it is both possible and essential for our state - owned economic order to undergo a strategic adjustment .
so we need to change the state in which the state - owned economic front is too long and has endemic control of all fields of our national economy , so that our state - owned economy can enter some fields and withdraw from others , doing some things but not others .
set up a corporate asset system , in which enterprises independently operate corporate assets and are liable for their own profits and losses . 3 .
form a scientific corporate management structure .
we need to act in line with the " company law " to set up an enterprise leadership and organization system , to evolve enterprise incentive and restraint forces .
we need to make a strategic reorganization of soes stressing the large and deregulating the small china now has around 230,000 soes which are duplicate and decentralized in their industrial distribution , with the large not having evolved an economy of scale , while the small lack market vitality .
between large enterprises and medium and small businesses , we need to evolve an enterprise group structure of specialized production and socialized coordination , to raise overall operating efficiency . 6 .
we need to downsize for efficiency , increasing equity and lowering debt due to historic reasons , soes are generally subject to surplus personnel , heavy debt , and heavy social burdens .
certain areas have also taken steps to take over from government enterprise - run social service agencies such as hospitals and schools , with 3,000 such agencies likely to be transferred a year nationally .
to improve the enterprise equity - debt makeup , we first need to stop inefficient or low - efficiency enterprise investment , conscientiously ending low - level duplicate construction , while supporting many means for enterprises to attract new investors and increase their equity .
qualified ones can attract foreign investment for grafting and cooperating .
the state has assigned boards of supervisors to wholly state - owned enterprises , to oversee enterprise finances and operating achievements . 9 .
for reform to succeed , we need to not only design good reform plans , but also reform our related innovation climate , dealing properly with all related interest relations , to overcome resistance .
in light of china 's two decades of reform practice , as well as the international expertise that we can draw on , i believe that reform will succeed through our sustained and steady practice and exploration .
beijing , 28 march - - it is understood that the financial regulatory authorities in china will implement a system of using real names for savings accounts starting next month .
dai xianglong , governor of the people 's bank of china [ pboc ] , revealed this january that the plan for a real - name savings system has been drawn up , and is expected to be introduced this year .
that is , before the implementation of the real - name savings system , money deposited under pseudonyms can be withdrawn under pseudonyms . however , starting from the day of the implementation of the real - name savings system , real names must be used .
dai xianglong noted : when implementing the real - name savings system , it is not difficult to request savings account holders to use their real names . however , we need time and a lot of investments to form a national network .
he indicated : after the implementation of the real - name savings system , banks will keep account holders information strictly confidential .
in specific terms , the main benefits of implementing the real - name savings system compared with the system of registering names for deposits , are as follows : first , the real - name system helps protect depositors interests .
second , the system helps improve depositors credit .
the reason is that banks and other financial organs no longer have to worry too much about debtors defaulting on due debt payments , and thus do not have to resort to all kinds of terms to guarantee the recovery of principal and interest for loans .
fourth , the system helps improve the tax collection system .
moreover , it is imperative to collect inheritance tax as the market economy develops .
under the real - name system , personal funds can be deposited in many financial organs . however , there is only one real name and one set of identification card numbers for one person .
it is therefore easier to make inquiries and statistical compilations on a person . this will impose an objective restriction on people who attempt to receive bribes and ill - gotten wealth . in other words , it makes it difficult to hide ill - gotten wealth .

nanjing , 29 mar ( xinhua ) - - china will have a law to abide by while patrolling its borders and administering the social order of vessels along its coasts .
the " provisions governing border patrol and administering social order of vessels along the coasts [ hereafter termed ' the provisions ' ] , " published by the ministry of public security on 15 february , will be formally enforced on 1 may 2000 .
at present , new situations and new problems concerning the administration of marine social order continue to pop up . problems where offshore fishing vessels operated beyond their designated marine areas or territories recurred repeatedly . criminal activities including illegal emigration , smuggling , drug - trafficking , piracies , and marine thefts rose gradually over the years .
in the past , our rules and regulations governing border patrol lagged behind ; in particular we did not have unified national provisions governing vessels along the coasts .
" the provisions " have 42 articles in six chapters . they are china 's first departmental regulations for facilitating a standardized and regulated administration over border patrol and social order of vessels along the coasts .
the meeting urged : while implementing " the provisions , " various local frontier guard departments under the ministry of public security must persistently enforce them according to law . they must strictly abide by law - enforcement procedures . they are strictly forbidden to levy fines which are beyond their authority , or which are too excessive .
they should intensify the examination and supervision over law - enforcement in some key links , including how law enforcement personnel handle cases and their administration over certificates and vessels .
they should abide by the requirement that police affairs must be open , and self - consciously accept the masses ' supervision by publicizing various operational systems and work procedures .

beijing , 29 march ( xinhua ) - - the party central committee and state council made a major policy decision of actively restructuring agriculture and devoting major efforts to developing agriculture that gives higher economic returns , on the basis that our country 's agriculture has entered a new stage of relative surplus in agricultural products .
many localities gained successful experiences in that aspect after they made efforts to explore . however , some other localities reported a series of problems . to sum up , peasants have fears [ san pa 0005 1830 ] .
first , peasants fear cadres who issue confusing orders [ xia zhi hui 4219 2172 2264 ] .
despite the fear of incurring debts instead of increasing incomes , peasants have to plant and fine strains that have been blindly introduced by cadres who have not analyzed the market thoroughly before forcefully popularizing the strains .
second , peasants fear that they will purchase bogus or inferior seeds and seedlings , or backward and outdated agricultural technologies .
the peasants fears highlight and reflect existing problems in agricultural restructuring . they show that restructuring is a formidable job . we should actively push restructuring forward , but should pay more attention to finding ways to solve present problems , and strive to ensure that the restructuring work proceeds healthily and steadily .
how do we carry out agricultural restructuring ?
agricultural restructuring is needed because of changes in the relations of market supply and demand . things produced according to old lines of thoughts are no longer marketable .
if one fails to study markets in a serious and thorough manner , one cannot accurately tell the directions and trends of markets . as a result , one will be exposed to tremendous risks during restructuring .
agricultural restructuring is a major matter that requires us to study market demand , and at the same time understand clearly suitable strains for us to plant and breed .
in other words , we should solve the problem of combining ideals with realities .
if we make the most of our strengths while avoiding our weaknesses , we will truly find a meeting point for local characteristics and markets .
we will be placed in an invincible position in market competition if we work on this meeting point .
third , we should insist on respecting the peasants wishes . historical experience proved that we could whip up mass enthusiasm , and our work would proceed smoothly , if we fully respect the wishes of the masses .
respecting the masses wishes does not mean cadres at all levels will have nothing to do or accomplish .
by providing service , one has to sincerely and wholeheartedly think in terms of the masses , and earnestly solve all kinds of problems encountered by the peasants pre - , during , and post - production .
when cadres at all levels solidly accomplish their jobs , they will provide powerful support for peasants to develop agriculture that is oriented toward quality and economic returns , and peasants will be able to discover new ideas for achieving prosperity in agricultural restructuring .

the standard for giving annual relief grain for each mu of grain plot that is returned to forests and grasslands are 300 jin for areas on the upper reaches of chang jiang , and 200 jin for areas on the upper and middle reaches of huang he .
the sources of relief grain for areas where grain pots are returned to forests and grasslands will be arranged locally or in the neighborhood in an overall manner by the provincial people 's governments .
in principle , the supply will be mainly based on the circulating commodity grain of state - owned grain purchasing and marketing enterprises in the locality . when necessary , the provincial authorities may use local reserve grain or apply for central reserve grain .
grains that are not examined or not up to standard are not allowed to be supplied to peasants in these areas .
these procedures state : the grain departments at all levels should be responsible for the organizational work of grain supply and state - owned grain enterprises will be entrusted to undertake the issuance of grain and the cashing business .
the grain transportation expenses would be undertaken by the local finance .
enterprises undertaking the grain supply task should issue grain to peasants in areas where the grain plots are returned to forests and grasslands according to forestry departments ' proof of the progress of returning grain plots to forests and grasslands and the quality examination and acceptance and in line with the state stipulated standard for giving subsidy .
townships and towns without purchasing networks may set up temporary supply networks and should basically attain the goal that each and every township and town undertaking the relief grain supply task will set up one supply network to make things convenient for peasants to receive grain .

china has made tremendous achievements in greening its land and last year , afforestation and greening maintained a positive momentum of development .
but we must also be soberly aware that the situation concerning china 's ecological environment remains rather grim and water losses and soil erosion are serious .
the deterioration of the ecological environment is severely jeopardizing and hampering the sustainable development of our national economy and society . improving the ecological environment has become an urgent requirement of economic and social development and the effort to improve the people 's standard of living .
it is necessary to have a heightened sense of urgency and responsibility , rise to action immediately , extensively mobilize millions of members of the public to involve themselves in the greening of their motherland , and speed up the process of creating a new , beautiful landscape .
wen jiabao stressed that making a success of this year 's land - greening work with a conscientious effort is of great significance to comprehensively expediting the construction of a new ecological environment in china in the new century .
the main tasks of afforestation at present are manifold . first , the all - people voluntary tree - planting campaign should be continued .
an active effort should be made to explore new mechanisms of bringing into play the forces from various quarters and enabling them to participate in afforestation in various ways .
second , the urban and rural greening process should be comprehensively accelerated .
it is necessary to adhere to the principle of letting urban areas lead rural areas , letting rural areas spur urban areas on , joining urban and rural forces , and moving forward in synergy .
third , conditions should be created for the improvement of conditions for agricultural production and the ecological environment and for the realization of sustainable agricultural development .
fourth , this process should be integrated with the strategy of developing the western country in a big way .
western regions should face the reality of a fragile ecological environment and focus their greening endeavors on the protection of the ecological environment and restoration of forest and grass cover .
all departments concerned should give energetic support to relevant industries in the greening campaign .
eastern regions should strengthen their cooperation with central and western regions , by developing forests and pastures in various forms , including acquiring shareholding through investment , joint exploitation , and cooperation for mutual benefit , so as to promote the joint development of the greening cause .
second , it is necessary to rely on scientific and technological advancement to raise the standard of land greening .
third , it is necessary to perfect the mechanisms and arouse the general public 's enthusiasm in afforestation .
mental mobilization and material incentives should be combined to benefit the public taking part in afforestation in real terms ; investors in different regions , industries , and under different forms of ownership should be encouraged to engage themselves in afforestation .
fourth , it is necessary to manage forests in strict accordance with law and comprehensively strengthen the protection of forest and pasture resources and the fruits of afforestation .
new progress should be made in legislation on land greening and new measures introduced to intensify law enforcement .
fifth , it is necessary to unify people 's understanding and conscientiously strengthen leadership over greening work .
the responsibility system based on greening targets should be upheld ; the tasks for afforestation , greening , and resource protection should be further clarified ; and substantial help should be extended to grassroots organizations in solving any practical problems they may encounter in their greening work .

a certain engineer regiment under the command of the general staff headquarters organized a research camouflage training under high - tech conditions in a certain place in northern china in late autumn .
reconnaissance teams from the " blue army " conducted reconnaissance on the targets of the " red army " from the air using high - tech reconnaissance devices of various types and did not found any real targets under camouflage .
the regiment was equipped with camouflage - painted motor vehicles , false target making vehicles , and camouflage reconnaissance vehicles one after another in recent years , and the regiment 's reconnaissance capability was thus enhanced to a certain degree .
to make the camouflage of important targets change along with different seasons , landforms , and reconnaissance means , they developed a computer auxiliary decision - making system , which can make both camouflage planning designs for targets under different conditions and provide plans for various auxiliary decisions on camouflage under complex wartime conditions .
to make static targets moveable , the task force engaged in tackling major technical hurdles worked without a letup for several months , made do with whatever was available , and thus succeeded in developing movable false tanks , false armored cars , and other false targets .
in the training sites , tanks and armored cars marched toward the areas under assault one by one , with their exhaust pipes spurting puff after puff of black smoke and their caterpillar treads leaving track after track of ruts behind them , thus making the camouflage effect more distinctive .
the one - man camouflage smoke launcher and assembled false target that they developed and improved won a third - class prize for military scientific and technological progress .
the task force led by engineer jiang shiwen succeeded in developing , through repeated experiments , a variety of shaped defilades , such as shaped umbrellas and shaped groves .
[ yan hua ] in the government work report written by chinese prime minister zhu rongji , in addition to the guiding plan of " speeding growth " was the guiding plan of food production , but it was n't included originally .
canceling the guiding plan of food production , canceling price supports for some types of foods , and implementing strategic reform were major events for a billion farmers .
for this reason , this journalist interviewed chen xiwen , who is a research fellow at the state council development research center , and also is the leader of the department of agricultural economic research .
chen xiwen has long been involved in agricultural economic theory and policy research . he worked on drafting documents for the central government regarding problems of farming villages . he wrote more than 10 books about this subject . he also published more than 150 dissertations and research reports .
does this mean that brown 's worries were without basis ?
take cereal , for example .
in 1998 , yield was 330.2 kg per acre , compared to 1992 , when it was 289.5 kg per acre , which is a 14% increase .
these years the food harvests have been good . those circumstances and necessary measures are reasons for this .
undeniably , there are many agricultural problems . between 1992 and 1993 , when the economy overheated , agriculture was ignored in many places . this caused a big loss of agricultural resources . the money and labor of some places went into real estate .
once the country implemented macroscopic economic reform , this situation eventually changed .
how do you view this ? [ chen ] regarding requirements for our agricultural products , the problem of quantity has already lessened .
last year the state department announced that beginning in 2000 , our country is going to start decreasing the scope of price controls and supports , so the price of low - quality food will no longer be protected .
the second - worst quality variety is the corn in the northeast . there is an idiom that says , " grow on the fire , harvest on the ice . " it means , the time to harvest the corn is when it is frozen to death . the corn is not completely mature .
but if you roast it , the kernel becomes flat and dry . it is poor quality and expensive . it is not easy to research and cultivate a new variety that can adapt to the cold northeast climate .
this is the third food surplus in recent years . the years 1984 and 1990 had food surpluses .
however , this did n't successfully promote higher - quality varieties . [ yan hua ] what is the difference between the agricultural reform this time and before ? [ chen ] before , agricultural reform was limited .
ancient people knew that logging and slash and burn land clearing were not good . but people had to feed themselves , so they had to do this .
but now , farm products are fully supplied . we now have the ability to encourage environmental ecology . for example , planting grass , protecting lakes , planned reforestation of farmland , and taking poor agricultural land out of cultivation .

beijing , 31 march ( xinhua ) - - the following are the stipulations governing the real - name system for individual saving accounts : article 1 . in order to guarantee the facts of individual saving accounts and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of the depositors , thereby , the provisions are stipulated .
article 3 . the financial institutions mentioned in the provisions refer to institutions doing individual saving business in line with the law inside chinese territory . article 4 .
individuals opening new saving accounts in financial institutions will be asked to show their own identification cards and use their real names .
when opening an individual saving account on someone 's behalf in a financial institution , the representative should show both his own identification card and the identification card of the person he represents .
when the depositors open individual saving accounts in financial institutions , the financial institutions should ask them to show their own identification cards , make checks , and register their names and identification card numbers .
financial institutions and their personnel are responsible for the secrecy of individual saving accounts .
financial institutions are not allowed to provide information concerning individual saving accounts to any unit or individual , and they have the rights to reject any unit or individual that inquires about , or asks the financial institutions to freeze or transfer the money of the individuals , with an exception for those cases stipulated by law .
article 11 . the people 's bank of china will organize these provisions for implementation .
a person in charge of the people 's bank of china today answered this reporter 's questions regarding the " provisions on the system of individual deposit accounts under real names , " which will go into effect on 1 april .
the questions and answers are as follows : question : what does the system of individual deposit accounts under real names mean ?
what significance does the practice of this system in china have ?
the principal purpose of practicing the system of individual deposit accounts under real names is to guarantee the authenticity of the individual deposit accounts and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of the depositors .
the existing deposit system has been practiced in china for several decades , under which when a financial institution opens an account for a depositor , it does not require him to show his identity document , nor use his real name .
in addition , the practice of the system of individual deposit accounts under real names will also play a positive , promoting role in improving social credibility , reforming the instruments of cash settlement , and introducing the use of personal checks .
q : what foundation does china have for practicing the system of individual deposit accounts under real names ?
moreover , it is also stipulated that depositors can only report the loss of their certificates or passbooks with their names on them but cannot report the loss of those without their names .
other circumstances that are not included in the above provisions should be handled according to relevant laws , administrative laws and regulations , and relevant provisions of the state .
for subsequent deposits into or withdrawals from this account , he only has to produce his deposit certificate or passbook without having to show his identity document ( except for the special circumstances such as early withdrawal or report of loss ) .
q : after the real name system is put into practice , will the problem of failing to maintain secrecy of an individual 's deposit account arise ?
a : maintaining depositors ' secrecy is a basic principle of financial institutions in handling individual deposit business .
article 29 of the " prc law on commercial banks " stipulates that " commercial banks have the right to refuse any attempt of a unit or individual to inquire , freeze , retain or transfer an individual 's saving deposit , unless otherwise prescribed by the law . "
article 5 of the " regulations governing the management of deposits " stipulates that " when savings agents handle savings business , they must abide by the principle that deposits are made voluntarily , money is withdrawn freely , interest is paid on deposits , and accounts are kept secret . "
at present , china 's financial institutions have instituted a system to strictly maintain secrecy of individual deposits , under which the financial institutions have the right to refuse any act of inquiring , freezing , retaining , or transferring an individual 's deposits in the financial institutions without legal bases or without going through legal procedures .
therefore , depositors need not worry about the secrecy of their deposits .
q : what are the requirements on financial institutions in handling deposit business after the system of individual deposit accounts under real names is put into practice ?

in april last year , the state council formally approved the bo hai pollution prevention and treatment work and regarded it as the priority of the " 33221 ( three rivers , three lakes , two districts , one city , and one sea ) " environmental protection work nationwide .
as of the end of february , they had already provided a special environmental investigation report .
as related , bo hai is a nearly enclosed inland sea of china with 77,000 square meters in sea area and an average of 18 meters in depth .
the mouth of bo hai bay is narrow but the inside diameter is big . its self - purification capacity is weak because the duration of time for sea water swapping is long .
during the recent decade , the quality of the sea water has continued to worsen .
fishery resources in bo hai have been seriously damaged , and large and little yellow croakers are on the verge of extinction . the dominating age of all kinds of fish has generally declined and the average weight of the fish is low .

after the end of the cold war , the united states began to pursue a foreign relations policy of equal distance regarding relations between india and pakistan in order to maintain stability in the south asia region , and ensure us strategic interests in asia .
however , in 1998 , india and pakistan proceeded in succession to test nuclear weapons , causing this us policy to suffer complete failure , and forcing the united states to carry out a re - examination of its south asia policy .
from a us standpoint , due to past close relations between india and the former soviet union , relations between the united states and india were frostier . this not only did not accord with us interests in south asia , it also did not conform to america 's global strategy and interests .
us public opinion also stated that this visit was preparation for carrying out genuine strategic cooperation between the united states and india .
a second reason is the requirements of economic interests .
the united states believes that india possesses one - sixth of the world 's population and is a potentially huge market for the 21 st century .
before clinton left for his south asia visit , us secretary of state albright stated outright that india has an enormous middle class - a group of consumers with immense power who are difficult to ignore . developing trade and economic cooperation with india will bring the united states enormous economic benefits .
during the cold war , the united states considered pakistan a frontline country for restricting the former soviet union 's expansion in south asia , and once formed an - pakistan alliance .

it was found later that the failure was caused by a clogged pipe in the cooling system of the thermal - inductance infrared detector .
the postponement of the third test is likely to affect us decision on whether to deploy the tmd and the nmd this summer .

according to a 23 march " wall street journal " report , the united states has 11 air - defense missile units in the rok and the gulf region , each armed with 64 missiles , and the pac-2 " patriot " anti - missile missiles there had been replaced in the 10 preceding days .
the decision to replace them was made after a series of tests failed .
the united states has also reminded seven other countries and region that the " patriot " missiles there might have technical problems .
taiwan has deployed 180 pac-2 " patriot " anti - missile missiles in three sets which it bought from the united states for $ 1 billion .
recently , the us tmd has developed a succession of problems and its tests have been far from being successful . people are particularly paying attention to whether the technical problems of pac-2 missiles will affect us tmd and nmd deployment plans .
us tmd and nmd are designed to cope with missile threat from hostile countries .
the discovery of technical problems on pac-2 will accelerate the replacement and will not affect the tmd deployment .
israeli prime minister barak said on that day the deployment of the " arrow " missile defense system would greatly strengthen israel 's defense capability .
despite the tmd 's test failures , the united states will give up neither the tmd and the nmd . on the contrary , it will step up their development and deployment .
it is a system jointly developed by israel and the united states for the defense against tactical ballistic missiles .
israel develops such anti - ballistic - missile missiles for the middle east and europe theaters because of ever - increasing tactical ballistic missile threat from its surrounding regions . the united states has joined the development and borne most of the spending because of its own needs and its special relations with israel .
the 1991 gulf war raised israel 's awareness of the imperativeness of deploying the anti - ballistic missile system .
today , israeli government officials and their supporters in us congress are attempting to make the clinton administration support a project , unofficially known as " post-2000 arrow " program , requiring approximately $ 200 million in spending and eight years of development .
if the united states agrees to defray the $ 50 - 70 million spending , the israeli ministry of national defense will undertake most of the work for the project .
while deploying the " arrow ii , " israel has already been planning to improve it .
the emphasis is on the asia - pacific region the united states has built an adequate early - warning and defense system against long - range missiles and icbm 's with a range exceeding 3,000 km .
after the dprk made its first satellite launching ( the united states said it was a missile , not a satellite ) , japan and the rok believed there was an opportunity for them to take advantage of ; and so , they immediately decided to participate in the us tmd program in an allaround way .
the experience of us - israel joint development of the " arrow " missiles shows that the deployment of the tmd will lead to proliferation of missile technology .
this is worrying .
at present , japan 's weaponry is incredibly sophisticated .
in ballistic missile for instance , the united states has always believed that japan dares not develop such an offensive weapon because of its " peace constitution . "
it goes without saying that japan is completely capable of developing ballistic missiles of even better performances .
when m-5 rocket is developed into an icbm , its range can be 12,000 to 16,000 km .
the real threat is that japan will accelerate its development of tactical ballistic missiles with advanced technology provided by the united states .
in september 1991 , japan launched its tr - ia rocket for the first time .
according to military experts , the tr - ia rocket , with a range exceeding 750 km , can be converted into a mobile tactical ballistic missile which can be launched from a cross - country motor vehicle to attack the rok and the dprk .
this shows that japan is not behind the united states in missile capability , and it even surpasses the united states in some respects .
the united states has not only extended its missile defense program to japan and the rok , but also included china 's taiwan in it , trying to use taiwan as a card [ in its hands ] to contain china .
this will inevitably yield a serious impact on regional security and even on the international strategic setup .
us congress has adopted a resolution asking the defense department to include taiwan in the tmd and submit a feasibility appraisal report .
people believe that taiwan 's tactical ballistic missile defense capability will be enhanced after 2000 . it is because of the following reasons : first , taiwan is not only receiving information furnished by us early - warning satellites . it is also actively developing its own satellites .
the " tien kung iii " ground - to - air missiles being developed in taiwan will have a much greater anti - ballistic - missile capability than " tien kung ii . "
third , taiwan is likely to obtain from the united states pac-3 " patriot " missiles with greater anti - ballistic - missile capability and to seek to join the united states in the development of the thaad , so as to further enhance its anti - ballistic - missile capability .

at present , those international arms races being extensively conducted are typical examples of the latter .
in the middle east region , national and religious contradictions are acute and disputes about resources and territories are complex and complicated .
as all sides involved in these disputes have been constantly strengthening armaments to meet the needs of their own interests , this kind of arms race is surging , wave upon wave .
the middle east peace process that began in the 90 s has failed to cool the passion for this kind of race .
according to data from the london institute of strategic studies , in recent years the military spending in the middle east region is still increasing year by year , and the proportion of military expenditure to the gross domestic product [ gdp ] in this region is far higher than in other regions in the world .
the yearly military budget of israel accounts for over 10 percent of its gdp , excluding the large amount of military assistance provided by the united states .
and those arab countries are also not willing to be outdone but are purchasing large amounts of advanced weapons .
now israel has commissioned its missile defense system , which will undoubtedly further stimulate the race between " spear " and " shield . "
the united states is the initiator of this surging wave .
since the cold war , the united states has become the only superpower occupying the " highest peak " in the world in terms of military technology and weaponry .
it possesses the most advanced conventional and nuclear weapons in the world .
last year , it also decided to increase its military spending by 112 billion us dollars in six years ' time to be spent on updating equipment and deploying the ballistic missile defense system .
it plans to replace f-16s and f/a-18s with combined striking fighters and f-15 with more advanced f-22, deploy more b-2 supersonic invisible strategic bombers , and also renew tanks and naval vessels .
this sounds absolutely terrifying !

as us secretary of state albright has said , strength needs to be used or it becomes useless .
on the other hand , in order to break away from its dependence on the united states , the european countries have decided to establish " european combined troops " and prepared to build it into a strategic force " upon which even the united states has to look in a different light from before . "
lately , india has also decided to drastically increase its yearly military budget by 28 percent .
however , weaponry is made of purely consumable materials that cannot be taken for food or fun .
people now are vying with each other in manufacturing , stockpiling , and occupying the " commanding point " of high - grade , precision and advanced weaponry .

in the final analysis , how great will the impact of china 's entry into the world trade organization [ wto ] on china 's shipbuilding industry be ?
on the one hand , after china joins the wto , import tariffs will be cut by a wide margin and this will help domestic ship owners , shipyards , and designing units directly use advanced , reliable , and fairly - priced , and serviceable complete sets of foreign ship equipment and spare parts with low prices .
at the same time , foreign corollary equipment will enter the chinese market at low tariff rates and their prices will drop significantly from the previous ones .
japan had a mind to follow suit in this regard .
once the plans of the eu and japan materialize , china 's wto entry will increasingly fetter its shipbuilding industry .
thanks to the efforts exerted in the last 20 years of reform and opening up , the shipbuilding industry has become one of china 's heavy industries that has been able to compete with its counterparts in developed countries .
nevertheless , we must notice that china 's shipbuilding industry is facing a grim situation in which its competitiveness has been declining in the last few years .
price competitiveness has always been the major strong point with which china 's shipping - related products have managed to acquire a " deserved place " in the international shipping market . the strong point stems mainly from china 's relatively low labor cost .
however , our country 's shipbuilding cost rose rapidly in a period of time in the past .
more seriously , a new effective technological innovation system and mechanism have not yet taken place in china 's shipbuilding industry . therefore , the industry lacks the capability to make technological innovations , so its technology develops slowly .
what is gratifying is that in 1999 when the world ship prices were on the low side , china 's shipbuilding industry received orders of building 1,005 ships with a loading capacity of 7.68 million tonnes , a record high .
we believe that no difficulty can daunt them and no waves can prevent them from forging ahead and in the future pattern of shipbuilding powers fighting for industry supremacy , china 's shipbuilding industry will have its own " deserved place . "

in the early 1960 s , comrade chen yun put forward four measures to resolve food shortages : readjusting the rural policy , asking the industry to support agriculture , importing grain , and mobilizing urban population to emigrate to the countryside .
in 1961 , the urban population was reduced by 10 million , which resulted in the reduction of 2 billion kilograms of food supply to cities .
at a central conference in 1962 , comrade chen yun again proposed importing more grain and less cotton .
it turned out that he made a comparative study : importing 1 metric ton of cotton cost $ 700 while importing 1 metric ton of grain cost $ 70 .
the foreign exchange spent for importing 1 metric ton of cotton could import 10 metric tons of grain while the land used for growing 10 metric tons of grain could produce 5 metric tons of cotton .
through comparative study of domestic and foreign human resources , comrade chen yun also arrived at the conclusion that processing imported materials was beneficial to china and had a great future .
he said : all developed countries have traveled the course of processing imported materials .
practice has shown that this is a reasonable and very profitable approach .
even though the united states is a major cotton producing country , it does not export cotton cloth because their wage is $ 3.8 .
it does not pay to process cotton on its own . the british wage is $ 1.6 .
china 's cost of producing cotton is far lower than those countries . its price is very competitive . there is a promising future for export .
comrade chen yun 's proposal accorded completely with china 's conditions and met the urgent need of economic construction at that time .
the reason for making this proposal was based on his comparative study of the benefits of importing grain and chemical fertilizer plants .

nevertheless , a dragon is absolutely not an animal which had ever existed . rather , it is a creature which symbolizes the cultural spirit of the chinese nation .
for example , the lion , tiger , and hawk have remained symbols in the national emblems of some european countries .
on the contrary , the creator or symbol of the chinese national culture is but an imaginary and abstract animal .
the dragon is able to fly high in the sky ; swim freely in the water ; and walk on the ground .
since the day it was born , the dragon has symbolized such precious spirit as seeking unity between the sky , the ground , and mankind , namely , the spirit of seeking communication between mankind and nature .
it is thus clear that the image of the dragon was initially a symbol of the chinese national unity and cohesion .
we may also demonstrate this by virtue of traditions and local traits relating to the dragon , which have been handed down .
in such a collective performance , should the individuals involved fail to integrate their strength with that of the collective , they would definitely sustain a defeat .
the lion dance , which is also an artistic gem of the chinese nation , needs to be performed by at least two persons in excellent tacit agreement whereas the dragon dance needs to be performed by tens , scores , or even hundreds of people , depending on the length of the dragon , in tacit agreement .
not long ago , the young people from the hong kong special administrative region and the young people of the hinterland held an activity called dragon dance on the great wall in the badaling area of the great wall . more than 5,000 people formed a dancing dragon 3,048 meters long and set a new record .
it is , thus , clear that such traditional cultural programs as the lion dance or the dragon - boat race may best embody the spiritual connotation of the dragon culture , namely , " unity is strength . "
the dragon is the symbol of chinese national unity and cohesion and the dragon culture has brought to light the profound truth that " unity is strength . "
i wish the first chinese dragon culture and art festival a complete success !

since the start of the 1990 's , human society has speeded up the pace of the switch to the information age , and information technology has been extensively applied in the military field , bringing about a revolutionary change on the battlefield .
at the same time , the change from " mechanized warfare " to " informationized warfare " [ xin xi hua zhan zheng , 0207 1873 0553 2069 3630 ] speeded up .
this change already emerged in the gulf war in the early 1990 's , and the kosovo war at the end of the century could be described as a preview of informationized warfare .
the new - style " three - three " is precisely the result of being drawn forward by the requirements of informationized warfare .
the old - style " three - three " was centered on exhausting the enemy 's vital forces , preserving our vital forces , and striving for superiority in manpower , firepower , and machine power , and the focal point of contention was to gain superiority in " material capability . "
the new - style " three - three " is centered on obtaining , transmitting , handling , and protecting information , and the focal point of contention is to achieve information superiority .
first , stealth planes , cruise missiles , and armed helicopters are the core weapons in the enemy 's weapons system for carrying out " hard destruction " of our information system composed of command , communications , and early warning .
second , defending against precision attacks , against electronic jamming , and against reconnaisance and monitoring mean using " passive means " to seal off our information flow , prevent the enemy from obtaining information and from destroying or damaging our information centers , and ensure that we can smoothly obtain and transmit information .
third , the key to the new - style " three - three " is to obtain and seal target information , and change from being " transparent " to the enemy ourselves to making them " transparent " to us .
hence , the key to " striking them " lies in obtaining target information as early as possible .
proceeding from system in entirety - - planning new " three - three " studying and training in the new - style " three - three " encapsulates the main contents of the modern battlefield and is the point of entry into training the troops through science .
tackling this training well requires not only the enthusiasm and eagerness of officers and men of the entire army in unfolding it , but also , still more , coolness and rationality so that it can develop and deepen .
an outstanding characteristic of the informationized battlefield is combined operations and confrontations of systems .
several recent partial wars have shown that reconnaisance and monitoring , electronic jamming , stealth attack , hyperprecision attack and so on constitute an entirety premised on , conditioned by , and supporting each other .
corresponding to this , " three - three " is also a closely knit and inseparable entirety .
second , we must form a system in equipment establishment , fully exploit the strong points of all branches of the armed forces and all the different types of equipment , and act in concert to curb the enemy with our joint force .
the specific combat elements of the different branches of the armed forces should have a clear picture of their position in the entirety of combined operations and bring their functions into play .
distinguish the levels and the key points .
as far as the group land armies are concerned , " striking at three things " is the main task of the air defense units and the amphibious [ lu hang , 7120 5300 ] units , and is also one of the tasks of the artillery troops , armored troops , and antitank missile units .
the upper - level units cannot exceed their functions and meddle in others ' affairs , while the grassroots units cannot get divorced from reality and go in for grandiose projects .
allocate resources in rational fashion .
centering on getting the maximum out of manpower , finances , and science and technology resources , we should do a good job in system design and rationally distinguish the tasks , following the principle of avoiding duplication and waste .
with regard to key projects , such as reconnaisance and early warning and automated command in " striking at three things , " we should show bias toward the focal points and pursue the greatest rate of returns on resources .
persist in simultaneous development of strategy and technology - - achieve optimum military effects taking a general view of the gulf and kosovo wars , powerful enemies always use the " technology gap " to execute " asymmetrical warfare , " weaken the opponent 's strong points , and force him to submit .
the main way to enhance the technology content of armament to meet the demands of the new - style " three - three " is to apply high technology and develop new equipment .
we should be skilled in " borrowing strength to move forward , " and draw support from the strong points of local talent , technology , and equipment , to solve problems of our insufficient technical strength .
training troops through science and technology is innovative - style training .
the nature of military strategy also lies in innovation .
curbing the " strong points " of the enemy 's hi - tech equipment and making up for the " weak points " in our own weaponry requires us to find an asymmetrical and unconventional method .
the weak side also has its own asymmetrical combat methods , and this is strategy .
we should continually be concerned for these changes in study and training in the new - style " three - three . "
this is a misunderstanding .
computerized mathematical simulation represents a major change in the military domain .
judging from the current situation of our army , the actual realization of this major change lies in this : it is necessary to get rid of the traditional model of mechanized war and quickly follow a new path , with information - based war as key contents .
war simulation serves as a means to win a war . instead of repeating the wars of the past , we should get a new perspective regarding wars in the future .
before the gulf war , us military units formulated a " white snow " plan , which included a simulated " electronic bombing " against iraq . us military units also developed computer viruses that were used later in the war . all these simulations have been developed with the guidance of " forward looking " thinking .
the reason is this : the outdated content of a simulation wastes labor , money , and time . more importantly , it goes against the common sense that the content of a simulation must conform to the environment of future wars .
during the gulf war , the automatic command system and operational procedures used by iraqi military units had been simulated by computers . but iraq suffered a big defeat , which can be attributed to the fact that their simulation content and procedures were developed in accordance with the experiences gained during the war between iraq and iran .
however , compared with these specific technical problems , the more important things are the experimenting and establishment of mathematical models and operational parameters that are compatible with information - based wars .
in fact , the expression of silicon chips beating steel and iron can be translated by this idea : people try to turn their experiences and knowledge in this aspect into corresponding mathematical models and operational parameters , which are integrated with weaponry , thus having some kind of intelligence .
if both sides have roughly similar hardware technology , those who has more advanced mathematical models will obtain advantages in information - based struggles .
therefore , to win an information - based war , a country should have advanced information equipment . more importantly , it should establish more advanced mathematical models as well as comprehensively reliably databases for the information - based war .
if the artillery observation and the firepower control system are interfered with by the other side , the discovery probability is equal to zero . in this case , the product of the hit probability and the destructive probability surely is equal to zero .
with the extensive use of the hookup of computers as well as various firepower systems and the c4i system , computers have played a major role in battlefield struggles . in addition , a new war pattern has been produced - - the computer internet war .

strategic and operational initiative is the premise for successful landings chang wanquan [ 1603 8001 0356 ] , ( director of a teaching and research section ) : an important reason for high rate of success of landing operations in modern times is that invading side holds the strategic and operational initiative .
first , it holds the strategic initiative .
viewing the many landing operations since the start of world war ii , the invading side usually launches the operation after gaining the all - round strategic initiative .
as everyone knows , the allied landings in normandy in northern france in june 1944 , the largest such operation during world war ii , were launched when the strategic situation in the world antifascist struggle was extremely favorable .
prior to the normandy landings , the soviet army had started to counterattack after its decisive victory at stalingrad ; the italian army had collapsed ; and the japanese army was continually retreating in defeat in the pacific theater .
hence , the entire world war situation was favorable for the allies to open a second front in the west .
although the enemy knows that the attackers may land at a certain section and in a certain area , it has no way of predicting the day , the time , the orientation , or the strength of the landing , and what method to will be adopted in the landing .
the success of modern landing operations is decided by careful and detailed preparations in all respects .
before each landing operation , concentrated and unified command organs with specific command responsibilities and various other relevant organizations are established according to the makeup of the participating force and the actual operational requirements , harmonious command relationships are specified , and scientific and rational operational plans are drawn up .
the plans for the us forces ' landing on saipan in june and july 1944 had been under study for 14 months .
second , preparations in combat training .
since a landing operation involves many branches of the armed forces , the action is complex and coordination is difficult .
third , preparations in equipment and hardware .
apart from preparing sufficient ammunition , fuel , equipment , hardware , spare parts , provisions , and so on , it is also necessary to prepare a great amount of landing transportation means .
first , form overall superiority in strength .
second , form partial superiority .
hence , the invading side always forms still greater superior strength over its opponent in the partial area of the beachhead , to ensure the establishment of the beachhead .
second , the specific combat action is executed with surprise .
whether before or in the midst of the operation , the invading side holds the initiative regarding what combat action to adopt , which enemy targets to suddenly attack , and how and when to execute this .
in a landing operation , the invading side fights with its back to the sea , and the moment the operation starts , with troops blocking it in front and the sea at its back , it is like an arrow in the bow with no way of retreat .
the invaders must give all they have and exert every effort to concentrate maximum firepower for a violent surprise attack on the enemy , to seek to paralyze at one blow their opponent 's defensive system , while the landing force advances wave upon wave and forges ahead with fierce determination to complete its task with lightning action .
take the normandy landings as an example ; before the operation the allied air forces destroyed through surprise attacks 100 luftwaffe bases along 560 km of the normandy coast , reducing by 50 percent the number of aircraft of luftflotte 3 which was responsible for defense in the west .
second , they attached importance to seizing command of air and sea in the landing operation .

if agriculture and the rural areas are not modernized , the national economy as a whole will not be modernized .
although the agricultural growth rate is not high , it plays a decisive role in the national economic development . this is because agriculture is the foundation of our national economy and a great majority of china 's large population is agricultural population .
for instance , our gdp growth has slowed down in recent years , but the contributions of rural economy to our economic growth as a whole did not decrease and on the contrary they continued to increase in 1997 , 1998 and even 1999 .
the development of township and town enterprises in china 's rural areas has played a great , direct promoting role in the national economic growth .
at present , township and town enterprises account for a considerably large part , around 28 percent , of the national economy .
in the last several years , township and town enterprises contributed to approximately 3 to 4 percentage points in china 's gdp increase . in addition , township and town enterprises have created a large number of jobs for rural surplus labor force .
in 1996 township and town enterprises had the largest employment , with a total of more than 130 million workers . 3 .
with the gradual progress of reform , the control of peasants ' migration has in fact been relaxed constantly .
according to a most authoritative survey statistics , as of 31 october 1996 , more than 72 million rural people left their homes and held jobs in other townships , towns , counties and regions .
after all , there are more than 900 million people living in china 's countryside . because of so many people there , the countryside should be a huge potential market .
during the period 1984 - 1985 , the retail sales of consumer goods in the rural areas accounted for around 53 percent of the nation 's total . in recent years , the sales dropped somewhat .
major problems facing china 's agriculture and rural economy some chinese experts believe that since china attained the objective of raising the people 's living standards first to the level of sufficient food and clothing and then to a better - off level of moderate prosperity , its agriculture and rural economy has entered a new stage of development .
the current situation shows that the proportion of agriculture in the gdp is less than 18 percent . ; and while the 1999 agricultural growth rate was only 2.8 percent , a further drop in the proportion is anticipated .
to the peasants , it is very likely that output increase even means income decrease .
on the one hand , the popularization rate of durable consumer goods among the peasants is still very low ; while on the other hand , there is a 50 percent surplus in the productive capacity of major durable consumer goods .
for this reason , to develop agricultural product processing industry can guide consumption and open up new agricultural products market . 3 .
in the past , all localities had to be self - sufficient in many agricultural products due to their short supply . now , we have had the conditions for giving play to regional comparative advantage .
many people hold various views on china 's plan to implement the strategy of small cities and towns . in my view , all cities , regardless of their size , should be open to peasants , if possible .
under the present situation , perhaps the costs for peasants ' entry into small cities and towns are relatively lower and the impact caused by it on the government is relatively smaller . so , the road of small cities and towns is likely to be easier to take .
the higher prices are due to the government policy of higher protective prices . in reality , however , the higher government protective prices have not been practiced in many localities . a recent survey of rural situation shows that the selling prices of grain are not high in rural areas .
however , a conspicuous problem is that most of chinese agricultural products have a fatal weakness - - comparatively poor quality - - because of the past emphasis on qualitative increase and evident neglect of quality .
the policy of self - sufficiency practiced in our country makes it very difficult to open the agricultural product market wide to the outside world and to make an optimal organization of regional production factors .
however , we should seriously consider the question of how much we are relying on market supply to obtain the most principal agricultural products .
for instance , according to chinese government 's 1996 white paper on the food grain issue , the degree of china 's self - sufficiency in food grain was 95 percent and the remaining 5 percent was imported from international market .
this is not a small quantity to the international market , accounting for about 12 - 13 percent of its total supply .
in fact , the import of 21.8 metric tons will not ruin china 's agriculture . china imported 20.8 million metric tons of grain in 1995 . even if china 's grain import in 2004 or 2005 is 990,000 metric tons more , the country can digest it .
besides , the import of 21.8 metric tons is smaller than what china has promised to buy - - 5 percent of its total demand .
viewing from this angle , the wto membership will not be a disaster to our agriculture .
some foreign experts ( xiao geng ) believe that if china imports some 20 million metric tons of grain after its accession to the wto , the grain prices in international market will promptly rise , but in fact it will be a short phenomenon .
if the international market can anticipate china 's import demand , the grain production and supply there will be very flexible , just as in our domestic market . a slight price increase will quickly stimulate a large increase in market supply .
on the impact of wto membership on china 's agricultural technological progress , chinese expert ( du ying ) believes that after joining the wto , our agricultural advantage will depend on agricultural technological progress .
generally speaking , industrialized intensive farming and agricultural industrialization can play a greater role than the technique popularization system built by the government .

after many years of practice in reform , the fourth plenary session of the 15 th party central committee held in september last year made a " decision " on the reform and development of state - owned enterprises [ soe ] , further clarifying the way of soe reform .
readjust the distribution of state - owned economy from a strategic perspective as a buyer 's market has taken shape for ordinary competitive industries , the state neither has the financial resources nor finds it necessary to support the state - owned economy that covers such a wide range of areas and is in such a large number .
following the rapid development of the economy of various ownership , it is possible and necessary to conduct strategic readjustment of the distribution of state - owned economy .
the role of state - owned economy lies not only in its own development but , more importantly , also in supporting the sound development of the entire national economy and the state security .
establish a standardized structure for company management by legal persons large and medium - sized soes should change their system according to the " company law " and make great efforts to turn themselves into limited companies with multiple shareholders or stock limited companies and develop the economy of mixed ownership .
enterprise leadership system and organizational system should be established in line with the " company law , " so that mechanisms of incentives and restraint can take shape in enterprises .
in view of the imperfect social security system , the state has adopted measures to develop the labor force market by establishing reemployment centers and encourage workers to seek jobs by themselves or develop their own businesses .
some localities have also adopted measures to allow the government to take over hospitals , schools , and other social service institutions run by enterprises . about 3,000 such institutions may be transferred throughout the country a year .
some enterprises may sell their stocks to their workers who buy the stocks voluntarily , and others may transfer the state - owned stocks to other investors . those with better conditions may raise funds through domestic or overseas stock markets to lower their liability rate on assets .
implement mergers and bankruptcy to make enterprises without competitive edges retreat from the market the state should refrain from indiscriminately " save " debt - ridden enterprises .
the state has formulated policies to address the problems concerning the basic living expenses of the workers who lose their jobs due to the bankruptcy or closure of enterprises .
a board of supervisors should be established by the state at solely state - funded enterprises to supervise the enterprises ' financial situation and the performance of their managers .
accelerate supporting reforms major ones are : establishing and improving old - age , medical , and unemployment insurance systems more rapidly .

in the international community , no country or force has the right to interfere in the taiwan issue , which is an internal affair of china ; similarly , on the island of taiwan , nobody , no force , and no party have any right to change the fact that taiwan is part of the chinese territory .
how can a regional leader who has no right whatsoever to represent all the chinese people be eligible and have the power to split a region from a country and proclaim it an " independent state ? "
by practicing " one country , two systems " on the basis of the one - china principle , it is perfectly possible for the mainland and taiwan to arrive at a scenario where the well water does not intrude into the river water .
on the other hand , if one follows the example of lee teng - hui , who was always up to some tricks outside the principle of one china , one would end up in a blind alley , never to find a way out .
the dirty business of trying to split our motherland by staking the interests of the public in the taiwan region is base and resisting the one - china principle by banking on a political fantasy that will never come true is also pathetic .
it is fair to say that there is indeed a certain foreign force that covets taiwan and has the vicious ambition to split china , using taiwan as an " unsinkable aircraft carrier " to pin down china .
but this policy never succeeded in the past and does not have any hope of success in the future , either .
what ought to be pointed out here is that the steps china is taking toward prosperity are unstoppable . china 's status in today 's broad political , economic , and military landscape in the world is irreplaceable by any other force .
currently , cross - strait relations are at a critical time . if the one - china principle is acknowledged , there will be boundless prospects and numerous opportunities for the development of the cross - strait relations ; otherwise , there will be no way out whatsoever and perils will prevail .
this has caused strong concern among our compatriots on both sides of the strait .
only in this way can the two sides of the straits establish a basis for mutual political trust and provide ample space for the peace and stability in cross - strait relations and , subsequently , improvement and development of cross - strait relations .
the article argues that cross - strait dialogue and negotiation are important indicators of the improvement of cross - strait relations .

shanghai , 10 apr ( xinhua ) - - the national enterprise reform and management conference was held in shanghai today .
it is an important strategic policy decision of the party central committee and the state council to lift most of the loss - making large and medium - sized soes from difficulties and establish an initial form of the modern enterprise system at large and medium - sized key soes .
state - owned and state - owned holding industrial enterprises made a profit of 96.7 billion yuan last year after offsetting their deficits .
li rongrong emphasized : the fourth plenary session of the 15 th party central committee held last year gave a comprehensive explanation on how to establish the modern enterprise system , thus laying a theoretical foundation for accelerating reform .
in the next step to establish the modern enterprise system , the following major points should be grasped well : first , it is necessary to reform large and medium - sized key soes in line with the standard company system and to promote diverse stock rights as much as possible after the standard company system is established .
except for a handful of enterprises which should be monopolized by the state , various measures should be adopted to vigorously develop stock limited companies and limited liability companies which have diverse investors .
enterprises conducting reform in line with the company system should establish a standardized and effective structure of legal person management structure and standardize its operation .
third , it is necessary to explore and establish the mechanisms for selecting , employing , encouraging , and regulating enterprise managers that meet the needs of the market economy .
at enterprises with good performance , experiment with the annual salary system , the holding of stock rights , and other incentive systems should be carried out , but such experiments should not be conducted nationwide .
the endeavor of intensifying enterprises ' internal reform constitutes an important part of the effort to establish the modern enterprise system and change enterprises ' operational mechanism and is also the foundation for enterprises to achieve long - term steady development .
li rongrong pointed out : strengthening management is the foundation for the success in all the work of enterprises .
we should effectively guard against the revival of the thinking to wait for , rely on , and ask state support and guide enterprises to focus their attention on their own capability and improve their skills .
enterprises with poor management are not entitled to the state 's policy support .
at present , the following work should be prioritized to counter the conspicuous weak links in soe management : 1 ) management of strategies and policy decisions should be strengthened .
enterprises should establish and improve the system to pursue the liabilities for policy mistakes and guard against the phenomenon in which no one is responsible for policy decisions or individuals make arbitrary decisions .
2 ) cost management should be strengthened .
3 ) financial and capital management should be strengthened .
4 ) quality control should be strengthened .

the information society is , in essence , the network society .
since the 1990 's , various countries have taken the building of computer network very seriously .
network has opened up a new living space for human being and , at the same time , brought the human competitive activities into a new domain .
network has become a new basic point for the development and prosperity of a country and nation and , at the same time , bred new crises in this country and nation .
globalization and " global village " do not mean a harmonious world when the industrial society is changing its type into an information society , people suddenly find out that the " atomic world " is changing into the " bit world . "
in the early 1980 's , someone said that since the microelectronic technology came into the world , space has been " depreciating , " time has been " appreciating , " and the globe has been diminishing and gradually growing into a " small village . "
as a global consciousness , it will have a powerful promoting effect on the sustainable development of the human society , and it is also an expression of human civilization and progress .
however , what merits our attention is that an erroneous concept came into people 's minds - - the arrival of a harmonious world .
since the world is a " global village " and " globalized , " people can share bliss and misfortune together ; and with the removal of distance and difference , everybody has a bright future .
who is the " chief " of the " global village " ?
they can only be those countries practicing hegemonism .
" to most countries , this globalization is a forced process . . . . . . but to the united states , it is a process intentionally promoted and maintained by its political and economic elite . "
the united states wants to control the world , and it has three cards for the building and maintenance of a " monopolar world . "
one is " human rights above sovereignty . "
this card is intended for the legalization of its intervention in other countries ' internal affairs .
another card is " globalization , " which is aimed at quietly pushing the liberal economic policies to the world in an attempt to gradually deprive a national state of its economic sovereignty .
the third card is its powerful military muscles , which are used for carrying out strategic deterrence and creating one kosovo - style " brilliant victory " after another .
in comparison , the second card is more likely to make people puzzled and taken in .
in the martyr xu xinghu 's battlefield diary was recorded such " shocking " information : " the west threatened to block yugoslavia from entering the internet . "
" the core product of the network economic era - - internet - - may likewise become the tool of hegemonism . "
from this our fellow countrymen should realize that the internet can certainly become the tool of hegemonism !
if china 's administrative , economic , educational , and scientific and technological information systems all depend on the internet , there will be inestimable hidden danger to the country 's security and interests .
it has been learned that the us rand corporation is speeding up devising the information war strategy , which is as famous as the nuclear war strategy , and the network war may become the center of this strategy .
the united states publicly declared that it will strive to hold the hegemony of the network war in the 21 st century .
apart from security control , the so - called hegemony also covers cultural control , political control , and economic control .
at the end of the 20 th century when the internet is continuously expanding in the world , if we do not rise up vigorously to take up the challenge , rejuvenate our national information industry , and build our own information network , then we may be reduced to the status of an information colony of the hegemonism .
we have the conditions to build our own information network our information war expert shen weiguang predicted that world war iii will be a comprehensive information war .
the expert believes that in the information war strategy , the hackers ' attack on a certain web site has merely the tactical significance ; it is only the network controlling power and network decisionmaking power that have the strategic significance .
according to general logical inference , any local network can develop into a regional network , national network , and even a global network so long as appropriate methods are applied .
