according to recent media reports , the tibet autonomous region government interfered in the sakadawa festival in lhasa this year .
a : the sakadawa festival is a traditional festival for tibetan people living in the lhasa area .
according to the legend of tibetan buddhism , 15 april of the tibetan calendar was the date when sakyamuni was born , achieved spiritual enlightenment , and passed away .
on this day , tibetan people of all ages and both sexes are dressed in their holiday best .
in the tibetan calendar , april is a buddhist month , which is called " sakadawa " in the tibetan language .
during this month , people should make a pilgrimage to buddhist temples and chant buddhist scripts . they should burn incense and kowtow .
religious festivals celebrated by monasteries include the shimo chento festival of tashilhunpo monastery , the nganjo festival of ganden monastery , the collecting sutras and religious dance festivals of samye monastery , the july vajra festival of sakya monastery , the erecting the prayer banner pole festival of tsurpu monastery , and the paltung tanbo festival of radreng monastery .
depending on different places , the scale and time of these festivals are different . some are religious festivals and some are traditional ethnic activities . participation is on a voluntary basis .
a : on 15 april of the tibetan calendar every year , tibetan people will circle around the potala palace , the jokhang temple , and other monasteries in lhasa . they will burn incense and pray by turning the prayer wheels . this is a normal annual activity of the masses , which is protected by law .
a strong festive air still prevailed in lhasa this year when the " sakadawa " festival was celebrated . the atmosphere of the festival was not different from previous years .

finally , i would like to say one more thing .
a recent example was when the minister of petroleum and mineral resources of saudi arabia announced on 3 july that saudi arabia and other countries would increase oil output by 500,000 barrels per day , the brent price fell by $ 1.50 per barrel the next day .
when the opec secretariat announced on 17 july that oil - producing countries would further increase oil output in the near future , the oil price in the international market further decreased .
it seems that opec has been controlling the world oil market .
how long will the situation last ?
can opec really monopolize the oil market again ?
in order to analyze whether opec has controlled the current world oil market or not , we must review the 40 years of opec history .
opec was established in 1960 . the founding countries included 13 oil - exporting countries , namely iran , iraq , kuwait , saudi arabia , venezuela , indonesia , equatorial guinea , gabon , nigeria , libya , algeria , united arab emirates and qatar .
opec 's most brilliant periods were the 1970 s and early 1980 s - - in other words , the often - mentioned periods of the first and second oil crises .
at the beginning of the 1970 s , demand for oil in the world increased by 100 million metric tons per annum ( 2 million barrels per day ) , and opec controlled 54 percent of crude oil output and 87 percent of the volume of trade in the world .
in october 1973 , the arab - israel war broke out . opec unilaterally raised the official oil price by 70 percent .
it caused immense losses to the world economy , especially the western economy that relied on the import of oil .
the war between iran and iraq started in 1980 , and it further increased the impression that oil production world slow down .
until 1985 , opec operated in a manner like an international cartel and decided target price and oil output of various member countries .
from 1985 to 1986 , opec endured the first serious crisis since its founding .
the high cost of petroleum for more than 10 years curbed demand . the crude oil price that was much higher than production and investment costs encouraged the development and production of petroleum resources in non - opec regions , including the north sea in europe , the gulf of mexico in america and the west coast in africa .
in early 1980 s , saudi arabia as the leader of opec always played the role as a swing producer . in other words , whenever oil price was affected by surplus supply in the market , the kingdom of saudi arabia would single - handedly reduce oil production to stabilize oil price .
having suffered enough losses , saudi arabia decided to give up the role as a swing producer and recover its share in the market .
a price war within opec lasted one year and oil price rapidly fell . in july 1987 , oil price fell to the lowest point ( $ 7 per barrel ) .
in 1998 , opec endured another serious crisis due to the asian financial crisis in 1997 .
prior to the financial crisis , the high speed of economic development in asia increased the demand for oil , and it was a motive force and supporting factor for the world oil market .
however , the most suitable description of opec is the " tea bag " effect mentioned by professor ( mbar ) , an opec expert of the british oxford university : it functions best when it is in hot water .
the rapid fall of oil price has brought great pressure to bear on many countries in the middle east where economic growth and social stability depend on oil income and also great financial pressure on non - opec oil - producing countries such as mexico , norway and russia .
therefore , led by saudi arabia , mexico and venezuela , opec and several non - opec oil - producing countries twice reached agreements in amsterdam and riyadh in 1998 on using the method of controlling oil output to reverse the trend of oil price .
until february 1999 when oil price fell under $ 10 , the " tea bag " started to play its role .
three main oil - producing countries reached the third agreement at a meeting in the netherlands on cutting down oil production .
the implementation of those agreements would reduce oil output by 4.3 million barrels per day .
oil - exporting countries all at once became united and observed discipline .
non - opec oil - exporting countries such as mexico , norway and oman also actively took part in the movement to reduce oil production .
the real unusual thing was that the rate of observing those agreements by oil - producing countries reached as high as 94 percent at one time and that the rate of observance has been high even when oil price has regained strength .
however , it is not a simple thing to control such a big world market , and the total output of opec also cannot be easily adjusted like a water faucet .
petroleum as a geopolitical commodity , its market has also been influenced by outside factors such as the 1973 oil embargo , the 1978 revolution in iran , the 1990 - 1991 gulf war , and the 1997 asian financial crisis .
the weather temperature also directly affects the market situation .
even if opec has great power , how can it control those unstable factors ?
at all opec meetings , they had to use secondary source data instead of official data as foundation for making decisions !
there is generally a time gap from several months to several years in the statistical data of demand of energy in the world . besides , statistics on the change of quantity of oil in storage in various regions of the world can hardly be quickly obtained .
even if correct , prompt and complete market information is available , it will still need the ability to react promptly .
this is another difficult thing for opec as a whole .
some member countries are rich , while some other member countries are poor . among the 11 member countries , there are differences in religion , culture and political system and different oil reserve and production capacity . the most crucial difference is the difference in surplus production capacity .
in discussion whether to increase production or not , countries without surplus production capacity would oppose the idea of increasing production while countries with surplus production capacity would be in favor of the idea .
now it seems quite difficult .
specifically speaking , it will obstruct oil refineries to have a normal storage because oil refineries always expect a lower price in the future and will not buy oil at a high price and keep oil in storage .
second , opec has not stipulated the correct scope of the " price zone " in any agreement .
the minister of petroleum of saudi arabia said he personally was inclined to set a scope of $ 20 to $ 25 per barrel , while some other countries hoped to stabilize the oil price at approximately $ 30 per barrel .
people should know that opec now only produces slightly over one - third of total oil in the world ( 36.5 percent ) and only account for 50 percent of the trade volume of oil . non - opec countries and international oil companies control other producers .
following the downfall of oil price in 1985 , many non - opec oil producing countries and international oil companies scored great achievements in technological renovation and greatly reduced the production costs of petroleum .
under such circumstance , artificial high prices will certainly encourage the production of oil by non - opec countries and of non - conventional oil .
sustained high prices will also lead to the slackening of discipline within opec , and most member countries will pick up the old habit of selling more oil at high price , and in the end disrupt the market and lead to a drop in oil prices .
anyway , although we are convinced that opec can hardly control the world oil market , we are not denying that opec is a force in the international market , and its strength should not be underestimated .
the middle east possesses two - thirds of known oil deposits in the world . with the passage of time , the dependence on oil in the middle east by china and the world will continue to increase .
the influence of opec will still be quite big in the following months and years .

party committees and political organs at all levels of the general armament department must attach great importance to the idea of the " three represents , " meticulously map out plans and make arrangements to comprehensively study , understand , and implement the " three represents " as an integral whole .
the crux is that we must take our own unit 's actual circumstances into consideration , focus our attention on the fundamental requirements of " victory in battle " and " no degeneration , " and further unify our thinking and action on major issues that have an important bearing on the general direction and the whole situation .
cao gangchuan pointed out : the central military commission 's decision to launch education by positive example for " three stresses " among grass - roots party organizations throughout the military is an important measure taken by the army to push forward the new , great project of party building in full swing .
now that this education drive has come to a stage of conclusion and enhancement , it is particularly necessary to guard against slackness and to prevent the tendency of overestimating the results of the education drive .
recently the central military commission [ cmc ] and headquarters decided to officially appoint military lawyers at political organizations of army groups ' corps , divisions , and brigades .
this is a major move to improve the army 's legal system and implement the policy of managing the army by the law .
military lawyers are also soldiers .
it also provides : as soldiers , military lawyers must observe military rules and perform the duties that soldiers should perform ; and as lawyers , they must receive their accreditation in accordance with the lawyer law and receive their operating licenses in accordance with state and military regulations .
in addition to observing a lawyer 's professional ethics and disciplinary rules , they must also obey the orders , decrees , regulations and rules of the armed forces .
military lawyers are professional law workers and political workers in the armed forces .
according to the lawyer law , lawyers are law workers in society . military lawyers naturally have the same attribute since their work is part of the legal profession .
however , according to the " regulations for political work in the chinese people 's liberation army , " political organs in the armed forces are in charge of the armed forces ' judiciary and legal services , which are an important part of their political work .
this being the case , military lawyers bear double responsibilities .
they must be knowledgeable with both state laws and military laws and regulations .
unlike civilian lawyers , military lawyers , as soldiers and political workers , must also have a mastery of military laws and other military regulations and rules .
first of all , military lawyers are officers in active duty and civilian staff in the military who are accredited . they are on the military payroll . the civilian counterparts are civilian citizens who are accredited to work as lawyers and their incomes come primarily from their professional services .
second , military lawyers , after they have been officially incorporated with the military establishment , become officers or civilian staff in the military with different official ranks . the work of civilian lawyers , however , is a civilian profession , not an official duty , and civilian lawyers have no official positions or ranks .
fourth , military lawyers ' operating expenditures are part of the military budgets , and their services are basically free of charge . civilian lawyers are financially independent . except for occasions when they have to provide legal assistance , their legal services are compensatory .
in view of military lawyers ' characteristics and actual duties , the main roles military lawyers have to play are : first , military lawyers are an important embodiment of the democratization of the judiciary system in the military .
a judiciary system without the participation of lawyers is not a democratic judicial system .
the official appointment of lawyers in the group armies is an improvement of the judicial system in the military . military lawyers should proceed with their work with a positive attitude to ensure legal assistance for all the accused suspects in the military in order to protect their legitimate interests .
second , military lawyers should provide legal advice to military leaders and organs at all levels so that their decisions are based on law and so that they can handle legal affairs according to the law .
third , military lawyers should work earnestly to protect the legitimate rights and interests of officers and men by helping them settle all forms of legal matters .
fourth , military lawyers should help officers and men heighten their law awareness and do their work more efficiently by providing them with legal consultations and educating them on law .
military lawyers should give full scope to their expertise . they should educate the armed forces to understand the legal system . while helping officers and men deal with law - related matters , they should help them understand the authority of the law and increase their trust on the law .

beijing , 24 july ( xinhua ) - - a relevant responsible person of people 's bank of china has answered questions raised by a reporter on the promulgation of " the measures for managing financial companies of enterprise groups . "
it can be said that supporting the development of the financial companies is tantamount to a certain extent to supporting the development of the state - owned enterprises .
people 's bank of china has all along given positive support to the financial companies in their development .
along with the economic development , the changed financial needs of the enterprise groups , and the continued deepening of our financial structural reform , the financial companies have also faced a series of new topics with regard to their own development needs or supervision .
in particular , owing to the accelerating pace of china 's accession to the wto [ world trade organization ] , our country 's financial companies have been under enormous competition pressure .
question : what are the key aspects of the latest revision ?
specifically speaking , " management measures " has revised the market access criteria for the financial companies to a large extent and has also laid down new or higher requirements for the enterprise groups which apply for setting up a financial company .
the new " management measures " has also laid down a series of new requirements for supervising or managing the financial companies . 1 .
for example , it has stipulated that a share - holder who fails to repay an overdue loan for a long time shall have to transfer its shares or its rights or interests in other aspects , and so on . 2 .
it has cultivated a concept of omnidirectional supervision and management and has added new contents like inspecting the financial companies through some intermediary institutions in the society ; ensuring self - discipline within various trades or professions ; and so on .
a relevant person of the people 's bank of china emphasized that the central bank has always given positive support for the development of financial companies because the support for developing financial companies means the support for developing state - owned enterprises to a certain extent .
therefore , in the aspect of liability operations , financial companies will be allowed in the future to issue medium - and long - term bonds with a view to gradually changing these companies liability structure and enabling them to do medium - and long - term financial operations .
however , a small number of financial companies are not perfect in terms of corporate management structure and have comparatively serious problems due to the influence from the bubble economy a few years ago .
major indicators are the relatively poor quality of assets and a certain degree of payment risks .
for this reason , in addition to defining the articles on supporting the sound development of financial companies , the new " procedures " have also added some articles on intensified supervision , management , and risk prevention .
specifically speaking , the new requirements china has set on the supervision and management of financial companies have first highlighted the responsibility of enterprise groups and their shareholders for preventing and eliminating the risks of financial companies .

the three articles published in this edition all concentrate their discussions on whether attention should be focused on firepower warfare or information warfare to " win a war . "
as a matter of fact , focus of attention in " winning a war " should also be the focal point of preparations for a military struggle .
this is a question of important practical significance . we hope it will stir up interest for our readers to all think it over .
all academic viewpoints expressed in such discussions may be different views by different people , but all are searching for and trying to get close to truth .
in the process of searching for truth , it is more important to open more new paths of understanding than speeding up along one single path .
we should persist in developing our information capability as the main approach reading comrade he tiemao 's article " shift the focal point of attention to firepower warfare , " we are pulled in by the article 's unique viewpoints .
to be clear about where attention in " winning a war " should be focused on , the first thing we must do is to be clear about where do firepower and information stand in the [ composition of ] fighting power .
firepower is a direct manifestation form of the fighting power .
it can be said that , to a certain degree , development of pure firepower is already utterly senseless . for firepower to become a new element of fighting power , it will have to find a way to combine itself with information .
some data indicate that , when the accuracy degree of a weapon is doubled , its combat efficiency will be equal to a 7 times increase in antipersonnel force .
further , if the former is increased twice as much , then the latter will be 27 times as much .
just as what modern enterprise aims at is benefit instead of efficiency , war is laying more stress on the degree of accuracy rather than destructive and killing force .
antagonism in the field of information and contention for information supremacy have become the center of combat in a regional high - tech war .
informationization has become the most essential , most distinctive characteristic of a regional high - tech war that distinguishes it from the past wars .
at present , the basic point of our army 's preparations for military struggle is to win in a regional war under the condition of modern , particularly high - tech , technologies .
as comrade he tiemao said , the pure military purpose of " winning a war " still is to " annihilate the enemy and keep ourselves alive . " this is the iron - clad law of all wars .
but , under the condition of modern high - tech war , the content of " annihilating the enemy and keeping ourselves alive " has undergone a qualitative change .
this point has been made clear to us by the gulf war and the kosovo war .
in the " desert storm " operation , out of consideration of the need of the mideast strategy , the us army did not subject the iraqi troops to complete destruction , did not send the saddam regime to its total collapse and the ground war came to a screeching halt after only 100 hours .
all this fully attests to the fact that the focal point in " winning " a modern war is on information , not firepower .
whoever has information supremacy will gain the initiative in a military contention and win victory in a war . based on this understanding , various countries have vied to readjust military strategy of their own accord to build up information combat troops of the future type .
to be sure , compared with foreign armies , our army is lagging behind not only in information but also in firepower . we are falling behind particularly in terms of penetration capability and antipersonnel force of our conventional arms .
therefore , while vigorously developing information technology , we need to also simultaneously step up research in firepower and to enhance the might of our combat troops equipped with modern weapons in order for them to give still better combat performance .
firepower warfare coexists with information warfare . it is not that information warfare will be in the service of firepower warfare . rather , it will become an independent type of combat . as for precision warfare , it is the combination of firepower warfare and information warfare .
war pattern and combat type are always closely connected with and correspondent to the times they are in , and will continue to develop along with the development of the times .
during this " transitional period " , the pattern of war actually possesses the characteristics of a combination of mechanized warfare with informationized warfare and the coexistence of firepower warfare and information warfare .
on july 4 th , the " forum " published an article written by comrade he tiemao , calling for focusing attention on firepower warfare to " win in a war . "
although the article contained many good points of view , because they were all dealing with one side of the matter without noting war characteristics of the times during the conversion and transitional period , it thus could not avoid being somewhat biased .
in the information era , while in weaponry we place emphasis on firepower , we place even more emphasis on information power certain type of combat is determined by certain technological conditions .
since world war two , the rapid development of new and high technologies with information technology as the core has made the status of information in future combat climb higher and higher and its role grow bigger and bigger . the development of weaponry has shown a trend toward informationization .
second , give prominence to information power in building the system .
third , lateral integration of technologies .
when war is turning from " fighting with metal " in the past to " fighting with silicon chip , " the contest in firepower will become contest in precision and reaction capability .
discovery is of primary importance when you want to destroy on sight .
information 's status and role in combat are growing daily , information warfare affects and restricts firepower warfare in combat , information not only directly affects the command 's combat decision , it is also developing from submitting to and servicing firepower to directly affecting and restricting the production of efficacy of various kinds of firepower .
information has become an important combat resource . it has become the power base of combat . like the attack force and mechanomotive force , information power has become a basic component element of the fighting power .
since hot weapon entered the war stage , the status and role of firepower warfare have been beyond challenge in war . it no doubt has become the most fundamental means to achieve the objective of combat .
however , as information technology develops and is widely applied in the military arena , it has become increasingly effective in controlling the energy release of attack weapons .
large numbers of long - distance , high hit - probability , precision - guided weapons such as guided missiles , guided shells , guided bombs and guided torpedoes are no longer firepower in the normal sense . they are firepower directly controlled by information .
precision warfare is no longer the same as firepower warfare in the traditional sense . it is one type of informationized war .
for the destruction of a target , it took 9,000 bombs in world war two , 300 bombs in vietnam war , and only 2 bombs in the gulf war .
when he talked about the firepower warfare , comrade he tiemao also included precision warfare in the discussion .
in fact , precision warfare is the combination of information warfare and firepower warfare .
therefore , firepower warfare and information warfare are supplementary to and closely linked with each other as neither can exist without the other .
it provides a " soft kill " combat approach to jam and suppress the enemy 's information as well as a " hard destruction " combat approach to destroy his electronic information system .
information warfare penetrates into various kinds of combat operations .
through the gunpowder smoke of several of the recent high - tech regional wars , people can more clearly see that information supremacy has become the " dominating point " on the battlefield , become a major factor for winning the war .
in sum , combat by integrating informationized warfare with firepower warfare will be the basic form of war for a period of time in the future .
from the gulf war to the kosovo war , war 's primary pattern in the early 21 st century period was clearly shown : " non - contact " firepower warfare is the leading factor that coexists with diversified forms of warfare .
the principal way to determine victory will shift from annihilation of the enemy 's personnel to destruction of his combat system ; the principal criterion of victory will shift from achieving the military goal to directly attaining the political objective ; the principal factor leading to victory will shift to the time controlled instead of the space controlled .
when the two sides of a war turn from the traditional contact - type firepower warfare to " non - contact " firepower warfare , they are still in a contest of war entities that are mainly represented by the strength of troops and by firepower .
during these two wars , the us military used its superiority in high - tech weaponry to win the so - called victory , realizing the so - called " zero casualty . " but for iraq and the fry , it was " real casualties " and " heavy casualties . "
this kind of firepower warfare will be different from the traditional .
information warfare 's sudden appearance on the horizon may have touched off the diversification of the form of war , but it will not cause firepower warfare to disappear .
for a considerable length of time to come , we will remain unable to pin our hope on the punching of the keyboard and the clicking of the mouse to win a war .
thus , we often move the future back to reality and replace individuality with universality .
guided by this kind of thinking , the only thing we can expect is a new theory of the type of an aerial castle .

according to an expert , it means that the china 's refined oil prices are speedily merging with the international markets .
china is a big oil - producing country , and is also a big oil consumer .
oil prices on the international markets remain high at present , and in the coming few months , the forward price of crude oil will remain over $ 25 a barrel .
that is why china has raised the prices of refined oil again and again . beginning 1 june this year , the factory prices of china 's gasoline and diesel oil have respectively increased by 300 yuan and 100 yuan a tonne .
it has been learned that the xinjiang area alone has increased its costs of cargo transports by more than 500 million yuan .
taking the opportunity of the price adjustments , a small number of enterprises in the petroleum oil business are reluctant to sell their goods or engaged in hoarding , and speculate profit earning .
on the other hand , affected by the price increase , china 's petrochemical industry rebounced its performance in general for 1999 , and its profit realized in the first half of this year continued to rise .
the expert pointed out that the economic returns brought by the price rise in refined oil is only temporary as the rising international oil prices will certainly come down .
china 's petroleum enterprises must seize the opportunity of the current high crude oil price to take the initiative in increasing input , accelerate technical transformation , quicken the pace of institutional innovation , set up a modern enterprise system , and repeatedly enhance their competitiveness .
therefore , the expert thinks that it is extremely urgent for china to set up a security system for petroleum .
affected by the increase in the international oil prices , china , as a developing country , has relied more on the international crude oil .
in 1999 , its demand for crude oil reached 191.5 million tonnes , but its output was only 159.35 million tonnes , showing a deficit of 32.15 million tonnes .
an expert from the institute of market economy of the state council development research center pointed out recently that in order to ensure china 's security in energy resources , it is necessary to set up the state 's strategic reserves for petroleum oil and enhance the ability to regulate the supply of crude oil in the country .

first , administration should be carried out on matters about which the grassroots level masses are most concerned , and the contents and methods should be constantly deepened .

of the 238,000 industrial polluting enterprises in china , the key enterprises that heavily polluted by over 65 percent number 17,925 , and 14,150 have fulfilled the anti - pollution requirements , accounting for 78.9 percent . of the 620 key state enterprises , 410 or 66 percent have fulfilled the requirements .
of the 210 key state enterprises that have not yet fulfilled the anti - pollution requirements , 11 are undergoing treatment and have entered a testing stage , 5 are to be shut down , 180 are involved in construction projects , and 14 have not yet taken action .
the official responsible for the state administration of environmental protection said that the main reason for the relatively low rate of key state enterprises fulfilling the anti - pollution requirements is the outstanding structural pollution in the state 's key enterprises , the difficulties in tackling pollution , depression in enterprise production , and a lack of capital .
the relative surplus production capacity is the most striking contradiction that exists in our economic structure .
then , the problem of economic overheating had regularly cropped up in china prior to the 1990 s . to aim high and go all out continuously under the background of supply shortages finally led to redundant construction projects .
ma jiantang particularly mentioned an industrial survey that china had completed five years ago , because it had revealed a major situation . the rate of utilization of approximately half of china 's production capacity of its industrial products was below 60 percent .
on the one hand , the general products produced far exceed demand . they cannot be sold . their price keeps on dropping . on the other hand , the production capacity of many products that are high - grade , refined , and advanced in nature is extremely low , " he said .
in addition to the relatively excessive production capacity , there also exists the problem of extreme decentralization . enterprises are scattered . they are small in scale and self - contained . their layout is irrational .
the result of decentralization is that enterprises are incapable of carrying out technical development . since they do not have enough capital , the inevitable result is that they are backward in technology .
dwelling on the main direction of attack and the main contents in economic restructuring , ma jiantang believed that speaking in general , we must remove two barriers . in brief , " let those that should die perish , and help those that can be rejuvenated expand and become stronger . "
" then , we need to eliminate and shut down those mines where natural resources are exhausted and those enterprises that are insolvent and suffering serious financial losses , " he added .
that involves settlement fees to be paid to workers and staff members , pensions for the retirees , expenses for the social undertakings that enterprises are running , and all kinds of arrears . ( 2 ) how can we handle the debts of the closed and bankrupt enterprises ?
it is said that banks may write off their loans to the enterprises , if enterprises are unable to pay them .
however , the banks cannot do so if the amount is huge .
where does the money come from for readjusting the economic structure ?
ma jiantang believed that first , it should be from the funds listed in the national budget . second , it is necessary to establish a mine - closing fund . third , it is essential to turn some of state - assets into cash and establish an insurance fund .
question : what is the background in issuing the " leasing company management rules ? "
in developed countries , the importance of leasing as means of financing is only next to bank credit in equipment investment .
question : could you brief me on the basic conditions and legal system building at china 's leasing companies ?
answer : since the establishment of the first leasing company in 1981 , china has had , by the end of 1999 , 15 leasing companies with aggregate assets of 18.2 billion yuan and an accumulated business volume of 190 billion yuan , which played a certain promoting role to the development of the national economy .
the people 's bank of china , after summing up experience and drawing a lesson from the development of leasing companies in china , collecting relevant operational documents on supervision , and making improvements and supplementation , devised the " leasing company management procedures " ( hereinafter referred to as rules ) .
answer : first of all , the " rules " settle the issue of the leasing companies ' functions and definition , give a clear definition to the leasing operation , standardize the rights and obligations of the parties concerned in leasing , and legally require that leasing firms adopt risk prevention measures .
third , a number of stringent requirements were set forth on managing debt ratio .
question : what are the special characteristics of the leasing companies ' liabilities and capital utilization ?
answer : taking into consideration of the leasing operation 's huge and long - term investment , we permit , in the area of debt management , leasing companies to issue financial bonds , to extend loans to financial institutions , and to engage in foreign exchange borrowing as a source and channel to secure long - term capital .
that way , leasing companies will genuinely acquire multiple functions of financing , investing , and promoting product sales and become non - banking institutions that mainly engage in financial leasing operations .
question : what roles will leasing companies play in the technological transformation of large state - owned enterprises and in the great strategy to develop china 's western region ?
answer : at present , china is adopting aggressive measures to support the technological transformation of state - owned enterprises and the great development of china 's western region . the problems of high debt ratio and backward technology and equipment are common among the state - owned enterprises and enterprises in the western region .
financial leasing - - a unique financial instrument - - can display its unique functions in supporting the state - owned enterprises ' technological transformation and the great development of western region .

this was a breakthrough to be made in the reform and development of state - owned enterprises .
relevant data show that china has approximately 14,000 large and medium - sized state - owned and state - holding enterprises and that the state - owned sector of the economy is the mainstay .
at the end of 1997 , 6,599 large and medium - sized loss - incurring state - owned enterprises set the objective of extricating themselves from difficulties in three years .
the main purpose was to enable most of the 6,599 large and medium - sized loss - incurring state - owned enterprises to make a profit instead of suffering a loss and to free themselves from difficulties in three years .
in other words , the three - year objective of extricating loss - incurring state - owned enterprises from difficulties does not require all , but most , of them to turn loss into gain or to make a profit in terms of such enterprises as a whole .
on the other hand , rigorous measures have been taken to effect the merger or collapse of enterprises , the change of debts into shares , and technical transformation , and stress has been laid on making full use of stock assets and on reducing the financial burden for enterprises , bringing vitality to enterprises .

the g-8 summit meeting was held from 21 - 23 july in okinawa , japan .

naha , the capital at the south of okinawa island , is okinawa prefecture 's political and cultural center . okinawa was the only place in japan where a land battle was fought during world war ii .
some 230,000 japanese and american soldiers died in the battle of okinawa , including tens of thousands of civilians . after the war , us forces set up military bases . japan and the united states signed the " japan - us security treaty " in 1952 .
during the talks then , japanese prime minister eisaku sato called for reducing and merging us military bases in heavily populated areas . the area of bases was only reduced about 15 percent following the return of okinawa to japan .
at present , 75 percent of the area of us bases are concentrated in okinawa , whose land area only accounts for 0.6 percent of japan 's territory .
us forces set up 39 military facilities on okinawa . the number of us troops on okinawa tops 27,000 at the most .
the united states had promised to return naha naval base to japan , but as there was no " replaceable " good military port , the us military has yet to move out of that port .
kadena air base is the largest air base with rapid reaction capability outside of the us proper .
the base 's aerial operation radius is 4,000 km , covering southeast asia , india , china , and russia 's entire far east region .
this unit is a unit that can make a " rapid reaction from hawaii to the cape of good hope . "

growing out of nothing the air defense unit of china 's armed forces is a combat arm of the services , which has gone through the test of protracted revolutionary war and grew to maturity out of nothing and from being small to large .
the first air defense unit in the history of the chinese armed forces in a real sense was born in october 1945 .
the liaodong military command accepted four pieces of 75 - mm antiaircraft guns from the japanese armed force in gongyuan , benxi at that time and thus formed china 's first antiaircraft artillery group .
the headquarters of the east china special unit decided to dispatch one antiaircraft artillery company to xibobo , pingshan in hebei province on 26 february in 1949 to shoulder the glorious mission to protect the party central committee .
the antiaircraft artillery troops shouldered the task of providing the first national congress of the chinese people 's political consultative conference with air defense in peiping in march the same year .
nevertheless , the two antiaircraft operations ended up with our army 's struggle against air raids winning victories .
the most famous anti - air raid battle was none other than the struggle against the " strangling battle " in the korean war .
most importantly , the enemy planes dared not to carry out low - altitude operations and consequently , their percentage of hits dropped from 50 - 70 percent at the beginning of the battle to below 5 percent .
after january 1952 , the enemy changed their tactics and launched the so - called " saturation bombing " on selected goods transportation railway lines .
for example , the enemy launched 47 sorties of b-29 bombers to attack the qingquan jiang bridge on the jingyi railway line ; they launched 1,600 sorties to bomb the manfu railway line .
a spokesman from the fifth wing of the us air force had to admit : " the days for us planes having free passage in korea are gone . "
compared with the korean battlefields , the us employed large quantities of modern weapons .
in addition to a large number of the latest type operational aircraft , including b-52 and f-105, the us also used the then most advanced television - guided bombs , laser - guided bombs , " bai niao she " antiradar missiles , pineapple bombs , bombs with steel balls , and air fuel explosive bombs .
these bombs , which had a high percentage of hits and were highly destructive , posed a grave threat to our personnel and weapons and equipment .

dai xianglong 's answer to this is : there is a solid basis for the stability of the rmb exchange rate , and the suggestion to expand the band within which the rmb fluctuates is worth studying . however , the people 's bank of china has not yet considered changing the current exchange - rate system .
actually , the reason that the market has been widely concerned with this question of late is mainly because china 's central bank has been " standing by and watching " as the rmb exceeded the old range of fluctuations on numerous occasions .
behind these concerns is the old question : once the rmb can float freely , will there be a major devaluation ?
however , without a doubt , the recent changes in the rmb market clearly show that china 's central bank is gradually reducing the extent and frequency of its intervention in the foreign exchange market .
in that case , will china increase the band for exchange rate fluctuations to the extent that the market is anticipating ?
once the market begins playing a greater role in determining the exchange rate , will the rmb face depreciation or appreciation and what will be the extent of the fluctuations ?
this is , without a doubt , the crucial factor that is influencing the decisions of monetary authorities .
therefore , the flexibility of the exchange rate is first and foremost based on the stability of the exchange rate .
this sets the stage for relevant administrative departments to appropriately loosen controls on fluctuations , while proceeding on a stable note .
due to the sensitivity of exchange rate indicators , china 's monetary authorities will be as careful as they can be in loosening controls .
this caution will entail not only detailed research on the above factors , but also paying careful attention to reactions from the market and from all quarters and carefully weighing losses and gains .
this will not only increase the government 's means of regulating the economy and increase the effectiveness of foreign exchange control , it will also be beneficial in changing the market 's expectations of a rmb devaluation and will strike a blow at domestic and foreign exchange rate speculation brought about by a relatively fixed exchange rate .

beijing , 26 jul ( xinhua ) - - the reporters have learned from the national fiscal work conference being held here that an important turn for the better appeared in china 's economy during the first half of the year , and the proactive fiscal policy practiced by the chinese government played a dominant role in the improvement .
chinese finance minister xiang huaicheng said that the good situation of economic development today would have been impossible , had we not implemented the proactive fiscal policy .
at the same time , the chinese government has accelerated the readjustment of economic structure and the promotion of scientific and technological progresses , linked short - term economic policy to long - term economic development objectives , and integrated the deflation prevention measures with the establishment of a marcoeconomic regulation and control system of market economy .
in the meantime , the government has increased spending on key projects .
in the first half of this year , the government 's social security spending increased by 195 percent and its spendings on public security , judiciary , science and technology , education , and agricultural science and technology also increased by a big margin , as compared with the first half of last year .
in the second half of the year , the chinese government will continue the proactive fiscal policy .

these " local wars " which are being fought more and more fiercely seriously affect the government 's image and reputation , constrain the development and maturing of a nationwide unified market , and hamper the optimized readjustment of china 's economic structure .
" local wars " gradually escalate , " market walls " are made ever thicker in the past the local protectionism in certain provinces was manifest in consumer goods such as beer , and the scope of protection was mainly in the area of counties and cities .
today , however , the local protectionism in certain provinces has expanded from the consumer goods field into almost all product fields and proceeded to spread into the investment field ; the scope of protection has expanded from county and city level to prefectural and city level and even to provincial level .
certain places have vigorously fought " local protection wars " over mainstay state industries .
a certain unit at jingmen in hubei province bought a " santana " car last october ; the sale price was only 172,000 yuan ; after completing the various procedures it had to pay 320,000 yuan , including 70,000 yuan as " funds for extricating from difficulty an enterprise in particular difficulty . "
what had happened was this : shanghai municipality at one time issued a regulation regarding private purchases of vehicles made elsewhere , laying down the scale of charges for a license plate for private purchases ; the base price for a shanghai - made vehicle was 20,000 yuan , and for a vehicle made elsewhere , 98,000 yuan .
the hubei side explained that charging 70,000 was not aimed at not allowing the sale of " santana " cars in hubei but at ensuring that its " fukang " cars could be sold in shanghai .
local embargoes on products are becoming more and more intense , and local protection in the investment field is also gradually becoming apparent .
there are two cableways for ascending to the great wall in a certain tourism area of beijing municipality ; one is operated with the participation of local investment , while the other was built by investors from elsewhere .
an extremely abnormal phenomenon has appeared in vehicles used for car hire in shanghai , wuhan , and changchun : in shanghai almost all are santanas ; in wuhan most of them are shenlongs or fukangs ; and in changchun most of them are jiedas from the no. 1 automobile plant .
for instance , shanghai prohibits the use of low - emission cars for hire , and local production enterprises and car hire companies have reached a " tacit understanding " that car hire companies must buy shanghai - made cars .
certain localities have eliminated xiali cars from hire cars under the pretext of technical indices .
changchun city for its part has publicly auctioned the operational procedure for car hire , but it is agreed that jieda cars must be used .

due to comprehensive factors such as the impact of the asian financial crisis , the excess of supply over demand has become quite serious in china 's markets in recent years , and deflationary signs have emerged .
in the face of this grim situation , certain localities have adopted measures to limit outside competition in order to ensure the continued existence of their local enterprises .
in fact , since early last year , some counties and cities in qingyang prefecture have been levying 12 yuan in " charges for permitting market entry " for every 50 kg of flour from elsewhere .
the reason given by the local government is that the local state - owned grain enterprises depend on loans for their operations and are already in extremely great difficulty ; they may collapse unless protected .

beijing , 27 july (zxs) - - china 's economy was on the decline for two years running . an " inflection point " [ guai dian ] , which people have been expecting for a long time , has eventually occurred at the turn of the century .
there is no doubt that china 's economic performance and the chinese government 's capability to handle the economy deserve special attention .
during the first half of this year , china 's economy increased by 8.2 percent . this was higher than what people generally expected .
aggregate demand of the society has gone up , and the " troika " of consumption , investments and exports has promoted economic growth . financial and monetary situation is steadily improving . after the downturn over the past two years , consumption price has been stable and has stopped further declining .
various signs have indicated that china 's economy has extricated itself from the situation of lacking a driving force for further growth over the past few years , that it has entered a new period of slight increase amid stability , and that the start of a new cycle can soon be expected .
recalling the past , one still remembers that china 's economy set a new historical record in 1993 , registering an increase of 14.6 percent . afterward , our economic growth has been declining gradually . the growth rate in the fourth quarter last year was 6.8 percent .
in 1998 , the central government decided to issue special construction treasury bonds and to implement a positive fiscal policy . our economy went up for a time . at that time , many people in economic circles believed that " a new turning - point has occurred . "
however , our treasury bond investments were weakened early last year , and our economic growth rate fell again .
in a series of his recent speeches , premier zhu rongji has pointed out that china 's economy has " taken a turn for the better " since this year , and that it has been " following a direction of virtuous circle . "
freight transport has increased by a big margin .
in addition , air freight , inland river transport and highway transport also considerably increased .
during the first half of the year , the selling rate of industrial goods was 96.8 percent , an increase of 1.15 percent over the same period last year . efficiency of state - owned enterprises has been markedly improved . their profits increased by 135 percent during the first half of this year .
the present smooth economic operations and high economic efficiency are initial and limited .
the foundation for recovery is not solid enough . our intrinsic power for promoting economic growth is still insufficient . the contradiction of insufficient demand has not yet been completely solved . some deep - level contradictions constraining consumption and investments have still existed .
li rongrong , executive vice minister of the state economic and trade commission , said : when the market plays a decisive role in deploying resources , this means a turning - point has truly occurred .
however , this has not yet been the case with our banking , finance and enterprises now .
it is true that the efficiency of the investments of our government bonds is low . however , without such investments , our economy might not be able to recover .
" of two options , utilize the better one . " it is a wise move to continue to implement a positive fiscal policy .
on the whole , the asia - pacific region is continuously moving toward peace and development , and gaining a positive and encouraging momentum .
however , some negative factors have also grown , posing challenges to the asia - pacific security .
dialogue and cooperation have now become a dominant characteristic of the relations between asian nations .
china and relevant asean members have made positive progress in their efforts to increase trust , dissolve suspicion , and settle disputes by peaceful means .
the north and south of the korean peninsula held a historic summit and signed a joint declaration .
on the other hand , the cold - war mentality is still affecting the way some countries perceive world politics and international relations .
the development of the nmd and the tmd is bound to undermine global strategic balance , lead to a new round of arms race , and produce broad , far - reaching negative impact on international peace and security , on the process of international arms control and disarmament , and on the international non - proliferation efforts .
in the meantime , globalization and the asian financial crisis repercussions have also adversely affected the asia - pacific security . the rich - poor gap is widening . ethnic and religious conflicts are cropping up one after another . the traditional and non - traditional security of some countries is now under pressure to a certain extent .
the maintenance of national unity , territorial integrity , independence and sovereignty is essential to the security and tranquillity of asian nations and the region at large .
only mutual respect and mutual trust can lead to peaceful coexistence and , hopefully , security in the asia - pacific region .
" mutual understanding and mutual trust , and healthy and stable relations between states constitute the political foundation of the asia - pacific security and are what we should work to achieve . "
third , the pursuit of most extensive common interests is an important way to maintaining asia - pacific security .
countries in the asia - pacific vary from one another in terms of national conditions or interests .
however , as globalization accelerates , their common interests will increase .
for example , they all wish to strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation so as to promote economic development , and narrow the north - south gap .
fourth , dialogue , cooperation , and the approach of seeking common ground while reserving differences are the best way to peace and stability in the asia - pacific region .
there are two different voices or propositions as to how we should maintain peace in the asia - pacific region .
one is for military build - up and strengthening military alliances . such policy is far from leaving the historical stage . the other is for promoting dialogue and cooperation , and enhancing understanding and trust .

development of socialist democratic politics is one of our party 's important fighting targets .
under the leadership of the party , in line with the regulations stipulated in the constitution and the law , and through various channels and forms , the people may exercise their rights to manage state affairs and to really be the master of the country .
making administrative affairs transparent is a key link to promoting legal administration , realizing the basic plan for ruling the country according to law , and building a socialist country ruled by law .
to implement the basic plan for ruling the country according to law and to build a socialist country ruled by law , all levels of government organs and their working personnel are required to do administrative affairs according to law and to realistically ensure citizens ' rights and interests .
there still exists a phenomenon that some government departments and some working personnel in government departments do not abide by law while displaying their functions and powers .
this will help government working personnel enhance the sense of legal system ; make policy decisions , handle affairs , and resolve problems according to law ; enhance the overall level of doing administrative work according to law ; and implement to the letter the requirements for ruling the country according to law . 3 .
making administrative affairs transparent is a key guarantee for helping organs of state power improve administrative forms and work styles , establish close relationship between the party and the masses and between cadres and the masses , and promoting economic and social development .
seeking benefits for the broad masses of the people and establishing close relationship between the party and the masses and between cadres and the masses is the foundation for building our party . cadres and the masses in some grassroots do not have close relations at present .
therefore , through this work , government organs and their working personnel will be able to effectively meet the development requirements in the new situation ; find ways to improve their administrative work , work methods , and work styles ; and better ensure administrative transparency , equality , and justice .
through this practice , we will find it easy to mobilize the broad masses of the people to actively , positively , and creatively take part in reform and socialist modernization and to create a good environment for promoting reform , development , and stability and realizing cross - century development strategic goals . 4 .
lacking effective supervision over and restraint of , particularly the supervision by the masses , over leading cadres ' administrative work was one of the important reasons why some leading cadres sabotaged the interests of the masses , embezzled collective and state property , and abused power for private gains in the past few years .
therefore , making town and township administrative affairs transparent is of great significance to improving the leadership , administrative levels , work styles , and work efficiency of grass - roots organs of state power and to establishing close contacts between the party and the masses and between cadres and the masses .
to make town and township administrative affairs transparent , we should resolve the issues that the people at the grass roots are most concerned with and continue expanding and intensifying the contents and forms of administrative transparency .
to carry out this practice , we should truly publicize conspicuous problems of this kind , so as to let the masses understand the real situation and conduct supervision .
different towns and townships have different economic development and social conditions .
even the people in the same towns or townships may have different topics of general interests in different periods of time .
in addition to making things known to the public and accepting supervision by the masses , organs of state power should make their affairs transparent among enterprises , institutions , and mass organizations and accept supervision by the units and organizations that have work relations with government departments .
town and township organs of state power should conscientiously make their administrative activities known to the broad masses of the people , in an effort to let the people understand the real situation and supervise their work .
besides , these organs should realistically strengthen their internal supervisory and restraint mechanisms , in an effort to ensure that the affairs that have been made transparent are true , just , and believable .
in the practice of making administrative affairs transparent , many localities have publicized their administrative systems , procedures , and results .
to achieve this , organs of state power should not only make their affairs known to the public but they should also strengthen self - supervision , self - restraint , and self - control .
the purpose of supervision is to improve the administrative work of organs of state power at various levels and to promote administrative honesty .
therefore , an extremely important aspect of this practice is to actually let the masses conduct supervision , to bring the people 's opinions and suggestions into real play , and to achieve results .
town and township government organs , as well as the grass - roots offices dispatched to towns and townships by organs of state power at a higher level should do a good job in making their administrative affairs transparent .
the grass - roots offices dispatched to towns and townships by all levels of government departments hold administrative management and supervision powers , which are closely related to the personal interests of the broad masses of the people .
it is imperative to strictly enforce discipline and to resolutely criticize , correct , and handle the grass - roots offices that fail to conscientiously make their administrative affairs transparent . 4 .
we should link the administrative transparency of towns and townships with that of villages and ensure mutual promotion , restraint , and coordination .
over the past few years , the rural grass roots throughout the nation have extensively and deeply launched activities of making known to the public the village affairs that the peasants are generally concerned with and that are related to the personal interests of the people .
therefore , administrative transparency is not simply a professional work but it is closely related to the party 's grass - roots organizational construction and ideological and political work and the government 's administrative , economic , and social management .
if we fail to achieve the work in these areas and there is not a good environment , it will be difficult for us to witness real results in making administrative affairs transparent .
strengthening leadership , conducting strict supervision , and ensuring a ceaseless deepening of the transparency of administrative affairs first , all levels of party committees and governments should realistically strengthen leadership over transparency of administrative affairs .
this work should advance in a step - by - step and orderly manner under the unified leadership of party committees , mainly under the management of the governments , and with the active participation by relevant departments .
departments should perform their own functions , fulfill their own duties , and make concerted efforts to attain all central requirements for making administrative affairs transparent .
the basic special features of these practices and experiences , such as proceeding from realities , laying stress on key points , stressing real results , and enhancing the direction and efficiency of administrative transparency , deserve to be studied and popularized .
third , we should strengthen supervision and inspection and ensure administrative transparency .
the interested parties who have one of the following situations may apply for judicial aid from the people 's courts : ( 1 ) the interested parties are seeking alimony , funds for dependents , funds for raising children , or funds for the disabled and survivors of those who die in the line of duty .
( 2 ) the interested parties seeking old - age pensions , social insurance funds , and labor remuneration really face financial hardships .
( 3 ) the interested parties seeking medical expenses and material compensation due to traffic accidents , medical accidents , industrial accidents , or other personal injury caused by an accident really face financial hardships .
( 4 ) the interested parties are childless elderly people , orphans , or from " households enjoying five guarantees " in the rural areas .
( 5 ) the interested parties are disabled persons who have no fixed sources of income to cover living expenses .
( 7 ) the interested parties are urban residents enjoying the minimum living guarantees or receiving unemployment relief , and they face financial harships because they have no other sources of income .
( 8 ) the interested parties face financial harships because of natural disasters or other irresistible forces and they are receiving government relief , or those whose families have difficulty in carrying out production and operations .
( 9 ) the interested parties who file a lawsuit against administrative organs for illegally requiring peasants to carry out obligations face financial hardships .
cases involving large sums should be submitted to the court president for examination and approval .
article 7 after the people 's courts examine the cases and approve allowing the persons concerned to delay payment of charges for judicial actions , they should begin handling the cases in accordance with the legal judicial procedures .
article 8 if the people 's courts have decided to give judicial aid to one interested party , the other party having failed in the lawsuit should pay for all the charges for judicial actions ; if they refuse to pay the charges , the people 's court may force them to do so .
article 10 these provisions will be implemented from the date of promulgation .

the united states has been planning the deployment of the nmd for a long time .
the nmd goes a step further . when it finally takes shape , we will see a three - dimensional defense system comprising early warning satellites , radars and computer guidance systems . in laymen terms , it is about hitting missiles with missiles in space .
the united states is building this system in the service of its quest for hegemony in the world .
thus , the us deployment of the nmd will pose the greatest threat to russia , and russia has never wavered in its strong opposition to the nmd .
china has always been opposed to the us dream of building a missile network in space .
while claiming that the nmd is definitely not targeted at china , the united states has been taking china as its main potential threat in its internal reports .
the united states already has the largest and most advanced nuclear and conventional arsenal in the world , and now it is exerting to develop the nmd . this not only goes against the trend of the times but harms international disarmament and arms control efforts .
the european countries are worried that the nmd will upset international strategic stability and trigger a new round of arms race . for the sake of its own security , the united states is sacrificing the security of europe .
the fact that so many countries are opposed to the nmd shows that the united states does not have any popular support .
even the us press admits that most countries in the world , including us allies , are taking the counterbalance of us forces as the keynote of their foreign policies .
if we must find a theme that runs through the foreign policy of russia after the cold war , it is its outright rejection of us leadership .
the principal contradiction between the united states and china and between the united states and russia is quite similar in nature , with the united states seeking to consolidate the international order under its domination while china and russia opposing us hegemony and striving to promote the formation of a multipolar international order .
the court of appeal of the high court of the hong kong special administrative region [ sar ] on 27 july ruled that anyone born in the hong kong sar automatically enjoys the right of abode in hong kong regardless of whether his or her parents are permanent residents of hong kong .
the number of cases were 4,426 in 1998 , 5,645 in 1999 , and 3,090 during the period from january through june this year , thus displaying an ever - rising trend .
this decision of the court of appeal is unfavorable to the enforcement of hong kong 's immigration regulations .
from a humanitarian point of view , the court of appeal 's decision also goes against the parents ' ethics and bound duty of guiding , supporting , and bringing up their newborn children and will have the effect of immediately breaking up families .
when deciding a case , a court has to give consideration to the original legislative intent , hong kong society 's well - being , and the ethics and morality that society identify themselves with .
when a case is decided in deviation from these preconditions , the judicial precedent would inevitably leave very serious aftereffects .
article 158 of the " basic law " says : " when the npc standing committee makes an interpretation , the courts of the hong kong sar , in applying the provision concerned , shall follow the interpretation of the npc standing committee . "
the npc standing committee 's law interpretation documents are the elaboration of the original legislative intent of the " basic law " and must be followed by hong kong courts in deciding a case .
yet this time the court of appeal did not follow the npc standing committee 's law interpretation document when making a decision .
according to the npc standing committee 's law interpretation document , the preparatory committee 's 10 august 1996 opinions on the implementation of article 24 , section 2 , of the " basic law " are legally binding .
on the surface , with administrative intervention , the " war " between hunan 's radio and television bureau and its postal and telecommunications bureau , which has lasted nearly four years , seems to have come to an end .
the cause of the " war " is that neither of them is willing to give up " cable television transmission " - - a piece of " fat meat " .
huang heqing , director of the hunan cable television station , said angrily : " they are really lawless , and what they said does not count . "
what did the changsha telecommunications bureau have to say ?
on 18 july , this reporter went to the bureau , and a person in charge of the bureau 's news center said : " this is a very sensitive issue .
our bureau has resolutely abided by the decision of the provincial cpc committee and government and has stopped transmitting television signals . currently , our network is on lease to the hunan provincial branch of xinhua for transmitting its signals . so you should go to ask the hunan branch of xinhua . "
liu min , director of the office of the hunan branch of xinhua , said : " we are not on the postal and telecommunications bureau 's side , nor are we on the radio and television bureau 's side .
we have been cooperating with the changsha telecommunications bureau since 1997 and have leased their broadcasting facility to transmit our encrypted ' xinhua audio and video reference .
on 29 june , to our surprise , the ministry of radio and television sent us a notice asking us to stop the transmission . but , the ' xinhua audio and video reference ' has always been valued by the high - level leadership , and we could not stop transmitting it just at short notice .
as to other television channels , we have never used them for transmissions . "
in addition , the hunan radio and television bureau also has met resistance from its subscribers in taking over the former " territory " of the changsha telecommunications bureau .
at a new residential area in shangmayuan ridge in changsha 's kaifu district , this reporter recently saw that only a few households connected radio and television cable into their houses , and most of them just connected the cable to the stairways .
they said television pictures transmitted by the telecommunications bureau were clear and that the bureau offered many channels free of charge , and asked why the bureau was ordered to stop transmitting .
when subscribers applied for service , they were asked to install multimedia devices , or their applications would not be approved . now that every household has completed the required installations , they were asked to install cable television .
besides , they were not allowed to install hidden cables , which looked better .
some of the subscribers also argued that because there was competition , the attitude and quality of service of the radio and television bureau 's workers became much better .
at about 0400 that afternoon , the linxiang city radio and television bureau sent workers to cut the telecommunications bureau 's transmission lines and , at the same time , held an emergency meeting to discuss countermeasures .
when the meeting had just ended and before those attending the meeting could leave the meeting venue , zhou wenquan , deputy director of the city telecommunications bureau , led a group of men to rush into the meeting room in a very threatening manner .
those people had long knives , guns , iron bars , and other kinds of weapons in their hands and hit everyone in their way . yang jianjun attempted to stop those people , but they fired at him , and his chest was hit by a pellet .
using the last drop of his energies , he dashed into a room with iron fence . after he entered the room , a technician named zhu zhixiong and wang guoqi , director of the chengxi district office of the linxiang city cable television station , quickly closed the door .
they hit the three inside the room through the holes of the fence with sabers of nearly one meter in length . each of the three inside the room used a chair as a shield and lied prone on the floor to dodge being shot .
according to an investigation , those taking part in the " bloody " incident included some youths who were not engaged in decent work , in addition to some young employees of the city telecommunications bureau .
on 15 may 1999 , the shaodong county telecommunications bureau hung horizontal banners in the county 's capital town and all townships and towns . the banners read , " channels of multi - media telecommunication for transmitting television programs are many and the pictures are clear . "
at 0500 in the afternoon on that day , workers of the county 's cable television station removed the banners .
after receiving a call from a radio and television bureau employee using a public phone , " 110 " people 's policemen again rushed to the scene to quell the second assault and , after that , stood guard at the gate of the building .
the county leaders continued to summon contingency units of local public security and militia to the scene as an enforcement , and finally were able to stop the telecommunications bureau 's assault .
as everyone knows , fees collected from cable television subscribers are a piece of " fat meat . "
it has been learned that currently there are about 3 million cable television subscribers in hunan , and the radio and television departments ' annual revenues exceed 300 million yuan .
the hunan radio and television bureau has striven to maintain its monopoly status because it is critically important to maintaining the revenues .
furthermore , only a multi - media telecommunications network is available in western hunan . once it is cut , no programs can be received .

at the central committee 's conference on ideological and political work , comrade jiang zemin emphasized that the most fundamental point in strengthening ideological and political work was to adhere to and strengthen the guiding position of marxism in the ideological community of our country .
this exposition has not only demonstrated the fundamental position of scientific theory in ideological and political work , but it also has proposed the fundamental task in strengthening and improving ideological and political work .
we must permeate this important guiding principle throughout the implementation of ideological and political work .
our party solemnly wrote marxism across its banner from the day of its birth and has been regarding it as the guide in all practice .
the history of china 's revolution and construction under the leadership of the party is a record of adhering to and strengthening marxism 's guiding position .
if we eradicate the leading position of marxism and adopt multiple guiding principles , it is very likely to cause confusion in peoples ' hearts and disorder throughout the country and bring about disaster to our party , our country and our nation .
in this sense , ensuring that marxism is in the guiding position is the fundamental task of ideological and political work and also the fundamental guarantee that strengthens and improves ideological and political work .
without this point , the existence of ideological and political work would be valueless and the reinforcement and improvement of this work would be meaningless .
marx and engles noted : " the ruling ideology in any era is but the ideology of the ruling class . "
western countries always label themselves with " absolute freedom of thought . " why do they not allow marxism to be in the guiding position of their ideology ?
the reason is obvious .
in the field of ideology , the struggle between marxism and anti - marxism and that between penetration and counter - penetration are protracted , complex and at times sharp .
we must maintain a clear understanding of this .
we must understand the extreme importance of the issue from such a heightened perspective .
adhering to marxism 's guiding position is by no means contradictory to the diversity of society 's economic components and economic interests .
in terms of ownership structure , many economic components coexist , with public ownership as the mainstay . in terms of the distribution system , there are many forms , with distribution according to laborers ' work as the mainstay .
in general , our " diversity " is diversity with the " mainstay " as a precondition , and our " mainstay " is a " mainstay " with " diversity " as supplement .
therefore , however diversified are the economic components and economic interests , as long as these two " mainstays " exist , the socialist nature of china 's market economy will not change .
our adherence to marxism 's guiding position not only complies with the " material relationship of the ruling position , " but it is also the inevitable demand of consolidating and developing this " material relationship " so that it remains correctly oriented and rises to a higher plane .
it is patently wrong that , since economic components and economic interests are diversified , guiding ideology should also be diversified .
marxism is not an enclosed system .
ever since its birth , marxism has been constantly expanding its theoretical and knowledge content and constantly innovates , far surpassing all kinds of other theoretical systems .
