hong kong , 11 jan (zts) - - taipei news : a mysterious aircraft cave shelter at an air base in taitung that the taiwan military built as part of the " chienan project " has been brought to light .
the strategic aircraft shelter , in the form of a tunnel dug through granite rock at the chihhang air base in taitung , is designed to station fighter units from western taiwan in wartime . it reportedly can withstand direct hits by conventional bombs . as a result , the air force 's combat strength will be preserved .
the " chienan area " of taitung 's chihhang air base , a top - secret site of the taiwan military , follows the mountain terrain along the side of the base runway .
as with hualien 's chiashan base , it was built with the approval of chiang ching - kuo [ jiang jingguo ] , when hau pei - tsun [ hao bocun ] was " chief of the general staff " of the taiwan military .
construction costs topped 10 billion new taiwan dollars .
to ensure that daily - use and wartime facilities inside the caves are in proper working condition , air and ground crews are required to spend a full day inside the caves each month .
from their words , it is not hard to get a glimpse of the contours of the new us administration 's foreign policy and global strategy .
recalling the time in the early 1990 's when the cold war had just ended , due to the breakup of the soviet union the united states boasted that it was now the world 's sole superpower and predicted that the world would become " unipolar , " with over 180 countries obeying america 's baton .
however , the calls for world " multipolarization " were very loud ; this was advocated not only by china and russia but even by america 's principal allies ; the european union and japan tended toward " multipolarization " while the developing countries supported this concept all the more .
in this situation , america 's " unipolarization " encountered all kinds of obstacles .
since the us economy has grown strongly in recent years , its military strength far outstrips anyone else , and it controls international organizations such as the world trade organization and the world bank , many in political and academic circles have become dizzy and declared that the us pursuit of world " unipolarization " is historically inevitable .
bush and his advisers criticize the democratic party and the clinton - gore administration for trying to take charge of everything in the world and causing resentment in various countries on that account ; they advocate in the future only taking charge of major affairs , not minor ones , contracting the overseas front , and pursuing real interests .
hence , the core issue in us global strategy in the new century will be " to mobilize all national resources " to build the nmd and theater missile defense (tmd) systems , to ensure us military security and absolute national security , the better to give free rein to foreign intervention and exercise " unipolar " hegemonism .
they believe that producing and deploying nmd will cost several hundred billion dollars and this can not only prolong the life of the defense industries but can also maintain us military hi - tech superiority in the new century .

second , the palestinian - israeli conflict , the korean peninsula , and the taiwan strait are currently the hottest regional problems for the united states , and they are all concentrated in the mideast and the asia - pacific region .
third , the weight of the china factor in us foreign policy strategy is on the rise , and the united states will carry out a policy of " engagement and containment " regarding china .

the golan heights has an area of 1,860 square km . it is situated in southwestern syria and adjacent to lebanon , israel , and jordan . its terrain is dangerously steep . it overlooks the galilee valley of israel to the west and guards the passageway into damascus to the east .
the heights has always been syria 's territory . however , in the third middle east war in 1967 , it was occupied by israel .
syria recovered part of the heights during the fourth middle east war in 1973 . in the following year , through the mediation of the united states , the israeli army withdrew from part of the region , and a non - military region was established under the control of un peacekeeping forces .

new delhi , 12 jan ( xinhua ) - - on the morning of 12 january , li peng , chairman of china 's national people 's congress standing committee , met indian external affairs minister jaswant singh at the taj mahal hotel and both sides held warm and friendly talks .
li peng stressed that india is china 's important and close neighbor and that it is china 's unswerving policy to establish and develop a lasting and stable good - neighborly relationship with india .
the mainstream of sino - indian relations lies in the common interests and common points of both sides .
china 's basic attitude is that differences and problems between the two countries should by no means become obstacles to the development of their relations and they could absolutely be well resolved through friendly consultations .
li peng said that when the late indian prime minister rajiv gandhi visited china , both sides reached the important understanding that the border issue should be resolved on the principle of " mutual understanding , mutual accommodation and mutual adjustment . "
in 1993 and 1996 , the two governments also signed two key accords concerning the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border area and confidence - building measures , adding that these two accords are being implemented with joint efforts of both sides and positive progress has been made .
the problems left over by the past can be gradually resolved as long as both sides work hard with good wishes and in an earnest manner .
singh said he agreed with li peng 's view , saying india and china , whose populations together account for one - third of the world 's total , would surely make greater contribution to the advancement of the mankind if the two countries cooperate with each other .
chairman li peng reminisced with deep feeling his association with the former indian prime minister rajiv gandhi .
he said that china and india have a long history of friendly relations but there were twists and turns between them in the 1950 s and 1960 s .
whenever we look back at the history of the relations between china and india , we will remember him for his significant contributions during his lifetime .
sonia gandhi was particularly pleased that she had the opportunity to meet chairman li peng and his wife again .
the chinese communist party and the congress party of india have always kept friendly exchanges and close ties and each party has made its own contributions to the development of the relationship between the two countries .
li peng said that the international situation is undergoing profound changes at the turn of the century .
he said that the chinese communist party shares a similar opinion on the two major trends of political multi - polarization and economic globalization with various parties of india and would further strengthen cooperation with the congress party and other indian parties to explore a better future for the relationship between china and india .
chen huanyou , gu shanqing , and zhou gang , who accompanied chairman li peng during the visit , were present at the meeting .

among these there were the " 4 july south - north joint communique " signed in 1972 - - which declared three principles of unification , and the " south - north agreement on reconciliation , nonaggression and exchanges and cooperation " signed in 1991 .
among these , what has most attracted attention were the first talks between leaders of both sides since the peninsula was split , and the issuance of the " south - north joint declaration . "
the major significance of this event was that it laid a foundation for reconciliation and cooperation by both sides , and it pushed forward the process of reconciliation for the peninsula .
since the north - south korean summit , both sides have already subsequently carried out multiple ministerial - level talks and other high - level talks .
finally , four agreements for the promotion of economic cooperation have been signed .
south korea for its part has improved its past method of " employing soft and hard , both enticements and pressure , " pushing forward a policy of reconciliation and cooperation , and striving for peaceful coexistence between south and north .
there are two chief internal factors which led to foreign affairs policy adjustments on both sides : first was public support and opposition .
ending confrontation , seeking reconciliation , and finally realizing self - independence and peaceful unification is the common wish of all the people on the korean peninsula , and was also an irresistible historical tide .
this was the fundamental internal factor causing a transformation in the situation .
second was economic factors .
in regard to north korea , overcoming economic difficulties and obtaining assistance from international society including south korea would help its economic recovery .
at the same time , the future economic development of north korea similarly required a peaceful and stable environment and fine international relations .
viewed from the perspective of external factors , peace and development had already become an irreversible global tide .
the decisions made in the " seoul manifesto regarding peace on the korean peninsula " issued at the third summit of asian and european leaders - - held last october - - were all a manifestation of this irreversible tide .
additionally , the respective roles played by periphery nations also were an important factor in promoting peace and stability on the korean peninsula .

new delhi , 13 jan ( xinhua ) - - on 13 january at india 's international center , china national people 's congress standing committee chairman li peng gave a speech entitled " promote understanding , develop friendship , enhance cooperation . "
in the 20 th century , mankind experienced two world wars ; and at the same time , the people also propelled the wheel of history forward .
india and china respectively won independence and national liberation , and these were precisely two of the great events that took place during the century .
in the 20 th century , mankind created a civilization that had never been seen before ; and thanks to the great impetus provided by the scientific and technological revolution , social productivity developed by leaps and bounds . today , we are entering an era marked by a greater prosperity and progress .
it is our hope that the new century will become one in which the people of all countries in the world can share peace and undergo a common growth , and in which different civilizations can learn from one another and achieve a common progress .
multipolarization is a natural trend in international relations in today 's world , and it is conducive to bringing true world peace , stability , and democracy .
international affairs are intricate and complex , and it is therefore unfair , as well as impossible , for one country or a handful of countries to manipulate them .
international affairs ought to be settled by all countries through consultations , global challenges ought to be coped with by all countries in cooperation , and the fate of the world ought to be held in the hands of the people of all countries .
globalization has already become an unavoidable reality in the world economy today , and it can help all countries expand their capital sources , introduce advanced technologies , and draw on the successful management experiences of others .
of course , we must not overlook the negative side of globalization .
the disparity between the poor and the rich is widening on a global scale , and the south - north contradictions have become increasingly acute .
what we need is a globalization which can bring about a win - win situation , coexistence , and a common development between developed and developing countries .
these principles have proved to be an evergreen tree that assimilates nutrients from both eastern civilization and the spirit of our times .
mr. nehru used to say : " if all countries can recognize and pursue these principles , then there will be no more conflicts or wars in this world . "
mr. deng xiaoping pointed out : " the five principles of peaceful coexistence have proved to be the best way ever for handling relations between different nations .
basing on our summarization of the practice of international relations , we can well say that the five principles of peaceful coexistence enjoy the greatest vitality . "
in ancient times , our forefathers feared no difficulties or hardships , and traveled over land and water to promote exchanges between the chinese civilization and the indian civilization , which were then two of the world 's major civilizations ; and what they did added a glorious chapter to the history of world cultural exchanges .
( jiumoluoshi ) [ name as transliterated ] and ( da - mo ) [ name as transliterated ] left home to pursue their studies in the east , bringing to the chinese people the true essence of buddhism .
in modern times , the people of our two countries sympathized with , understood , and supported each other in the struggle for national independence and people 's liberation .
history requires us to add yet another new chapter to the friendship between china and india on the foundations laid by our forefathers .
china and india are two of the largest developing countries in this world , and both share common interests of a wide range in the world politics and the international economy .
during president narayanan 's visit to china last year , both countries reaffirmed that china and india would not regard each other as a threat or a rival , and we both reiterated our continued adherence to the five principles of peaceful coexistence .
the leaders of both countries also reached consensus on issues of an extensive range concerning future ways to push forward the friendly cooperation between china and india .
all these have laid a foundation and have provided a guarantee for a healthy growth of the sino - indian relations in the future .
india is a major neighbor of china ; and promoting good - neighborly and friendly relations with india has been our consistent policy , and has also been an important content in china 's foreign policy of peripheral peace .
we have never regarded india as a threat , and neither do we have the intention to pose a threat to any other countries or to seek any scope for interference .
we are willing to step up cooperation with india in international affairs .
we have assigned great importance to enhancing understanding and mutual trust with india .
we believe that there indeed exists the problem of insufficient mutual understanding between china and india , and enhancing understanding and mutual trust is therefore a pressing matter of the moment in our current effort to promote bilateral relations .
china wishes to see a prosperous , well - developed , and rich and strong india ; and it welcomes india to play a greater active role in both international and regional affairs .
we are gratified to see that over the past decade , india 's economy has been growing at an average annual rate of over six percent , its information industry is undergoing rapid growth , and the country has ranked among the world 's first in software development .
china congratulates india on all the achievements that it has attained in various fields over the past more than 50 years since its independence , and it appreciates india 's past efforts in safeguarding the rights and interests of developing countries .
china supports all efforts that aim at bringing about peace and stability in the region of south asia , and supports south asia 's process of regional cooperation .
ladies , gentlemen , and friends , like india , china used to be bullied and humiliated by western powers in modern times .
to win independence and liberation for themselves , the chinese people , led by the communist party of china , waged an unyielding struggle , advancing and filling the breach left by fallen comrades .
historical experiences have told us that only under the prerequisite of its state sovereignty not being violated and its society remaining stable can a country concentrate its energy and attention on economic construction , and can it constantly enhance its national strength and improve the living standards of its people .
the targets set for the first two steps have already been met smoothly .
the objective set for the third step of the development strategy is that by the middle of this century , china is to attain the level of moderately developed countries in per - capita gnp , basically realize modernization , and build itself into a rich , strong , democratic , and civilized socialist country .
we have three major tasks in the new century : continuously pushing forward the country 's modernization building , fulfilling the objective of reunifying the motherland , and safeguarding world peace and bringing about common development .
china 's development will not only bring benefits to the chinese people , but will also prove conducive to the peace and development of the world ; and it will never pose a threat to any other countries .
china opposes hegemonism , and will never seek world dominance itself .
as a large and responsible country , china will pursue without wavering its independent foreign policy of peace , and will strive to make new and greater contributions to mankind .
over the past more than 20 years since china started the practice of reform and opening up , we have always regarded it a basic national principle to develop a socialist democracy and improve the socialist legal system .
today , together with other asian countries , china and india are shouldered with common responsibilities for the future of asia .
new delhi , 13 jan ( xinhua ) - - li peng , chairman of the standing committee of the chinese national people 's congress who is visiting india , was interviewed by reporters of india 's all india television station and the " hindu " at the hotel where he is staying on the morning of 13 january .
reporter : chairman li , how do you appraise the current situation of sino - indian bilateral relations ?
li peng : the mainstream of contacts between china and india is good .
since then , exchanges of high - level visits have continued .
my visit this time has given me a strong impression that the two peoples and two governments of china and india hope to develop relations of friendly cooperation between the two countries and to get along with each other harmoniously .
the common points between us far outnumber differences .
the boundary issue between china and india is an issue handed downed from history . if both sides hold talks on the basis of the principle of mutual understanding and mutual accommodation agreed between us , i think it will not be difficult to settle the issue .
li peng : political multipolarization is a trend of world development and china and india share the same view .
china and india are two of the largest developing countries in the world and both face the task of development .
the trend of economic globalization is both advantageous and disadvantageous to the developing countries and we should pursue advantages and avoid disadvantages .
china and india can cooperate on this issue and make efforts to establish a just and rational new international political and economic order .
china is opposed to any country 's interference in the internal affairs of another country .
it is precisely on the basis of this basic viewpoint that china and india share an identical or similar stand on some international issues .
however , because we are developing countries , we should attach greater importance to the right to existence and the right to development in addition to political rights . india supports us in this respect .
reporter : you made your first visit to india in 1991 and now you are revisiting india again . what changes you think have taken place in india in the past 10 years ?
what impression has it made on you ?
this time , i have the opportunity of visiting other cities . i have been to bombay and i am going to visit bangalore and agra , india 's famous cultural city . in this way , i can gain a relatively comprehensive understanding of india .
reporter : how does china look at the existing boundary issue in the sino - indian relations ?
in 1993 , the governments of the two countries signed an agreement on maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas along the line of actual control of china and india , which is a very important agreement .
i believe that as long as there is the political wish of settling this issue , the issue that has been handed down from history will certainly be settled gradually and properly through negotiations on the basis of the five principles of peaceful coexistence .
besides , the settlement of this issue will inevitably enable china and india , two big developing countries , to play a better role in international affairs .
what is its attitude toward the process of the settlement of the kashmir issue ?
li peng : china pursues an independent foreign policy of peace and hopes all its neighboring countries , including india and pakistan , will maintain peaceful and friendly relations .
both india and pakistan are important countries in the subcontinent of south asia and their relations will have a direct impact on peace and stability of the region .
we have noticed that both india and pakistan have recently adopted some new measures for the kashmir issue .
we welcome and support all efforts conducive to improving the relations between india and pakistan and to relaxing tension in the regional situation .
reporter : what is china 's stand on the issue of international terrorism ?
li peng : the chinese government has always been opposed to and condemned all forms of international terrorism , and opposed to taking terrorist and violent actions by any country , organization , collective or individual .
terrorism can only do harm to the people .
li peng : regarding the united states ' setting up the missile defense system , china is opposed to it , russia is opposed to it , and there are also people in the west and in the united states who are opposed to it .
the setting up of the missile defense system is a kind of new arms race and a kind of cold war mentality , which is harmful to world peace .
we welcome the same stand taken by india .
we hope the 21 st century will be a century of peace and a century of development . it should not be a century of war . we hope there will not be any hot war or cold war in the new century .
before the end of the interview , li peng asked india 's news media to convey to the indian people the cordial regards and good wishes of the chinese people and himself .
according to wto regulations , developed countries have the right to provide 5 - percent subsidies to their agriculture , and this figure rises to 10 percent for developing countries , but china 's agricultural subsidies now stand at merely 2 percent .
long said : china upholds this request in consideration of the vast numbers of farmers who are still not well off .
with regard to some countries requesting that china revoke the right to raise its agricultural subsidies , he said this is unacceptable because such a request is totally unreasonable .
according to reports from geneva , the meeting will go on for a week .
at present , other issues still to be discussed include foreign companies ' access to china 's service industry and their rights to conduct business in china .
he said those friendly people at the meeting were envoys of sino - indian friendship and thanked them for having made precious contributions to promoting sino - indian friendship over the years , especially during the period when sino - indian relations experienced difficulties .
at the meeting with people of india 's business circle , li peng first heard suggestions made by chairmen of various specialized industry committees of the india federation of industry on carrying out cooperation in the infrastructure construction , information , tourism , pharmaceutical , and other industries between the two countries .
he said : trade between china and india has increased 10 folds over the last 10 years , which is quite a significant progress . however , currently trade volume between the two countries is still not large and is not commensurate with the scales of the two countries ' economies .
we should jointly work to continue this good development trend .
there is still huge potential in cooperation between the two countries .
li peng stressed : china and india are the world 's two largest developing countries . their current economic scales and foreign trade development levels provide a huge possibility to further develop economic and trade cooperation between the two countries .
china will soon enter the wto and china 's market will be opened wider .

article 2 - - a marriage system with freedom of marriage , based on monogamy , and with equality between the man and woman shall be implemented .
article 3 - - marriages involved with bride - trafficking , mercenary marriages , or other acts that interfere with freedom of marriage are prohibited .
taking advantage of a marriage to exact money or property is forbidden .
bigamy is prohibited , as are all other acts that violate the monogamous marriage system .
desertion of family members is prohibited .
article 4 - - husband and wife should be faithful to each other and should support each other . family members should respect elders and love children , and uphold equal , harmonious , and civilized marriage and family relations .
chapter 2 - - marriage contract article 5 - - both the man and the woman must be completely willing participants in order to marry . any force by one party toward the other or third party interference is prohibited .
later marriages and childbirth in later years should be encouraged .
if the marriage complies with the stipulations of this law , the couple will be allowed to register and will be granted a marriage certificate . a husband and wife relationship is established as soon as a marriage certificate has been acquired .
article 9 - - after registering a marriage , the woman may become a member of the man 's household or the man may become a member of the woman 's household , in accordance with the agreed wishes of the two parties .
article 11 - - for marriages that are a result of force , the party that suffered coercion may request the marriage registration office or the people 's court to nullify the marriage .
the application of the party that suffered coercion should be proposed within a year from the date of registration of the marriage .
article 12 - - marriages that are null and void , or that have been nullified , are null and void from the beginning [ of the marriage ] .
however , all properties obtained during the period of cohabitation , except for cases of bigamy , will be divided based on the principles of jointly owned property . when one party is at fault , it is permitted to give said party a smaller portion or none at all .
for all children of the parties involved , the regulations regarding parents and children in this law will be applied .
article 14 - - husbands and wives shall both have the right to use their own surname and given name .
all property acquired during the time husbands and wives had married relations that does not have a clear and definite agreement jointly belongs to the husband and wife .
article 19 - - husbands and wives may draw up a written agreement indicating property before the marriage and property from the time of married relations that is jointly owned or owned by respective parties , or that is jointly owned in part , or owned in part by respective parties .
if a husband or wife has outside debts and a third party is aware of an agreement regarding property from the time of married relations that belongs to respective parties , then the husband 's or wife 's property may be used to pay off the debts .
article 21 - - parents have an obligation to raise and educate their children , and children have an obligation to support and assist their parents .
if parents do not carry out their obligation to raise their children , children who are minors or who are unable to live on their own have the right to demand support payments from their parents .
article 24 - - husbands and wives have the right to inherit each other 's property .
parents and children have the right to inherit each other 's property .
article 25 - - children born out of wedlock have the right to enjoy equal status as children born in wedlock . no person may harm or discriminate against said children .
the biological parents of children born out of wedlock shall both shoulder the living expenses and education expenses of the children , until the time that the children are able to live on their own .
article 26 - - the state protects lawful adoptive relationships .
relevant provisions in this law regarding relations between parents and children shall apply to the rights and obligations in relations between adoptive parents and adopted children .
the rights and obligations between adopted children and biological parents are terminated as a result of the establishment of adoptive relations .
article 27 - - abuse or discrimination between stepparents and stepchildren is prohibited .
relevant provisions in this law regarding relations between parents and children shall apply to the rights and obligations in relations between a stepfather or stepmother and the stepchildren that they raise and educate .
grandchildren who have the ability to support [ their grandparents ] have an obligation to support their grandparents when the children of the grandparents are dead or are unable to support them .
younger brothers or younger sisters who have been raised by their elder brothers or sisters and who have the ability to support [ their elder siblings ] have an obligation to support elder brothers or sisters who lack the ability to work and who lack means to support themselves .
article 30 - - children should respect the marriage rights of their parents , and may not interfere with their parents ' remarriage or life after marriage . the obligations of children to support parents do not end as a result of a change in their parents ' marriage .
chapter 4 - - divorce article 31 - - marriages in which both parties wish to divorce may be granted a divorce .
both parties must apply in person for a divorce with the marriage registration office .
article 33 - - if the spouse of a soldier in active service desires a divorce , the soldier 's consent must be obtained .
this restriction shall not apply in cases where the wife applies for a divorce , or when the people 's court deems it necessary to accept the divorce application made by the husband .
article 36 - - the relationship between parents and children shall not come to an end with the parents ' divorce .
after divorce , whether the children are put in the custody of the father or the mother , they shall remain the children of both parents .
if a dispute arises between the two parents over the custody of a child who has been weaned and they fail to reach an agreement , the people 's court shall make a judgment in accordance with the rights and interests of the child and the actual conditions of the parents .
the mode and times of visitation shall be negotiated by the parties concerned . if they fail to reach an agreement , a judgment will be made by the people 's court .
debts incurred separately by the husband or the wife shall be paid by the party who incurred them .
in cases where domestic violence is ongoing , victims may ask the public security office for assistance , and may also ask villagers ' committees or neighborhood committees to intervene on their behalf .
in cases where one party has deserted family members , victims may ask the people 's court to , in accordance with the law , pass judgment on and make a decision on payment [ by the deserting party ] of costs of upbringing , maintenance or support .
article 47 - - if a husband and wife draw up an agreement stipulating ownership of property acquired before marriage and property acquired during the time of married relations , with the intention of evading debts , then the agreement is null and void .
related individuals and units shall have an obligation to assist such executions .
article 50 - - with regard to all other acts related to marriage and the family that violate the law , the law has other regulations for punishment , and will act in accordance with said regulations .
chapter 6 - - supplementary provisions article 51 - - the people 's congresses of national autonomous areas and their standing committees may formulate certain adaptations or supplementary provisions in keeping with the principles of this law , and in light of the specific conditions of the local nationalities in regard to marriage and family .
provisions formulated by autonomous regions must be submitted to the standing committee of the national people 's congress for the record .
article 52 - - this law came into force on 1 january 1981 .
the marriage law of the people 's republic of china promulgated on 1 may 1950 , shall be invalidated as of the day this law comes into force .
beijing , 14 january ( xinhua ) - - good news comes thick and fast as one century is about to give way to the next .
the goal of reforming and turning around state enterprises in three years , which has received broad attention , has essentially been accomplished .
the drive to create a modern enterprise system composed of the large and mid - sized mainstay state enterprises will also make substantial progress .
persevere in enterprise reform , fully confident that success is inevitable state enterprises are the pillar of the national economy and the backbone of the republic .
the cpc central committee 's working conference of april 1979 proposed that enterprises be given more decision - making authority . this was followed by a series of successively deeper reforms , including the delegation of production and operational power , the contract system , and the taxes - in - lieu - of profits reform .
nevertheless , the thrust of reform during this period was directed at delegating power and letting enterprises keep their profits .
as market - oriented reform began deepening by the day after 1990 , problems like the state enterprises ' rigid mechanisms and inefficiency became more and more pronounced . reform deepening has become a matter of burning urgency .
general secretary jiang zemin has emphasized many times , " making state enterprises , especially large and mid - sized state enterprises , a success is both a major economic issue that impacts the development of the entire national economy and a weighty political matter on whose outcome hinges the destiny of the socialist system . "
he demanded that every cadre delve deeply into the enterprises to conduct painstaking research , obtain first - hand materials on enterprise reform , honor the masses ' innovative spirit , review experiences in a timely manner , and correctly guide enterprise reform . "
in october 1992 the 14 th cpc national congress made it the goal of china 's reform to establish a socialist market economy .
it also pointed out that changing the operating mechanisms of state enterprises , especially large and mid - sized state enterprises , is a central link in the creation of a socialist market economy and is pivotal to solidifying the socialist system and bringing out the superiority of socialism .
this goal summed up the lessons we have learned from economic structuring , especially enterprise reform , in china for the last dozen years and more .
in 1994 , the cpc central committee and the state council decided to let 100 enterprises test the modern enterprise system on a trial basis .
his speech unified the thinking of the whole party and bolstered the confidence of the cadres and masses .
the 15 th cpc national congress also emphasized the need to make the entire national economy a success , turn around the large enterprises while deregulating the small ones , and conduct strategic restructuring .
the shift from reviving state enterprises one by one to making the entire national economy a success represented yet another significant breakthrough in state enterprise reform .
addressing a plenary session of the state council , premier zhu rongji emphasized that state enterprise reform impacts the whole situation and that " the two goals " must be accomplished within three years as scheduled .
nineteen ninety - nine was a critical year in state enterprise reform .
in early spring general secretary jiang zemin toured inner mongolia , sichuan , hubei , shaanxi , shandong , and liaoning for in - depth studies .
the " decision " analyzed the situation facing state enterprise reform and development , further clarified the major objectives and guiding principles , put forward strategic measures aimed at putting state enterprises on a sound footing , and laid a solid foundation for achieving the goal of reforming and turning around state enterprises within three years .
the cpc central committee and the state council have made meticulous plans . making a concerted effort , all localities , sectors , and enterprises firmly implemented the string of important policy measures devised by the central government to put state enterprises on a sound footing .
a new look has emerged in state enterprise reform and substantial progress has been made .

washington , 15 jan ( xinhua ) - - like a mirror , the development of sino - us relations has reflected , from one aspect , the volatile changes in international situation in the past century .
in the 21 st century , the continued development of sino - us relations in a steady and healthy manner will make a greater contribution to world peace , prosperity , and progress .
in the first half of the 20 th century , starting with the invasion of beijing by the " eight - power allied forces , " the chinese people were subject to insult and humiliation by the western big powers including the united states .
their successful cooperation in the antifascist war proved , for the first time in history , that sino - us relations play a major role in safeguarding regional and world peace .
in the 20 - odd years following the birth of new china , the united state held on to its policy of containment , regarding china as its enemy . it enforced a military encirclement and economic blockade of china and supported the taiwan authorities in usurping china 's seat at the united nations .
in 1968 , in an effort to extricate the united states from the morass of the vietnam war and cope with the soviet expansion , richard nixon , after being elected president , began to gradually adjust the us china policy .
after president jimmy carter took office , the two countries signed the " joint communique on the establishment of diplomatic relations between the united states and the prc " in december 1978 .
the normalization of sino - us relations started simultaneously with the introduction of china 's reform and opening up , while the latter added a strong impetus to the development of the former .
thanks to the firm struggle of the chinese side , the two governments signed , on 17 august 1982 , a joint communique on resolving the issue of us arms sales to taiwan step by step .
between the late 1980 s and early 1990 s , the most drastic turmoil and the most profound change since the end of world war ii occurred in the international situation .
in the wake of the drastic changes in eastern europe and the disintegration of the soviet union , anticommunist and anti - china forces in the united states and the west were once rife and rampant .
in 1989 , the us government announced the imposition of economic sanctions against china and the suspension of high - level exchanges between the two countries .
an opportune moment enabling sino - us relations to bottom out came at the informal meeting of leaders of the asia - pacific economic cooperation (apec) held in seattle in november 1994 .
during the meeting , president jiang zemin and president clinton held the first meeting between both sides .
president jiang stressed that both countries should have the whole world in view , have their eyes on the future , and bring a stable and healthy sino - us relationship and a peaceful , stable , and safe world into the 21 st century .
under the impetus of the sino - us top - level meeting in seattle , the clinton administration put forward a policy of engagement with china in 1994 .
in the same year , the senior officials of both governments resumed the exchange of visits , which the united unilaterally suspended for more than three years ; the us government announced the de - linking of human rights issue with the " mfn status . "
however , the development of sino - us relations again suffered another setback in 1995 .
in may , ignoring the chinese government 's repeated opposition , the us government flagrantly approved lee teng - hui 's visit to the united states , causing sino - us relations to plunge to their lowest point since the establishment of diplomatic relations 16 years before .
in response to this , the chinese government filed a strong protest with the us side .
between 25 june and 3 july 1998 , president clinton visited china .
both parties further defined the direction and framework of the development of sino - us relation facing the 21 st century .
the successful exchange of visits between the two heads of state instilled new vitality to the improvement of bilateral relations .
following the meeting between jiang and clinton in auckland , new zealand , in october of the same year , relations between the two countries began to move out of the shadow of the " embassy - bombing incident . "
in november , china and the united states finally reached agreement on china 's accession to the world trade organization .
in 2000 , sino - us relations were further repaired and attained steady development .
during the un millennium summit and the informal meeting of apec leaders , the two heads of state held one meeting after another ; the two countries resumed security dialogues and military exchanges ; the us congress approved the bill on permanent normal trading relations for china .
taking a panoramic view of history , we can see that the development path of sino - us relations has been very rough and bumpy .
whether or not the question of taiwan can be handled in accordance with the principles laid down in the three joint communiques has a direct bearing on the stability , improvement , and development of sino - us relations in the new century .
fourth , it is necessary to resolve differences between both sides in the spirit of mutual respect , consultation on an equal basis , and seeking common grounds while reserving differences .

sanya , 14 jan - - the second globalization forum drew to a close today .
he says , the delegates who participate in the forum have examined and explored this important contemporary phenomenon and the issue of economic globalization from all angles and from various empirical experiences , which should help all to gain deeper knowledge of the process .
the international and domestic situations at the crossroads of the centuries have decided that if we want to develop , we must accelerate the readjustment of the economic structure . this is the background behind the " proposal " that makes structural readjustments the mainline of the " tenth five - year plan . "
today 's structural readjustments are active readjustments made on our own initiative under the condition of ample supply of goods , spurred by the new - tech revolution , and are interactive with the world economy ; they are strategic readjustments .
two , this round of readjustments is comprehensive and not partial . china 's existing economic structure is riddled with problems .
primarily , the industrial structure ( the primary , secondary , tertiary , and within various industries ) is poor ; regional ( primarily the eastern , central , and western regions ) developments are not coordinated , and the standard of urbanization is low .
these are the more serious contradictions in the country 's economic development .
this round of readjustment is not partial readjustments of certain sectors or regions but consists of comprehensive readjustments of the whole industrial structure , regional structure , urban and rural structure , as well as the mix of ownership systems .
the readjustments emphasize economic efficiency as the core , and the goal is to raise the industrial standard , the technological level , and the competitive capability .
on the one hand , we want to eliminate backward productive capability , and on the other hand , we want to form new economic growth points that in turn provide the motive force to drive further economic development .
therefore , we must properly handle the relationship between development and readjustment , insist on making structural readjustments amid development , and use the readjustments to promote economic development .
today 's readjustments are carried out in an environment where we have a preliminary socialist market economic system and we are about to join the wto . in the structural readjustments , we must primarily use market measures , and we must abide by the market 's rules of the game as recognized worldwide .
liu guoguang said , this round of structural readjustments in fact is an issue of resource allocation , and it includes the readjustment of the existing resource allocation - - stock readjustment , but it also includes the readjustment of the new investments - - readjustment of the incremental assets .
gearing to the market means making structural readjustments to suit the changing market demands , so that the resources are shifted from sectors with excess supply to sectors with shortages , and from the inefficient domains to the efficient domains .
the process of adjusting to the changes in market demand is a process of nurturing new economic growth points , such as housing , automobile , telecommunications , and tourism , to create new demand .
here we must properly handle two relationships : one , the relationship between developing high - and new - tech industries and transformation of the traditional industries ; two , the relationship between information orientation and industrial orientation .
china 's industrialization task is still incomplete ; we must work harder to achieve industrialization , and on the other hand , we must selectively and vigorously develop high - tech industries , led by the information industry , and use information to bring along industrialization .

beijing , 15 jan - - space experts said the unmanned spacecraft shenzhou ii has been operating normally since it was launched . according to information obtained so far , the re - entry cabin is orbiting according to design specifications and preset procedures and is expected to return to ground smoothly according to plan .
beginning from november 1975 , china has successfully retrieved 17 recoverable satellites and one unmanned spacecraft .
it was revealed that the capsule [ rong qi ] of the shenzhou ii 's re - entry module is the largest of all near - earth spacecraft in the world . the module will land at a key landing area in inner mongolia in due time .
the shenzhou ii spacecraft launched this time is china 's first proper unmanned spacecraft .
compared with the experimental spacecraft shenzhou i , the unmanned spacecraft shenzhou ii is equipped with a number of additional systems and functions , namely , the continuing orbiting function , the environment control system , and the emergency rescue system .
numerous subsystems on the spacecraft are part of the flight experiment in this mission , and basically all equipment related to the astronauts ' life support system are the actual equipment .
as for the transportation method , land transport was used in the previous spacecraft launch , whereas the shenzhou ii was air - lifted onto the jiuquan satellite launch center .
on 8 november 2000 , two large transport airplanes carried separate modules of the spacecraft shenzhou ii onto the launch site .
since the successful launch of the experimental spacecraft shenzhou in november 1999 , new technological upgrades and improvements conducted over the past year or so have passed state acceptance evaluations and have been formally incorporated in the current launch .
the current flight experiment is also the first time china made a space launch at low temperatures in the bitter winter .
in terms of payloads , this is the first time china conducts multi - discipline , multi - field , large - scale , and state - of - the - art space science and applied research on a spacecraft developed and launched by china itself .
approximately seven hours before the launch of the shenzhou ii , several scientists placed biological incubators into the re - entry module , which was loaded with 15 pieces of scientific experiment equipment .

shanghai , january 16 (xna) - - the work meeting on china 's implementation of the chemical weapons convention [ cwc ] was held in shanghai from january 15 to 16 .
li rongrong , vice minister in charge of the state economic and trade commission , spoke at the meeting .
he pointed out that in spite of the big retrenchment of organs and personnel and other difficulties , china still did an outstanding job in its implementation and its work was highly praised by the international community last year .
sha zukang , director general of the arms control and disarmament department of the ministry of foreign affairs , briefed the meeting on the situation of international disarmament , arms control and cwc implementation .
all relevant departments should assign still greater importance to the implementation of the convention from the high grounds of " stressing politics , " overcome difficulties , and ensure the stability and continuity of the ranks by rendering the necessary institutional and personnel support .
gu juesheng , executive deputy director of the national cwc implementation office , delivered a report in which he summed up the implementation of the convention in china 's civilian industries and mapped out plans for work this year .
it is a very timely exercise to call the national implementation meeting against the backdrop of the further deepening of the implementation , the streamlining of government institutions and the initial establishment of the socialist market economic system .
the participants agreed that they would definitely be able to make a success of implementation as long as they assign importance to the work in their thinking , persist in taking the convention as the yardstick , strive to overcome difficulties and do a good job at their respective posts .
the convention went into effect on 29 april 1997 and now has 141 signatories .
the organization for the prohibition of chemical weapons , an international organization monitoring the implementation of the cwc , was established in the hague in may 1997 .
china was a victim of chemical weapons , as the japanese were using chemical weapons in cold blood against chinese servicemen and civilians during the war of aggression against china .
the national cwc implementation office is now under the state economic and trade commission , but it was under the former ministry of chemical industry and later under the state petrochemical bureau before the chinese government reshuffles .
although the reform of government institutions has brought many temporary difficulties to the implementation , the leading group for cwc implementation remains in operation and the establishment and functions of the national cwc implementation office remain unchanged .
since 1997 , china has submitted civilian industrial applications and other declarations to the organization for the prohibition of chemical weapons , and has received over 30 international inspections .

us president - elect bush stated early this year that the chief aims of his military policy are military reforms and armament modernization . he also declared that he will work to build armed forces with still more superior armaments and greater combat strength geared to the 21 st century .
the us military has adopted some measures in light of this concept .
so far the united states has carried out three tests of nmd missile interception technology ; the first was successful and the other two failed .
however the director of the us missile defense agency has insisted that 93 percent of the key nmd functions and the all - round capability of the system have been verified .
this exercise further reflected the evolution of the nmd concept and the requirements of system integration and combat environment examination .
the department of defense has already decided to provide the boeing corporation with $ 6 billion as expenditure for research and development of the nmd system from january 2001 to september 2007 .
at the same time , it was also announced that another nmd development test will be held from the end of january to early february 2001 ; the specific test dates will be determined according to the weather conditions and possible technical issues .
at the same time , the united states is stepping up its new aircraft carrier (cvnx) development program .
four years have passed since the us navy launched its new - generation carrier (cvnx) program in 1996 , and this program is tending to become continually perfected in the course of comparing other schemes .
the new carrier also uses a computer aircraft launching system instead of the present widely used steam catapult ; the launch power of this system can reach 12,200 kilowatts , and it can launch planes of all types ( including pilotless and other light planes ) .
at the same time , the us navy 's pilotless combat planes will enter service simultaneously with the cvnx , and form an equipment pattern for the mixed force of planes aboard the new generation of carriers .
work may start on building cvnx-1 in 2006 , and it is expected to come into service in 2013 or 2014 .
work is expected to start on the next one , cvnx-2, in 2011 , and it will come into service in 2018 .
the development of these new carriers indicates that carrier strategy still plays a mainstay role in us national strategy , and the new carriers equipped with hi - tech armament will remain the main weapons in sea warfare in the 21 st century .
the us air force 's pilotless combat plane (ucav) seems ready to come out at the call .
two and a half years have passed since the us military started development of pilotless combat aircraft ; the latest x45-a pilotless combat plane was recently displayed at ( lambert ) airbase , st. louis .
it is a stealth plane with no elevators , 9 meters long , with a wingspan of 12 meters , and an all - up weight of 4,000 kg ; it can carry a payload of 150 kg .
since it is small , it does not require flyers or a training process , and it can be reused and stored for a long time , ucav saves 65 percent of the expenditure of a manned aircraft .
pilotless combat planes can complete various missions without the limitations set by the human body , such as approaching close to forward positions , carrying ground tracking sensors , synthetic aperture radar sensors , moving target indicators , and so on , or else doing on - the - spot monitoring of chemical and biological substances .
the plane will begin flight trials in spring 2001 , and simulated air defense neutralizing [ fang kong ya zhi ] tests will also begin this year . the plane will equip units in 2010 and will become the us air force 's main combat force after 2010 .
the emergence of the pilotless combat plane will further consolidate the us military 's dominant status in aerial warfare .

recently , as issues of the new century have become hot topics of discussion , people have become more concerned with the military developments in space .
the space command of the us armed forces [ usspacecom ] states in its " vision for 2020 " that the us armed forces ' " military operations depend greatly on their space capabilities . "
a former us army deputy chief of staff emphatically pointed out that " winning or losing a future war rests with the space strength of the different sides . "
it is stated in the military theory russia developed in 2000 that " space bases will be the centers around which future wars will be fought , " and " space supremacy will become one of the prerequisites for seizing air and naval supremacy . "
because electricity and petroleum were the lifeblood of the national economy and national defense of the industrial age in the 20 th century , this shows the strategic role played by space in the information age of the 21 st century .
creation of space troops space , the military " commanding height " and the " high - altitude frontier " of national security , is also one of the main sources of economic growth .
with respect to space forces , they have appeared because there is the need for a country to protect its economic interests , and also the need to support ground , naval and air operations .
so far , space forces are carrying out the missions of supporting responsive operations , and the antisatellite weapons that have appeared will eventually support the ground forces from space .
the united states and russia established their military space forces in the mid - eighties and early nineties . these forces are embryos of future space forces .
the us air force has even taken steps to form its " aerospace force . "
with respect to scientific research , the us air force has decided to shift the focus of its research to space .
during the 1999 - 2005 period , the us air force will allot more than 50 percent of its research budgets to the research of space - related technologies , and it will double the budgets for space development every year after 2005 .
according to the us air force 's estimates , within the next 10 years , it will spend $ 130 billion on developing new spacecraft and spend $ 22 billion on launching space vehicles .
for a very long time , the us armed forces have been intensifying their preparations for space offensives and defensives .
in fact , enormous amounts of money have been allotted for the development and testing of the national missile defense system and other antiballistic weapon systems .
it is estimated that these space operations aircraft for practical use will be commissioned to service in 2012 .
there are also plans that development of aerospace aircraft for practical use that can enter the orbit by one stage will begin in 2014 , and that the aircraft will be commissioned for service around 2025 .
according to reports , russia , in addition to taking active and passive defensive measures in developing its satellite systems , is also developing its antisatellite weapons on the basis of the operational antisatellite satellites , which the former soviet union developed , and on the basis of testing the land - based antisatellite laser weapons .
russia , because of its world leadership in terms of its powerful laser and high - powered microwave technologies , has already had a good foundation for developing weapons for space wars .
just as what the us armed forces have concluded following their studies : " in the next 20 to 30 years , other countries are not likely to be able to counter the united states in terms of conventional forces , but they can inflict enormous losses to the united states ' aerospace systems . "
development of space weapons picking up speed the types of space weapons being developed or conceived include antisatellite weapons and upper - atmosphere antiballistic missile weapons , as well as space war platforms , aerospace aircraft , and aircraft for space operations .
such weapons , known as " space killers , " can attack the spacecraft operating in orbits by totally destroying them or crippling part or all their functions temporarily or permanently .
there are all types of antisatellite weapons .
generally speaking , the strengths of antisatellite weapons are : ( 1 ) their deployment is flexible .
these antisatellite weapons are respectively called land - based ( based on land and ships ) antisatellite weapons , aircraft - carried antisatellite weapons , and space - based antisatellite weapons .
modern antisatellite weapons can destroy enemy satellites by colliding directly with them , or by destroying them with directional energies , such as laser , microwave , or particle beams ; and even with nonlethal destructive measures , such as spraying chemicals on them .
currently , space systems have increasingly become systems in which countries ' key interests lie .
if an antisatellite weapon destroys a space system in a future war , the destruction will have dealt a heavy blow to the side that owns and uses the space system , stripped its space supremacy , and weakened its supremacy in conducting information warfare and even its supremacy in the war at large .
antisatellite weapons that can be developed at low cost and that can strike at the enemy 's enormously expensive yet vulnerable space system will become an important option for the majority of medium - size and small countries with fragile space technology to deter their powerful enemies and protect themselves .
today , both the united states and russia have the capabilities of developing antisatellite weapons to be used in real operations .
from now on they will focus their attention on developing precision control technology , tracking and targeting technology , and miniaturization technology needed for further improving the capabilities of their antisatellite weapons .
as result of development of technologies , space - based antiballistic missile weapons will also be gradually maturing for practical use , and will play a significant role in defense .
owing to the rotation of the earth and space - based antiballistic missile weapons ' round - the - earth movements , they can , through choosing appropriate orbits and properly deploying the interceptors , shorten the interceptors ' operational distance in launching global interceptions .
during the boost phase , a ballistic missile 's velocity is low , its storage tanks are bulky and structurally fragile , and is susceptible to being destroyed .
and since it has yet to project its warheads or decoys , that phase provides the best opportunity to destroy it . interception during the missile 's boost phase also means that the usable time and space for the interception can be fully utilized , thereby creating the conditions for multiple interceptions .
because directional - energy weapons are limited by their beams ' straight transmission and by the earth 's curve , and because of kinetic - energy weapons are limited by their velocity , the interceptor must be deployed on a low earth orbit in order to intercept an icbm while it is at the boost phase .
( 3 ) the virtually vacuum space is advantageous for improving an interceptor 's capabilities , such as reducing the attenuation of laser energy in the atmosphere .
space - based antiballistic missile weapons , however , have the shortcoming that they need enormously amounts of resources to build .
it is a vehicle that functions as an aircraft , a carrier , and a space vehicle . being capable of flying with hypersonic speed in the atmosphere and operating in the orbit , it is one of the key weapons to be employed for controlling space and vying for space supremacy in the 21 st century .
( 2 ) they can be used as space platforms for weapon launching .
in future space wars , aerospace aircraft can be used as platforms for launching all types of weapons and ammunitions - - including kinetic - energy weapons , high - energy laser weapons , and microwave weapons - - to attack the enemy 's important ground , sea , air , and space targets .
( 4 ) they can be used as high - speed transport airplanes .
an aerospace aircraft flies at high speed . taking off from an ordinary airport , it can reach any place on earth within an hour , and so it can respond quickly to any regional conflict in the world or launch a sudden attack against the enemy .
an aerospace aircraft , like a manned space station , can stay in space for a long time . and since it is equipped with advanced commanding systems , it can directly undertake the mission of commanding operations when necessary during wartime .
( 6 ) they can reconnoiter , monitor , and issue early warnings .
its mobility in the orbit is extensive . it can stay in the orbit for weeks , months , and even a year ; and can be summoned back to earth any time . it has strong tactical application capabilities .

on the surface , tax reduction seems to be able to increase funds in the hands of nationals so as to stimulate economic development .
however , in fact , it might not necessarily effectively increase demands because if the grand economic environment is worrying , people would not easily place money in their hands on investment and high consumption .
over the last 50 years , several republican presidents of the united states often advocated the theory of keynesism , namely increasing demands in a timely manner through tax reduction or consumption stimulation can prevent or relieve recession .
nevertheless , the precondition for this prescription is that it must be dispensed at the right time .
according to the analyses of economists , tax reduction is a kind of emergency measure and only suitable for those situations which are similar to the big economic depression in the 20 th century in the united states and the continuous economic recession in the 90 s of the 20 th century in japan .
and the question at present is whether such an opportunity has already arisen in the united states .
some officials of the us federal reserve system and observers believe that the key factor for greenspan suddenly cutting down the interest rates is that he is worried about the tax reduction plan of mr. bush .
in fact , this move is reminding bush and his economic decision - making body that interest rates readjustment can play a role in supporting economy and that they do not have to rely on tax reduction .
in fact , just as many people from the academic circles , greenspan also does not favor tax reduction .
it was the same viewpoint with which greenspan strongly advised the newly - elected president clinton not to do eight years ago .
at that time , clinton favored vigorously implementing financial means to stimulate economic development .
but eventually , he was convinced by greenspan and other people . at that time , greenspan pointed out that tightening control of finance is favorable to long - term development , which can provide a guarantee for the implementation of low interest rates .
but people still find it difficult to conclude whether his economic policy can maintain the trend of good development in us economy .
some people have predicted , greenspan will become the " economic president " of the united states in the next few years .
however , during this period of time before he takes up his office , the circles of public opinion have raised questions about some moves of bush and his aids .
the clinton administration has always been very careful to avoid inputting political factors into the decision - making of greenspan . in fact , clinton never comments on the moves of the us federal reserve system .
nevertheless , after bush taking up his office , this situation might change .
judged by the figures published by the us department of labor , both the new bush administration and the us federal reserve system feel somewhat relieved .
from a different perspective , it indicates that the saying about an economic recession breaking out in the united states should subside at the moment .

the general tariff level was reduced from 1 january , from 16.4 percent at the end of last year to 15.3 percent , representing an average drop of 6.6 percent .
this is china 's eighth reduction in nontariff measures since 1992 and is an important content of self - determined opening up .
the chinese government has made positive efforts to reduce tariffs in recent years to meet the needs of developing china 's foreign trade and also in order to merge faster into the tide of world economy .
on 1 april 1996 china announced the lowering of import tariffs on 4,971 items , thereby reducing china 's average tariff level from 35 percent to 23 percent .
the average tariff level in 1997 was reduced from 23 percent to 17 percent .
at the same time , high tariffs are prone to cause certain people to sabotage normal foreign trade order by making reckless moves and smuggling and peddling contraband .
as far as china is concerned , this first of all involves the question of tariffs .
given , however , that china is reducing the tariff level and changing from nontariff barriers to tariffs , china still attaches importance to giving play to the proper role of tariffs in protecting domestic industries .
second , china needs to make big efforts to take stock of , straighten out , and cut favored treatment policy measures for reducing or waiving tariffs .
although we have carried out major stocktaking and readjustments several times in recent years , there is still too much , too extensive , and too indiscriminate favored treatment in tariff reduction or waivers .
finally , china needs to establish and perfect an antidumping and antisubsidy tariff system .
the commodities relatively greatly affected by this downward readjustment are mechanical and electrical products and certain industrial production materials ; the reduction of the tariff on these items will have a very great impact on the returns of the processing trade , which accounts for a large proportion of china 's foreign trade .
and the main pressure on domestic industries resulting from the drop in tariff level on imported goods will fall mainly on advanced [ shang you ] industries producing these goods , but the general impact will not be great .

between 16 and 17 january , the general office of the state council held a national work conference on reforming the system for pharmaceutical supervision and management .
this phenomenon was attributed to following factors : first , there were too many pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprises ; medical drugs were produced excessively in a disorderly way ; the vicious business competition gave rise to a large quantity of counterfeit and inferior pharmaceuticals .
being driven by the attempt to seek staggering profits , some lawless people acted unscrupulously to build pharmaceutical plants in various names and produce pharmaceuticals without passing through required procedures and obtaining medical certification , and they produced a large quantity of counterfeit brand - name drugs and other counterfeit and inferior pharmaceuticals .
second , there was a disorderly environment in the pharmaceutical market . there are too many enterprises involved in distributing and dealing in medical drugs , and this provides an opportunity and a channel for counterfeit and inferior pharmacies to access the market .
over a certain period , the layout of pharmaceutical wholesale and retail enterprises was improper . many business were engaged in selling medical drugs without licenses and certifications , or those holding one license used it to do business in many fields .
third , under the new historical conditions , the existing system for pharmaceutical supervision and management was no longer suited to the objective needs under the new situation and could hardly exercise effective supervision and management over the pharmaceutical market .
at and below the provincial level , such problems as the lack of coordination among institutions for pharmaceutical supervision and management , the mixing of administrative functions of a governmental institution with the business operation of an enterprise , and the effects of local protectionism all seriously affected the fairness and authoritativeness of the supervisory work .
therefore , it is absolutely necessary to advance the reform of the system for pharmaceutical supervision and management .
the meeting stressed : at present , pharmaceutical supervision and management departments at all levels in all localities should seriously and effectively implement the " program for reforming pharmaceutical supervision and management system " approved and relayed by the state council and should take this as a major task .
at a press conference for chinese and foreign reporters , which was sponsored by the information office of the state council , dai xianglong said : the people 's bank of china conscientiously implemented the prudent monetary policy last year , and the objectives of macro financial control were smoothly achieved .
by the end of last year , the ratio of money flow ( m1 / m2 ) was 39.5 percent , the highest since 1997 . this showed the gradual increase of money flow .
the excess - reserve rate of financial institutions was 8.3 percent , showing their adequate paying ability .
the loans granted by the financial institutions totaled 9.9 trillion yuan , increasing 13.4 percent over the previous year .
last year , the inter - bank lending and repo transactions amounted to 2.32 trillion yuan , up 22 percent from the previous year .
dai xianglong said : it is necessary to continuously maintain an appropriate growth of money supply .
we should concentrate on improving the mechanism for the operation of the open market , standardize the interbank bond market , expand the variety and scope of bond trade , and increase trade instruments in the market .
dai xianglong stressed : the people 's bank of china should strengthen its supervision over credit and prevent any possible risks .
we should quickly improve the bank credit registration and consulting system and experiment on instituting a system for personal credit rating .
dai xianglong said : the people 's bank of china should lay stress on financial supervision this year in order to create favorable conditions for effectively carrying out the monetary policy .
it should exercise strict supervision over commercial banks ' ratios of non - performing loans , rates of returns on capital , and abundance of capital and evaluate them strictly .
the banks should support the development of small and medium commercial banks and urban and rural credit cooperatives in the course of reform .
now it is still very difficult to determine interest rates completely according to conditions in the market , and the central bank still has to set the levels of interest rates for bank deposits and loans .
