beijing , 25 mar ( xinhua ) - - finance minister xiang huaicheng delivered a speech at the " high - level forum on china 's development " this morning . his speech focused on how china can promote sustained and stable economic development by using financial policy .
xiang huaicheng said : judging from china 's overall economic strength and growth trend , it can bear its debts at the current level .
a series of financial policies and measures has effectively promoted the basic balance between the total social demand and total social supply , the balance of international revenue and expenditure , and stabilized economic growth .
since last year , the chinese government has improved the method of drawing up the budget for paying the interests of treasury bonds . such interests are included in the budget for current expenditures .
in this way , we can effectively prevent the debt risk . xiang huaicheng also stressed that the implementation of the proactive financial policy will not lead to inflation .
he said : at present , china witnesses a fairly large increase in residents ' saving deposits .
by the end of 2000 , the amount of saving deposits of urban and rural residents reached 6.43 trillion yuan . the amount of various deposits in all financial institutions was 12.38 trillion yuan and the amount of various loans was 9.94 trillion yuan , with a deposit - loan gap of 2.44 trillion yuan .
therefore , turning a part of deposits into the government 's investment in infrastructure facilities by issuing more bonds will not increase monetary issue . the approach will also stimulate commercial banks and non - government sectors to make more investment .
at present , china witnesses stable economic growth , ample supply of grain and other farm products , as well as industrial consumer goods and capital goods .
spokesman of the china securities regulatory commission said on 25 march : the commission has preliminarily decided on the first trial unit for open - end fund . other companies that have completed self - examination and rectification and reform are paying close attention to relevant preparation work .
at this important moment , china will speed up the pace of reform of the banking system and capital markets .
dai xianglong said : after more than 10 years of effort , reform of china 's financial system has shown clear results , and a financial system that is commensurate with a socialist market economy has taken initial shape .
a securities market , consisting primarily of government bonds , financial bonds , corporate bonds , and stock markets , is developing rapidly .
fourth , a new system for implementing industry - specific operations and management in the banking , securities , and insurance industries has been established .
in order to reach this goal , beginning this year , in accordance with the requirements for establishing a modern enterprise system , we must undertake comprehensive reforms in stages of the wholly state - owned commercial banks .
at the same time , joint - stock commercial banks must continue to be standardized and developed .
we must speed up the pace of reform of the rural financial system , greatly expand agricultural loans , and support efforts to increase farmers ' income .
during the 10 th five - year plan , we must continue to develop the stock markets .
we must further promote the marketization of the mechanisms for issuing stocks . as of the end of 2000 , 2.1 trillion yuan worth of treasury bills and financial bonds had been issued .
at the same time , we must increase the issuance of corporate bonds in a step - by - step fashion .
we must further expand the scope of investment for foreign businessmen and study methods for managing purchases of the bad assets of financial assets management companies by domestic and foreign investors .
wu bangguo stressed : in the period of the tenth five - year plan , the strategic adjustment of the economic structure will be focused on the adjustment and upgrading of the industrial structure .
it is necessary to adopt various measures to quicken the pace of industrial restructuring and strive to enhance the overall quality and international competitive power of the industry in our country .
according to the actual conditions of each area , such high and new technology industries related to information technology , biological engineering , and new materials should be selectively developed ; breakthroughs and developments to a higher level should be made in certain fields .
through the forms of going public , merger , and reorganization , in major industries , develop a batch of large companies and enterprise groups which possess their own intellectual property rights and produce brand - name goods .
fifth , it is necessary to improve the market withdrawal mechanism , actively dredge and gradually regularize the channel for making enterprises operating in unfavorable conditions withdraw from the market .
wu bangguo pointed out : under the correct leadership of the party central committee , with the joint effort of the whole nation from top to bottom , the objective of freeing state - owned enterprises from business predicaments in a period of three years has been basically achieved .
however , this was just the result in a certain stage , and the foundation is still not solid enough . it will still be a long way to go in reforming and developing state - owned enterprises .
the effective traditional management methods should be combined with the use of the modern information technology , thus promoting the innovations of the enterprise management system as a whole .
input to technological transformation should be increased so that the technology and equipment of the enterprises can be really improved and upgraded .
good preparations should be made for entering the world trade organization , and the work in all fields in the transitional period must be done well .
the enterprises ' ability to withstand business risks and participate in international competition must be continuously enhanced .
wu bangguo pointed out : it is necessary to continue to make unswerving effort to effect the " two guarantees " according the requirements and objectives laid down by the central leadership .
leaders at all levels should show special concern for the livelihood of the laid - off workers and the retired workers who may encounter financial difficulties , and should adopt serious measures to help them overcome difficulties in their daily lives .
punishments meted out to those violate the regulations and rules for industrial safety should be combined with positive education .
beijing , 25 mar ( xinhua ) - - at the " china development high - level forum , " which opens today , yang jingyu , director of the state council office of legislative affairs , gave a special report , entitled " accession to wto and chinese government 's legal system building . "
yang stressed that china 's accession to the wto will have a profound impact on china 's economic and even political and social life and that the existing administrative and management concepts , systems , structures , methods , and means need to be transformed in an in - depth manner .
yang pointed out : with the deepening of the reform , the expansion of the opening up , and the establishment and development of a socialist market economic structure , china 's administrative and management structures have been reformed accordingly and marked results have been scored .
emphasis should be laid on carrying out well the following three points : first , it is necessary to change government functions and separate them from those of enterprises .
institutions and personnel should be streamlined .
all government organs , no matter which , should handle official business in the pay of the government , all the tax and charges collected according to the law should be brought under financial management , and power should never be linked with money .
the government structural reform is actually a reform of the administrative and management systems with the change of government functions as the key content . it is a revolution of the superstructure .
since it is a revolution , it will inevitably involve adjustments in the relation of different interest groups , as well as the vested interests of certain interest groups , and it is hard to avoid obstructions .

beijing , 25 mar - - president jiang zemin met washington post executive chief editor steve kohl and his entourage in zhongnanhai on 23 march .
as economic globalization is speeding up , countries compete with one another in the fields of economy , science , technology , trade , and human resources . this is a characteristic of world development . there is competition between china and the united states as well .
nevertheless , we also cooperate with each other in many important fields , and i believe that such cooperation enjoys a broad prospect .
in short , a healthy and stable cooperative relationship between china and the united states is in the interest of peace and development in the asia - pacific region and the world as a whole .
but china remains a developing country with a large population , a weak foundation , and a low development level .
to devote ourselves to economic development and improve our people 's lives will always be the central task of china 's construction .
the chinese nation has always been a peace - loving nation .
we have long declared to the world in unequivocal terms that china does not seek hegemony and will never do so even if it becomes developed in the future . this has been appreciated by the people throughout the world .
many countries and nations in the world have differences and contradictions between them on this or that issue .
what is essential is that we should put these differences and contradictions in the right perspective and handle them properly so as to prevent them from hindering the normal development of state - to - state relations and from affecting regional and world stability and development .
taiwan has been part of china 's territory since ancient times .
the us side has on many occasions explicitly stated that it supports the one - china policy and abides by the three joint communiques and its commitments .
as you know , the united states sent its seventh fleet to the taiwan strait in the 1950 s and the us government always sheltered the taiwan authorities for more than 20 years thereafter .
after the establishment of diplomatic relations between china and the united states , the us congress passed the taiwan relations act in disregard of the opposition of the chinese people .
it has recognized the one - china principle and made commitments to the government and people of china . but at the same time , it has sold large quantities of advanced weapons to taiwan . this has in effect abetted the separatist activities for " taiwan independence . "
regarding how to resolve the taiwan issue , we have long put forward the principle of " peaceful reunification and one country , two systems . "
it is our consistent proposition that the taiwan issue should be resolved peacefully through negotiations on an equal footing on the basis of the one - china principle .
we will spare no effort to achieve peaceful reunification . we have full confidence and capabilities to resolutely stop any activities for " taiwan independence " and safeguard china 's state sovereignty and territorial integrity .
in answering the question on the reform of the political system in china and other issues , which an american correspondent was interested in , president jiang pointed out that to develop the socialist democracy system and political system is an important objective of china 's modernization drive .
our political system also needs to be continuously improved in the course of practice .
we have put forward developing a socialist democracy and political system , governing the country according to law , and building a socialist country under the rule of law . this is an important move to strengthen and improve our political system .

indirect cross - strait trade amounted to $ 30.5 billion last year , 31.1 percent higher than the previous year .
in the first two months of this year , taiwan businessmen invested $ 440 million on the mainland , a 21 percent increase over the same period last year .
without such surpluses , taiwan 's international balance of payments would have severely deteriorated and taiwan would not have more than $ 100 billion of foreign reserves .
most of these surpluses were the result of taiwan businessmen on the mainland buying all kinds of raw materials and parts from the island . the contribution to taiwan 's economy made by taiwan businessmen investing in the mainland cannot be denied .
although the taiwan authorities have set all sorts of obstacles , they still fail to stop taiwan businessmen from " boldly entering western china . " taiwan 's high - tech industry also follows close on the heels of traditional industries in going to the motherland to invest .

article two these " regulations " shall apply to the armed forces ' war and operational theory research , national defense and army building theory research , and other relevant military theory research activities ( hereinafter referred to as military scientific research for short ) .
( 4 ) practicing academic democracy ; letting different schools of academic thought contend ; enlivening academic thinking ; and building a democratic and harmonious research atmosphere in which knowledge and qualified personnel are respected .
( 5 ) observing political or organizational disciplines ; strictly abiding by a secrecy system ; and safeguarding national military interests .
a five - year plan is mainly formulated for the sake of planning or arranging for research on major realistic issues or basic theories in accordance with an army building and development program for a specific period and in light of actual needs .
a five - year plan shall normally be formulated by a unit at or above the military region level .
an annual plan is mainly formulated for the sake of planning or arranging for research set to be completed in a particular year as stipulated by a five - year plan , and in light of actual needs as well .
an annual plan shall normally be formulated by a unit at the military region level or by a unit , an academy , or a school at or below the army level .
a specialized plan shall normally be formulated by individual units in light of actual needs .
a military scientific research plan shall spell out clear - cut tasks ; identify key aspects ; ensure unified planning with due consideration for all issues concerned ; and be practical and feasible as well .
a military scientific research plan for an individual unit shall normally be examined and approved by a work meeting held by the commander 's office of the unit concerned .
chapter four managing research topics article 16 a research topic listed in different military scientific research plans shall be managed by different levels .
the leader of a topic group shall be a person with an academic background and with the ability to organize or lead such work , and the person 's background and ability shall correspond to the work of studying a specific research topic .
the leader of a topic group shall be appointed by a unit assigned with a research task , and the unit shall report the leader 's appointment for the record to a military scientific research management department in charge of the relevant research topic .
leaders and military scientific research management departments at all levels shall create conditions for the leader of a topic group to perform his or her duties and for a topic group to conduct research work as well .
article 18 the work of studying a research topic listed in a military scientific research plan shall be subject to an examination system .
a research topic listed in a military scientific research plan for the whole army shall be examined by the academy of military sciences .
a research topic listed in a military scientific research plan for an individual unit shall be examined by a military scientific research management department of the unit concerned .
in examining a research topic , the authorities concerned shall normally also examine the situation of the personnel studying a research topic , the progress of the work of studying a research topic , the use of funds earmarked for studying a research topic , the experiences of or problems in studying a research topic , and other issues .
the work of examining a research topic may be conducted in the form of general examination or sample examination .
article 19 a research topic listed in a military scientific research plan shall be finalized within a specified period of time .
the military scientific research management department at a higher level shall directly organize personnel to appraise , test , or accept the research results for a major topic and may authorize or entrust other departments to appraise , test , and accept the research results for other topics .
if a topic is found to be an unsuitable one after being appraised and tested , the leader of the relevant topic group may organize personnel to revise the topic within a specified period of time before applying for the topic to be appraised , tested , or accepted again .
article 22 personnel who have played a key role in achieving military scientific research results may apply for the relevant research results to be appraised or rewarded in accordance with the regulations .
all general departments may also introduce other rewards for research results and may organize personnel to appraise or reward military scientific research results scored under their leadership .
military scientific research results shall be appraised or rewarded in accordance with the relevant procedures and with the principle of being open , fair , and just ; seeking truth from facts ; upholding democratic centralism ; stressing quality ; and encouraging new ideas .
article 23 leaders and military scientific research management departments at all levels shall safeguard military scientific research personnel 's legitimate rights and interests relating to research results and protect intellectual property rights as well .
military scientific research personnel shall abide by " the prc copyright law " and other regulations laid down by the state or the army as well .
the military scientific research results deemed confidential or of a higher secrecy grade shall be managed by specialized personnel under a strict secrecy system in order to prevent the loss or leakage of a secret .
when needed , a unit at a higher level may also handle the research work and ensure coordination in this regard .
while carrying out research through coordination with one other , the relevant units shall abide by the principle of optimizing organization and bringing into full play one another 's strong points .
article 26 military scientific research management departments shall actively organize activities of academic exchanges by laying down clear - cut goals and ensuring sufficient preparations and shall meticulously organize the relevant activities with stress on actual results .
activities of academic exchanges may be conducted in the form of a symposium , a report meeting , a forum , a pen meeting , an exhibition of research results , and so on .
article 27 the units or personnel involved in a military scientific research project shall submit an application for examination and approval in accordance with the regulations before starting research in cooperation with a foreign party or conducting academic exchanges with a foreign party .
after receiving official approval , the units or personnel concerned shall strictly abide by the relevant state or army regulations ; observe disciplines governing foreign affairs ; and safeguard the state 's or the army 's interests while conducting research in cooperation with a foreign party or conducting academic exchanges with a foreign party .
article 29 all military academic journals published with official approval shall set great store by bringing forth new theories ; enliven academic thinking ; display unique characteristics as a journal ; and create conditions for academic exchanges or for different schools of academic thought to contend .
the units in charge of or sponsoring a military academic journal shall strengthen leadership or management of the journal ; adhere to a correct goal in running the journal ; strictly abide by the state or army policies or decrees on publishing work ; and work hard to raise the journal 's quality .
individual units shall support research on a topic listed in their own military scientific research plans by allocating funds from their funds earmarked for developing undertakings .
general equipment for military scientific research shall be developed , distributed , used , and managed together with the office equipment in a unified way .
information exchanges or data support for military scientific research shall be governed by the secrecy regulations .
article 34 the units , academies , or schools involved in military scientific research shall introduce a system for training qualified personnel for military scientific research .
article 41 the armed forces shall manage social science programs or funds assigned by the state in light of this " regulations . "

after questioning by the concerned public security organization , jin ruchao confessed all his crimes and the course of setting off explosions .
where did jin ruchao obtain dynamite ?
jin ruchao confessed that on 9 march he killed wei zhihua whom he had cohabited for three months in yunnan 's maguan county and returned to hebei province .
according to his confession , as early as may or june in 2000 , he had contacted wang yushun on the procurement of dynamite and learned how to use detonators and blasting fuses to start explosions . he also created a test explosion by using a small amount of dynamite and detonators provided by wang yushun .
based on jin ruchao 's demand , wang yushun manufactured a large quantity of nitro - amine compound explosives and put the explosives in more than 10 yellow knitted bags with the words " chicken feed " printed on those bags .
at about 0900 on 14 march , jin ruchao again went to wang yushun 's place , paid the latter 950 yuan and temporarily stored the explosives at wang 's storehouse .
jin ruchao also confessed that he purchased detonators and blasting fuses from a civilian worker of a quarry in luquan city last year and he hid them under a pipe at a suburban plant in shijiazhuang city .
after returning to shijiazhuang from yunnan , jin ruchao went to that place to pick up the detonators and blasting fuses .
it was learned that the police have already arrested wang yushun who provided explosives for jin ruchao .
because jin ruchao did not pay the driver enough transportation fee , the driver stopped the car near a water gate at shuanghe village and dumped the bags out on the ground .
the time was around 0430 .
the concerned public security organization is stepping up the interrogation of suspect jin ruchao and further gathering proof in order to hand over the case to the procuratorial organization at an earlier date .

the united states now wants to turn the national missile defense (nmd) and theater missile defense (tmd) that it advocates into a " net of heaven " covering the united states and its security in the asia - pacific region .

one pole can hardly " make up for " many poles the greatest change in us foreign policy after the cold war is that it has developed from maintaining a balance of power to pursuing absolute superiority .
this strategy of pursuing one pole was expressed as : a fundamental decision in us foreign policy was to make a choice between the policies of falling into and getting out of cold war .
the clinton administration 's idea of a unipolar world has been inherited by the new us administration team .
as ms. rice , the new national security adviser , has put it , the first us administration of the 21 st century will pursue a policy of " national defense strength in coordination with powerful diplomacy " in handling relations with the rest of the world .
considering things in detail , however , the us unipolar strategy is not without loopholes .
this was because the great powers agreed on certain core issues in international relations and could preserve world stability . this is a profound explanation that accords with the development of history .
in fact , the united states itself does not necessarily believe in the myth of a unipolar world .
for instance , during the clinton administration , even secretary of state albright , who was an active advocate of nato 's eastward expansion , could not but acknowledge in many of her speeches that the united states could not dominate the world for ever .
it can be said that the us " loopholes " essentially lie in the contradiction between american greed and the practical limitations , and this is something that no missile defense system can make up for .
in a multipolar world characterized by competition and conflict , us foreign policy should not pursue one pole .
if the united states wants russia and china to control the development of their strategic forces , it should encourage cooperation and establish coordination instead of using the " domineering " method of nmd .
many loopholes in the asia - pacific region the united states not only stations 100,000 troops in the asia - pacific region but also has bilateral military relations with the rok , singapore , the philippines , thailand , and australia , while also maintaining " quasi - military ties " with china 's taiwan .
japan formally joined in tmd research and development on september 1998 .
tmd will readjust us defense strategy to the level of dealing with one and a half regional conflicts .
according to japanese research data , statistics from the us combined chiefs of staff headquarters show that before the cold war the united states urgently sent troops overseas on 10 occasions , but after the cold war this increased to 33 times .
second , economic globalization has revealed loopholes in the us asia - pacific security structure .
since the asian financial crisis , china 's influence has extended to southeast asia .
at present asean has reached a consensus that peace in the asia - pacific region depends on the triangular relationship of the united states , japan , and china .
an example of this is that , after the new us - japanese defense guidelines were made public , the nine asean members demanded that the japanese government clarify the geographical scope of its defense cooperation .

finally , this article will suggest three types of underlying difficulties and contradictions faced by china on its road to democratic politics with the characteristics of its own nation .
this process is eventually fulfilled by political parties that represent various interest groups .
but these conditions will only emerge when a market economy has developed to a considerable extent .
to be more specific , the political party that represents majority votes in society , dominated by the public opinion represented by these votes , has to pursue policies that accord with this kind of public opinion , which represents the mainstream opinion of society .
every policy pursued by the cabinet formed by the political party reflects the opinion of the congress majority , whereas the congress majority reflects the opinion of majority voters in society .
various social interest groups and their political representatives cannot but standardize their own conduct in accordance with the political rules of the game sanctioned by usage , and resolve disputes between each other in a programmed way .
' quasi - multiparty system ' in modern china in modern times , as far as the understanding of multiparty politics is concerned , chinese people have a special perspective that is different from that of the west .
oftentimes , chinese people , when examining pluralistic democracy of the west , unconsciously overlook the social substructure of the multiparty system in western politics , and try to understand the positive significance of this system by merely proceeding from the political function and efficacy of western multiparty politics in terms of interests expression .
this way of thinking was reflected in both instances .
we may call this way of thinking as " system determinism . "
however , for a causal relationship between this kind of western system and the desired outcome to be established , there must be a foundation laid by a string of social supporting conditions , without which multiparty politics will not be able to create what people desire .
the practice of " multiparty politics " in the early roc years led to serious disorderly party struggles .
faction - like political parties which widely existed did not have any organic link to the social system , neither were they influenced or checked by the social system .
as pointed out by liang qichao long ago , multiparty politics in the early roc years neither has any communication with the social forces nor represented social interests and classes .
due to historical , psychological , and other reasons such as usual practice , no effort was made to act according to the forceful procedural rules systematized by the west .
what is " quasi - multiparty system ? " what i call a quasi - multiparty system is a kind of virtual democratic system that does not have a procedural consensus , cannot work effectively , lacks stability and efficacy .
this kind of multiparty system only has the exterior form of western multiparty system , but since it does not possess the economic , social , political , and cultural conditions for western multiparty politics , so the society cannot be effectively integrated in the way western multiparty politics does .
from a political - sociological point of view , the failure of faction - like party politics in the early roc years was virtually caused by the inability to bring about integration of the system of " quasi - multiparty politics " with the then social system .
in the twenties of this century [ as published ] , two new modes of political party began to emerge in china .
one was the kuomintang 's statism and authoritarian party politics .
the other was the cpc 's revolution - and mobilization - oriented party politics .
since " 4 june , " china has virtually formed a kind of authoritarian mode of modernization and development .
however , such problems as social inequality , bureaucracy , and social corruption also exist in the authoritarian mode of modernization .
under such circumstances , the multiparty system has once again been proposed by some nongovernmental figures as a political option for overcoming bureaucratic corruption and bringing about a fuller degree of interests expression .
china nowadays is no longer an all - embracing socialist system in its original sense .
whereas under a post - omnipotent system , china , through the establishment of market economy , has gradually made room in the non - political sphere for a society acting on its own accord .
if this social system and its organizations develop further , a civil society that has chinese characteristics , that is rising , healthy , and full of energy will come into being .
here , what is meant by a civil society is a self - organized setup beyond state control and outside the system .
second , the basic symbol system of socialism remains intact in the ideological sphere , but the symbol content of its ideology no longer has the original goal consciousness for equalitarian communism .
to analyze from a political - sociological point of view , this kind of historical transition from an all - embracing society to a post - omnipotent society is undoubtedly of vital substantive significance to china 's political modernization and future democratization .
in china nowadays , the new type of contractual inter - personal relationship in daily life , the compromise mechanism embodied through bargaining , and the corresponding legal system concept and new type of lenient political culture are precisely things nurtured through the practice of market economy .
ideological division breeds future democracy in the social and ideological spheres , people can also find that in china nowadays , there are certain new traits unforeseen in the days prior to reform and opening up .
as a matter of fact , ideological division among the intellectuals and the division of social strata are two different areas , but between them , there are , intentionally or not , important relevance and similarities .
these diverse thoughts are undoubtedly favorable to the selection of a rational orientation for china 's modernization if they compete with each other on an equal footing under certain rules of the game .
from a long - term perspective , ideological pluralism and diversification of interest groups under market economic conditions echo go hand in hand and complement each other , and they exactly offer the necessary conditions and a real foundation for the establishment of democratic politics with the chinese nation 's characteristics in the 21 st century .
to be more specific , pluralistic check and balance , which is essential to political democracy , will be out of the question if there is only division of strata and of interests in a society , but there is neither corresponding ideological division nor any interest group that corresponds to the ideological division .
people should attach full importance to the vital significance of the phenomenon of ideological pluralism in the nineties to future democracy .

the central economic work commission clearly pointed out : " adhering to the expansion of domestic demand is a long - term strategic policy for china 's economic development .
adhering to the policy of expanding domestic demand actually means adhering to the important thinking that development is the last word ; it means taking development as the main theme . "
how , then , should we understand the proposition that adhering to the expansion of domestic demand is adhering to " development as the last word " ?
expansion of domestic demand can promote economic growth .
therefore , speeding up infrastructure construction to expand investment demand is an important aspect of promoting economic development . stimulating demand in personal consumption is an even more important aspect of promoting economic development .
due to the fact that the international economic situation took a turn for the better in 2000 , china 's total imports and exports registered fairly large growth .
accordingly , some people believe that expanding domestic demand is no longer as important as it was during the past few years .
when we speak of import and export trade , there is always the issue of balance .
as a large developing country , china has a fairly large potential market capacity .
if , over the next two decades , china 's per capita gdp rises from the current $ 800 - plus to $ 4,000 , then it could be said that this is a vast market .
expansion of domestic demand can promote industrial upgrading .
under normal circumstances , when real personal income soars to the $ 800 mark , consumption demand in society will enter a stage of rapid structural change .
expansion of domestic demand can promote the improvement of people 's standard of living .
fundamentally speaking , the purpose of development is to satisfy people 's ever - increasing material and cultural needs to the greatest extent possible , and to increase china 's comprehensive national strength as much as possible .
we can observe from the above that adhering to the expansion of domestic demand is adhering to the thinking that " development is the last word . "
to be sure , expansion of domestic demand and expansion of exports are interconnected and mutually reinforcing ; they are not mutually exclusive .
in adhering to development as the last word , we must not only adhere to the expansion of domestic demand , we must also actively expand exports .

our willingness to recruit more capable personnel shows we have a sense of respecting capable personnel , but this is not enough . we must establish a sense of correctly using personnel so that the capable personnel recruited are needed for the work of our respective units .
how can we ensure capable personnel recruited can meet the needs of respective units ?
only by putting these high - level capable personnel in authoritative positions will they think they are fully trusted , will they have a very strong sense of responsibility , and will they properly fulfill their tasks together with others .
when he was studying the issue of human needs as early as in 1844 , marx already pointed out that human needs can roughly be put under for aspects , that is , material needs , spiritual needs , needs for contact and needs for labor .
this is also true of high - level capable personnel , who belong to the high - level intellectual community . besides , their needs may even be more special than those of ordinary people and have a higher standard .
recently , the four general departments issued a notice on increasing the remuneration for some high - level experts . each fellow is given 2,000 yuan a month as subsidy and a car is provided for each of the professional and technological cadres at and above the third grade , and so on .
all these should be given to high - level capable personnel to meet the needs of their work and life .
they have given up liberal remuneration offered aboard and resolutely returned to serve their country . with regard to these very patriotic capable personnel , we should also try our best to meet their reasonable needs .
if a unit or a leading cadre really respects knowledge and capable personnel , it should ensure and show greatest concern for the needs in livelihood of intellectuals while providing ample scope for them to display their abilities and talents .
in view of such a situation , we must avoid our weaknesses while exploiting our strengths , give play to our advantages , and regain the initiative .
first , the environment for political life is good .
in a certain sense , the results of such scientific research are results of cooperation . this kind of advantage of cooperation can seldom be found among commercial research institutions .
advantages like this have actually provided a very good environment for capable personnel to display their intelligence and wisdom . therefore , in the process of introducing capable personnel , we must clearly tell them about this . besides , after introducing high - level capable personnel , we must provide all kinds of convenience for them .
in view of the special needs as described in policies for making use of personnel , the armed forces should explore flexible ways to make use of personnel while introducing high - level capable personnel . there are of course strict requirements for the armed forces to introduce high - level capable personnel .
however , if we do not have such capable personnel for the time being , we must also make sure " we have other personnel to use . " this means we have to be good at using substitutes . for example , we can appoint some people to form a scientific research group for tackling difficult problems .
in the process of making use of personnel , we must also properly handle the relationship between " reputation " and " ability . "

why is the united states spending this huge sum on secretly developing spy satellites ?
military scouts - - future war will bring victory to the discoverer the military theory believed by the united states is : " future war will being victory to the discoverer , " and whoever discovers , wins .
for the nro , the most secret us government organ , with an annual budget of $ 6 billion , to carry out this top secret program is for the purpose of exercising surveillance and control of terrestrial targets from space , so as to win by " being the first to discover . "
the main body of spy satellites consists of imaging satellites , also called photo - reconnaisance satellites ; these are mainly used for gathering strategic intelligence , identifying targets , and monitoring the observance of arms control treaties .
on 18 august 1960 the united states launched the world 's first military imaging satellite , publicly claiming that this was a scientific satellite called " discoverer-14, " whereas actually it was mission 9009 satellite of the corona program .
the united states has now developed the sixth generation of imaging reconnaisance satellites , with a ground resolution of 0.1 meter and a working life of eight years ; these satellites can take clear photographs of ground targets in poor light or even in complete darkness .
electronic reconnaisance satellites are mainly used for determining the nature , position , and operational state of military electronic systems , tests of new weapons , and the state of weapon development .
us electronic reconnaisance satellites have now developed to the sixth generation , and at present nine such satellites are in orbit , including reconnaisance survey , geostationary , wide elliptical orbit , and new extreme angle [ ji du ] types .
satellite warning satellites are like forward sentinels and are used for spotting missile launches and providing early warning information , .
at present there are two kinds of satellites deployed abroad ; one is a geostationary satellite , and the other is a wide elliptical orbit satellite .
both use on - board infrared monitoring devices and visible light tv cameras to receive infrared radiation from the missile 's flame emission to monitor and track it .
ocean surveillance satellites are like a backup ; these are used for monitoring and tracking ships and submarines .
through intercepting radio signals from ships ' radar , telecommunications , and other radio equipment , they can identify and determine the type , position , speed , and course of such ships .
ocean surveillance satellites have developed to the stage where they can detect submerged submarines and sense changes of 0.003 degree in sea water , because passing submarines warm the water .
hence these satellites can also monitor the launch of cruise missiles .
political trump cards - - whoever controls space can control the globe artificial earth satellites have brought epoch - making changes to the world .
their characteristics are as follows : first , speed .
satellites travel fast , at more than 7 km per second , and orbit the earth in 90 minutes .
second is breadth .
satellite surveillance and reconnaisance is broad in scope , and a satellite can look down on 42 percent of the earth 's surface , while one photograph can cover 34,000 square km .
in the early 1960 's , after eisenhower , us president kennedy , who was facing a great nationwide uproar after the soviet union launched the first satellite , loudly called : " whoever controls space can control the globe . "
spy satellites have thus played the part of trump cards ; they see the earth and think of power , and their true goal and essence is to " control the globe ! "
vanguard of science and technology - - alliance of space superiority and information superiority the " military model " that the united states upholds is " to build security on the greatest possible use of science and technology , " and the peak of modern science and technology is " the alliance of space superiority and information superiority . "
spy satellites thus demonstrate the image of vanguards of science and technology .
it should be pointed out that although satellites were very much in the limelight during the gulf war , in common with all hi - tech weapons , they were not boundlessly great , and they made an exhibition of themselves , leaving a sufficient shadow for comment by military experts .
throughout the war the satellites were unable to detect the mobile launchers of " scud " missiles and could hardly make out their camouflage , tunnel , and trench concealment , with the result that special forces had to be sent in .
india applied the method of making a feint in carrying out its recent nuclear test and concealed it from us reconnaisance satellites .
this similarly shows that satellites are by no means omnipotent .
sensors are held to be the " antennae " of high technology , and it is said that " conquering sensors means conquering high technology . "
visible light and infrared cameras and antimissile lasers represent the trend of development of sensors .
the new type of sensors will use a mega - image array [ zhao xiang su zhen lie , 0340 6272 4790 7109 0441 ] weighing a few kilograms and using a few watts of power , which can produce pictures with a resolution of one to 10 meters .
power consumption of the several score - kilogram laser device is increased to several hundred watts , and it can carry out space and instantaneous measuring of readable date on water evaporation and weather elements .
the technology for satellite clusters is closely linked to small satellite technology .
( william tong , ) a micro electrical and mechanical systems (mems) researcher at the us jet propulsion laboratory , imagines that " much smaller " satellites will be launched after another five to 10 years , and that clusters of satellites each weighing only 1 kg will be launched within 10 to 20 years .
a group at the nasa spaceflight center is currently working to develop a satellite cluster composed of satellites weighing 10 kg ; the group hopes to launch as many as 20 satellites all at once into a distant elliptical orbit in 2007 .
( jan brocker ) , executive in charge of research and development at the us matra marconi space corporation , says : " on - board processing will be the only major breakthrough in satellite technology in the next 10 to 15 years . "
it is not difficult to see that the united states is certainly not acting blindly in spending huge sums - - more than was spent on the manhattan project - - on secretly developing spy satellites ; it is a matter of hitting three or even more birds with one arrow .

[ editor 's note ] the dawning of the information era has brought about a profound reform in the field of military affairs in the world , which has provided us with both opportunities and challenges .
starting from this issue , the serial introduction on knowledge of information security will face up to the leading issue of information security along with the reading public .
the increasingly growing incidents related to network security has brought about an enormous threat to the security of the military information system and the work of keeping information confidential in various countries .
according to relevant information , 20,000 people in the world have the potential of launching an attack against networks . hackers have resorted to more than 1,000 kinds of software tools . one hacker - related incident takes place every 20 seconds on average in the world .
the experiments conducted by the us military showed that the success rate of attacks launched by hackers on its non - confidential computer system reached up to 88 percent , and only 5 percent of the attacks were detected .
according to reports , the network system of the us department of defense alone was invaded as many as 250,000 times in 1995 .
if the information system is damaged , and the military information is intercepted or altered , the whole military system will fall into chaos or even into the condition of a breakdown , and the army is likely to lose its combat power .
the fight for a favorable situation in modern warfare is manifested in the fight for " right of controlling information . " information security and keeping information confidential has therefore become the " commanding height " for winning a war .
in modern warfare , the " right of controlling information " is the synonym for having the favorable situation in war .
the essence of information security and keeping information confidential is to fight for the " right of controlling information . "
therefore , in future warfare , the fight for the " right of controlling information " will require a high investment , and will be all - sided and unusually fierce . information security and keeping information confidential will definitely become the " commanding height " which the two sides at war fight for with all their strength .
obtaining and counter - obtaining , interference and counter - interference , control and anti - control , and destroying and counter - destroying will become one of the important operational modes in future warfare .
the urgent task of preparations for military struggles in recent years , the building of informationalization of our army has seen rapid development , which has greatly enhanced the level of operational commanding , educational training , and scientific research .
however , our army 's dependence on computers and related facilities of the information system is growing stronger and stronger , and problems related to information security and keeping information confidential have become increasingly prominent .
therefore , vigorously strengthening the work of information security and keeping information confidential for our army has become one of the extremely urgent tasks in terms of strengthening preparations for military struggles and enhancing the capacity of the army to " win a victory . "
in addition , such aspects as the management system , cultivation of talents , and contingent building regarding the work of information security and keeping information confidential of our army do not match perfectly with the rapidly developing situation .
it is necessary to enhance understanding , and make a concerted effort .
in order to do a good job of the work of information security and keeping information confidential , it is necessary to first enhance our understanding in thinking : first , it is necessary to fully recognize the importance of the work of information security and keeping information confidential .
second , it is necessary to accurately understand relations between security and development .
however , we should not give up on our undertaking or slow down our steps in making progress for fear of the existing hidden dangers in the work of security and keeping information confidential . the biggest factor of insecurity is to stop making advancement .
the work of information security and keeping information confidential is system engineering , which has a strong tendency to synthesize and integrate , and involves a wide range of aspects . decentralization into many directions will easily result in the situation of shifting responsibility onto each other , functional repetitions , and low efficiency .
therefore , it is necessary to hold the concept of " the work of information security and keeping information confidential being an unshirkable responsibility of everybody . "
it is necessary to strengthen studies and explore countermeasures .
it is necessary to vigorously develop the core technology and key products that have independent intellectual property rights , establish a system of protection of technological security , and enhance in an all - round manner the comprehensive protection capability of the military information system and the army 's capability to deal with emergencies .

this system is mainly composed of three parts , ground - based radar , improved early - warning radar , and space - based infrared satellites ; combat management , command , control , and telecommunications systems ; and ground - based interceptor missiles for intercepting and destroying incoming weaponry .
nmd is mainly used for intercepting long - range and intercontinental ballistic missiles with a range of over 3,000 km that can hit the us homeland , and their purpose is to protect the us homeland from limited ballistic missile attack - - at present , ballistic missiles are the most menacing weapons in the world .
miss li ( journalist ) : can you give us an example to explain nmd 's operational procedure ?
when the incoming missiles have come within the surveillance range of ground - based early - warning radar , the radar computes information of their trajectory and orbit .
these missiles follow the highly distinct tracking data provided by the ground radar , approach very close to the incoming target missiles , intercept them at high speed , and destroy them .
yuan zhiming ( senior expert on military matters in the basic faculty of the national defense university ) : generally speaking , missile defense is a matter of " many to hit one , " that is , firing many missiles to hit one incoming missile .
whether they are launched all at once or in batches ( launch - - observe - - relaunch ) , by launching many interceptors at every incoming missile the interception success rate is greatly enhanced .
yuan zhiming : the us defense department successfully completed its first assessment of the progress of nmd in july 1996 , and the focus of the program started to shift from technological preparations to deployment preparations .
so far , the us military has carried out three test interceptions , and they will carry out a fourth such test in the first half of this year .
the first step will be to deploy 100 interceptor missiles and one x - waveband high - grade radar in alaska ; the fist batch of 20 missiles will form into initial combat capability by 2005 , and the entire deployment will be completed by 2007 .
after the completion of the second base deployment in north dakota , around 2011 , the entire program will be complete .
by that time the entire nmd system will include at least two launching sites , three command centers , five telecommunications relay stations , 15 radars , 29 artificial satellites , 225 underground missile bases [ as received ] , and 250 missiles .
corresponding bases will be built on the us homeland and in various parts of the world , including two radars in asia , possibly located in japan and the rok .
wang weixing : on the surface , the united states says that nmd deployment is aimed at protecting the united states from possible missile attack by a number of " rogue states " and accidental missile launches .
a well - known think - tank figure in the us government recently gave away the " secret " by saying that those " crazy " countries will " absolutely not be able " to launch a missile attack on the united states , because they will bring devastating retaliation on themselves .
nmd is precisely this kind of shield . it means that other countries in the world are unable to threaten the united states , but the united states can threaten any country at any time .
yuan zhiming : the full name of the abm treaty is the " treaty on limitation of abm systems , " which was signed by the former soviet union and the united states in 1972 .
the treaty lays down that neither country can build a missile defense system covering its entire territory for intercepting attacks by the opponent 's long - range nuclear weapons .
it is precisely this mechanism for mutually assured destruction that formed into subsequent strategic balance between the great powers and played a role in preventing the outbreak of nuclear war .
chair : in that case , overturning the " abm treaty " by means of nmd will certainly have a major impact on the world .
russian defense minister sergeyev has said : " if the united states unilaterally withdraws from the 1972 abm treaty , this will wreck the entire system of international treaties ensuring global strategic stability . "
this may trigger a new round of the large - scale arms race 10 years after the end of the cold war .
yuan zhiming : the arms race will also further expand into space .
this is actually the case in reality ; in the face of the grim situation in which the united states is going all - out to push nmd , russia is taking a hardline stance despite its lack of national strength .
strategic rocket forces commander yakovlev has stated that if russia has no alternative , it will resolve the multiple - warhead problem for its new " topol - m " icbm , draw up afresh plans for producing mrbms , and increase the number of nuclear warheads in its cruise missiles .
xiong mingfeng : spear and shield are for ever twins constraining each other .
in spending such huge sums on forging a missile defense system , and not shrinking from using the security of the whole of mankind as hostage , the united states is very likely to end up with just an illusion .

due to lobbying and pressure by military industry and arms dealers , the us government has to sell weapons to taiwan .
first , people have exaggerated the influence of military industries on us arms sales to foreign countries .
if arms dealers really could influence the government , taiwan could have purchased f-16 fighters as early as in the later part of 1970 s instead of 1992 . also , we should have gotten all weapons and equipment needed by taiwan and not have to provide a similar military procurement list year after year .
second , we have overlooked the level of importance american people attach to their appropriate roles .
many us government officials have worked for ordnance companies after leaving official posts to receive a relatively high income .
however , when they are assigned to official posts again , they know how to adjust their position and handle matters of arms sales in a strict and prudent manner .
such understanding in their change of position is due to prolonged influence of social consciousness and effective supervision system . individuals will not dare to violate basic ethics of a public official .
therefore , almost any arms sale must first go through a test , especially arms sales to sensitive regions .
fourth , they have overlooked the initiative of us government departments .
we should not depend on arms sales to seek a balance of military strength between the two sides of the strait .
many people are convinced that the purpose of us arms sales to taiwan is to promote a balance of military power between the two sides of the strait and enable taiwan 's military strength to be equivalent to that of communist china at all levels .
judging from us arms sales to taiwan during the past 50 years , the united states has never sought to achieve a military balance . if the us goal were to seek a military balance , the us government would have promised to sell all weapons and equipment we wanted to have long ago .
the basic concept of us arms sales to taiwan is to seek a deterrence balance . it is to enable taiwan to maintain superiority in some key areas so that communist china will have to pay a heavy price if it wants to invade taiwan by force and will thus refrain from taking hasty action .
in order to allocate resources for more appropriate uses , we should stop the arms race .
this concept is quite correct , but it has practical difficulty in putting the concept into practice . 1 .
progress of science and technology will lead to progress in armament and so science and technology will influence the development of weapons and equipment .
in other words , the development of science and technology will propel the existence of arms race .
there are factors of the attitude of mainland china and the structure of relations between the united states and china .
therefore , it wants to rapidly improve its armament , and its military modernization is not purely influenced by the cross - strait relations . facing the change of power structure of the united states and communist china , taiwan can hardly refrain from getting involved .
accordingly , we cannot single - handedly try to improve relations with communist china without considering the us factor .
moreover , communist china 's weapons to counter the united states can also be used to counter us . 3 .
there is a psychological factor .
the experience of the cold war between the united states and the soviet union told us that a stalemate between the two sides might turn out to be a condition for promoting arms control .
in a certain sense , this is also a necessity and an awkward predicament in formulating taiwan 's security policy .
moreover , he said that " beijing might make a strong reaction to give the bush government a lesson to let him know that it should take the concern of the republic of china seriously . "

over the last 20 - plus years , china has witnessed rapid economic growth at a speed of nine percent or more .
from historical and practical perspectives , one can see that the china threat theory is not tenable .
in the history of human civilization over the past 5,000 years , china has been far ahead most of the time .
if china intents to pose a threat to the world , it does not have to wait until today .
but there is not an inevitable link between the increase of strength and aggressive ambition .
it seemed more logical that the dynasty 's troops would sail across the sea to attack japan .
the ming dynasty controlled a state with highly centralized power . china was ruled by an extremely organized officialdom . the central government could command localities just like the way a man controls his arms .
meanwhile , our imperial country had in name a 2 million - strong standing army , the largest in the world at that time .
however , the unified ming dynasty that owned a 2 million - strong standing army did not have the slightest intention to invade japan . on the country , japan had a great intention to incorporate china even when it was not yet unified and troubled with frequent internal conflicts .
a sharp comparison can be found in another examples : zheng he 's [ 1371 - 1435 ; navigator and diplomat of the ming dynasty ] voyage to the western seas and columbus ' discovery of the new world .
influence by chinese culture , which treasures peace , chinese people are the most peaceful , gentle , and kind people in the world .
people will multiply endlessly and cultural tradition , with people as a carrier , will also stretch long and unbroken .
it is evident that china will never become hegemonic . it is absolutely not an empty slogan . it is a basic national policy that will be carried out persistently .
will such a peace - loving country pose a threat to the world ?
it is high time for those who advocate the china threat theory to stop .

zeng peiyan introduced the process and methods of drawing up the " outline . "
first of all , the high degree of importance attached by the central authorities was the key to successfully drawing up the 10 th fyp .
veteran comrades , economic experts , scientists , fellows of the two academies , and entrepreneurs who have long been engaged in economic work were invited to forums so as to listen to their views .
local meetings were held to listen to the views of local comrades , .
third , attention was paid to participation by society , and the process of drawing up the plan was turned into a process of coordinating the interests of the government and all sectors of society , unifying people 's thinking , and reaching consensus .
an advisory and deliberation body on the 10 th fyp was organized and set up ; we dealt seriously with the motions and suggestions of people 's congress deputies and chinese people 's political consultative conference members ; and a nationwide drive to contribute schemes and ideas was launched .
a planning setup was established , composed of three levels , namely the " outline , " specific key topic planning , and sector and regional planning .
china has entered the stage when economic development can only be promoted through restructuring .
in light of the problems of uncoordinated regional development and widening of regional disparities , the " outline " proposes restructuring regional economy , aiming at prosperity for all and taking the speeding up of western development as a fine opportunity .
the " outline " proposes actively and steadily pushing the urbanization strategy in order to improve the urban and rural structure and fundamentally resolve the " three rural " [ san nong ] problem .
highlight the " two innovations , " that is , system innovation and science and technology innovation .
the " outline " proposes actively exploring reforms in the system of transfer of land operating rights , deepening the reforms of gearing the grain circulation system to the market , and comprehensively promoting the rural tax - fee reform .
promoting science and technology innovation is the fundamental way to enhance our development reserve strength and international competitiveness , and is also the urgent requirement of china 's accession to the world trade organization .
it proposes the goals of science and technology innovation in striving to catch up and narrow the disparities with advanced world standards in major fields ; reaching advanced world standards in some fields in which we are relatively strong ; and achieving breakthroughs in some fields in which we can achieve leaps .
the " outline " proposes the organizational framework for science and technology innovation , sets out the focal points for innovation , and proposes the focal points for breakthrough in certain essential strategic fields and in hi - tech fields related to our national economic lifelines and security .
the weight given to this is greater than in any previous five - year plan .
the " outline " points out that we must continue to increase input in resource and ecological environment construction , intensify support for it , pay attention to resolving problems in strategic resources such as water and soil , and raise our implementation of the strategy of sustainable development to a new level .
the " outline " emphasizes that people are the core of development , and regards improving living standards as the fundamental point of departure in economic development , and thus fully expresses the demands of the party 's fundamental purpose and the nature of socialism .
over one - third of the indices in the " outline " are related to the people 's livelihood ; thus the masses feel tangible benefit , prospects , and confidence .
in this sense , the 10 th fyp is not only a plan for " making the country strong " but is also a plan for " making the people rich . "
the " outline " regards strengthening the exploitation of manpower resources , enhancing the quality of the laborers , and stepping up the building of a force of talented people as powerful motive forces for spurring economic development .
in implementing the " outline " it is necessary to persist in taking economic construction as the central task and regard development as the main topic .
we must implement the mass line , respect the masses ' pioneering spirit , and guide , bring into play , and protect well the initiative and creativity latent among the masses .
the government must create a good atmosphere and environment .

however , china not only attaches importance to citizens ' political rights , but also attaches importance to citizens ' economic , social , cultural , and development rights .
the human rights specified by the un " international covenant on economic , social and cultural rights " are a package of rights composed of three interrelated parts , namely , the economic , social , and cultural rights .
first , there is citizens ' social right , whose core point says that citizens should have the right to enjoy a fairly good living condition for themselves and their families in their daily activities , including sufficient food , clothing , housing , and the continuously improving survival right .
therefore , the state is obliged to adopt measures to improve food production , preservation , and distribution , and guarantee food supply and fair distribution according to people 's needs .
to enable citizens to develop their work capabilities and make comprehensive individual developments and improvements , they must be able enjoy cultural rights , such as the right to receive education .
the state should develop compulsory education , basic education , secondary education , vocational education , and higher education , and should adopt appropriate means to ensure that all people have equal chances to get access to such education .
the chinese experts pointed out : according to the international human rights covenant , the obligations for the state will mainly be fulfilled through legislative activities and administrative measures , thus guaranteeing the realization of various rights for the citizens .
the most stipulations of china 's current constitution , administrative laws , and social laws are in keeping with the stipulations of the international covenant , and the relevant law enforcement departments should be able to play a positive role in implementing the covenant stipulations .
therefore , the personnel in the state organs , especially in the administrative departments , should receive training about the international human rights covenant so that the phenomena of violating the covenant stipulations and infringing upon citizens ' basic human rights may be prevented .
china has pointed out that 47 out of the 127 countries and regions that have signed and ratified the international covenant on economic , social and cultural rights made reservations on part of the covenant contents - - on more than 150 articles in total .
therefore , china will make reservation in the implementation of the relevant covenant stipulation . china has made an explanation to the united nations about its domestic condition on the basis of the chinese laws .

theory and practice of constructing rural markets construction of modernized agriculture hinges on the issue of rural market construction .
the money required for agricultural and rural development can only come from the market . rural surplus labor can only be disposed of by relying on the market to carry out an orderly shift . and , agricultural products can only be sold through the market .
reform of our socialist economic system first began in rural areas .
the process of rural reforms since the third plenary session of the 11 th party central committee has been one of developing the socialist market economy in the rural areas .
according to statistics , there were over 238.1 million independently operated peasant households nationwide in 1999 , and individual private enterprises in the rural areas reached 19 million .
second , we have basically realized price transformation for agricultural products from planned fixed - prices to market - set price .
according to statistics , the proportion of state - set prices in the total purchase sales of farm produce and sideline products has declined from 94.4 percent in 1978 to below 20 percent in 1999 .
through overall price easing on agricultural products , a price system for agricultural products suitable to the market economy was gradually established , and this has played a significant role in promoting the formation of rural market mechanisms .
third , the rural market system has gone from being basically nothing to taking on a nice shape .
in the wake of increased improvements in income levels , national peasant spending levels have also increased , from an average cost of living of 116 yuan per person in 1978 to 1,577 yuan per person in 1999 , an average annual increase of 13.2 percent .
fifth , the rural market has started to move from a domestic - oriented economy to an export - oriented economy .
b. the contradiction involving the need to build a unified market and the long - standing significant split between agricultural product markets and agricultural key element markets .
at the same time , during the transformational period between the new and the old systems , some departments in certain areas have used their power to protect their regional interests , and as a result , market fragmentation has become increasingly severe .
under the planned economy system , the state mainly relied on agricultural accumulations to support development in industry and cities , while putting little effort into agriculture .
under the major trend of the market economy , agriculture possessing such inferior quality will naturally be in an inferior position while participating in market competition .
agriculture possessing an inferior position has become one of the important factors that restrict the advancement of rural markets .
d. the contradiction between the profit mechanisms of the market economy and each individual chain as well as different main bodies in production and marketing which distribute profits unreasonably .
although the rural economy has achieved significant development after liberalized reforms , it has not yet established a reasonable market mechanism in profit distribution . this results in extremely unreasonable profit distributions between production , processing , marketing and the different main bodies of the market , and this impacts the healthy development of the rural market economy .
entry will help in market expansion for our agricultural products . china is a major agricultural country and one of the most important producers of agricultural products in the world .
prior to our entry into wto , because our nation was not yet a member of the world trade organization , we could not enjoy equal treatment in the international free trade of agricultural products , and domestic markets remained as the main outlets for our agricultural products .
in 1998 , export of labor - intensive products accounted for 83.71 percent of our total exports of agricultural products .
if we are able to export huge quantities of labor - intensive agricultural products , this means that we indirectly export huge quantities of labor and we expand the markets for our rural labor forces . 2 .
after our entry into wto , when we reasonably import small amounts of grain , cotton , and lumber at lower prices on the international market , this will mean that we are importing a slice of land and forest resources . 3 .
in the wto agreement , there is a mechanism for settling disputes in a more fair and reasonable manner .
the average area of per capita farm land in our country is small , and most of the land is used to plant grain , cotton and oil crops which are needed for daily life .
it will probably have a negative impact on the improvement of international competitiveness for some of our agricultural products .
after our entry into wto , other member countries will certainly require that we relax the prices on our agricultural products and implement commercialized production and management of our agricultural products .
after our entry into wto , under the restrictions imposed by the pertinent regulations of the agreement on agriculture , the comparative advantage for some of our agricultural products will shrink . 3 .
tariff cuts and reductions in non - tariff trade barriers will have a negative impact on trade protection for our agricultural products .
countries of the world have long placed great emphasis on trade protection for their agricultural products . most of the countries , and in particular the western developed countries , have employed tariffs , as permitted by " the green box policy " in the wto agreement on agriculture , to protect their agriculture and agricultural product trade .
wto entry will probably magnify the difficulties that we may encounter in the course of constructing rural markets .
promote construction according to requirements of agreement on agriculture after our entry into wto , we will experience changes in the goals , tasks and emphases for construction of rural markets , and this will require that we promote the construction of rural markets along the same lines as world agricultural competition and development .
the main measures to do this are : 1 . enhance the ability of the main bodies of the agricultural market to participate in international market competition .
at the same time , we must vigorously cultivate various agricultural enterprises and other economic organizations with corporate qualifications .
the construction of rural markets not only involves market construction in rural areas , but also involves construction of large market systems including domestic city markets and foreign markets .
second , we must smooth out price relations .
we must completely liberalize pricing of agricultural products and let the market set prices , guiding peasants toward arranging , producing and managing on the basis of these prices which objectively reflect the relations between supply and demand in the market so as to adjust their agricultural production to the demands of market .
at the same time , we must , through talks and negotiations , form a distribution mechanism which is able to reasonably distribute profits between departments and regions , so as to ensure fair , just and open competition in the marketplace . 4 .
we must take full take advantage of " the green box policy " to provide protection measures for the main bodies of our rural markets participating in international competition .
after our entry into the wto , customs tariffs on import goods levied by each member country can only be reduced , not increased , according to the principle of " tariff cuts " and " tariffication on trade measures " in the wto agreement on agriculture .
this will require that we take full advantage of the " green box " policy found in the agreement on agriculture and strengthen trade protections for our agricultural products .
first , we must act in a timely manner to draft and revise such income support policies as agricultural product reserve stores and agricultural insurance and disaster subsidies to increase the support and protection force of domestic agricultural developmental policies .
second , we must readjust the investment direction of governmental agricultural capital .
we must concentrate agricultural infusions from finance departments at every level on the construction of agricultural production and the agricultural infrastructure .
third , we must ease agricultural taxes .
sixth , we must build a mechanism for risk prevention in agricultural trade to provide reliable protection for the large number of peasants , agricultural enterprises and other economic groups participating in international competition . 5 .

proceeding from their anticommunist aims , two reactionary forces collude in secret after the establishment of the prc in 1949 , the taiwan authorities headed by chiang kai - shek regarded the tibet separatist forces as one of the most important anticommunist forces that they could use on the mainland .
in 1950 the taiwan authorities colluded with the tibet separatist forces to block the people 's liberation army 's peaceful liberation of tibet .
in 1956 they dispatched special agents and provided money and arms in supporting an armed revolt against democratic reform in the tibetan part of sichuan .
in 1959 chiang kai - shek personally wrote to the 14 th dalai who had fled to india after being defeated in the revolt , telling him that he would give the tibetan people the right of " national self - determination " after completing the great undertaking of " opposing communism and recovering the country . "
these moves of the taiwan authorities were aimed at roping in the dalai clique for jointly opposing communism .
at that time , the dalai clique , which had just fled to india , had different ideas from the taiwan authorities on joining hands to oppose communism , and there was fierce controversy within the clique .
